L154: 【89†Anatomical terminology】
L155: The celiac (【90†/ˈsiːli.æk/】) artery (also spelled coeliac in 【91†British English】), also known as the celiac trunk, Haller's tripod or truncus coeliacus, is the first major branch of the 【77†abdominal aorta】. It is about 1.27 cm (half an inch) in length. Branching from the aorta at the level of the T12-L1 【92†intervertebral disc】 in typical anatomy, it is one of three anterior/midline branches of the abdominal aorta (the others are the 【93†superior】 and 【94†inferior mesenteric arteries】).
L156: ## Structure
L157: 
L158: [【95†edit】]
L159: 
L160: The celiac artery is the first major branch of the descending 【77†abdominal aorta】, branching at a 90° 【96†angle】.^{【97†[1]】}^{【98†[2]】} This occurs just below the 【99†crus of the diaphragm】.^{【98†[2]】} In typical anatomy, this is at the T12-L1 vertebral level.^{【100†[3]】}
L161: 
L162: There are three main divisions of the celiac artery, and each in turn has its own named branches:
L163: Artery  | Branches
L164: --- | ---
L165: 【78†left gastric artery】^{【98†[2]】}  | esophageal branch, stomach branch
L166: 【79†common hepatic artery】^{【98†[2]】}  | 【101†proper hepatic artery】, 【102†right gastric artery】, 【103†gastroduodenal artery】
L167: 【80†splenic artery】^{【98†[2]】}  | 【104†dorsal pancreatic artery】, 【105†short gastric arteries】, 【106†left gastro-omental artery】, 【107†greater pancreatic artery】
L168: 
L169: The celiac artery may also give rise to the 【108†inferior phrenic arteries】.
L170: ## Function
L171: 
L172: [【109†edit】]
L173: The celiac artery supplies oxygenated 【110†blood】 to the 【111†liver】, 【112†stomach】, abdominal 【113†esophagus】, 【114†spleen】, and the superior half of both the 【115†duodenum】 and the 【116†pancreas】.^{【98†[2]】} These structures correspond to the embryonic 【117†foregut】. (Similarly, the 【93†superior mesenteric artery】 and 【94†inferior mesenteric artery】 feed structures arising from the embryonic 【118†midgut】 and 【119†hindgut】 respectively.
L174: Note that these three anterior branches of the abdominal aorta are distinct and cannot substitute for one another, although there are limited connections between their terminal branches.)
L175: The celiac artery is an essential source of blood, since the interconnections with the other major arteries of the gut are not sufficient to sustain adequate 【120†perfusion】. Thus it cannot be safely ligated in a living person, and obstruction of the celiac artery will lead to 【121†necrosis】 of the structures it supplies.
L176: ### Drainage
L177: 
L178: [【122†edit】]
L179: 
L180: The celiac artery is the only major 【123†artery】 that nourishes the abdominal 【124†digestive organs】 that does not have a similarly named vein.
L181: 
L182: Most blood returning from the digestive organs (including from the area of distribution of the celiac artery) is diverted to the liver via the 【125†portal venous system】 for further processing and detoxification in the liver before returning to the 【126†systemic circulation】 via the 【127†hepatic veins】.
L183: In contrast to the drainage of midgut and hindgut structures by the 【128†superior mesenteric vein】 and 【129†inferior mesenteric vein】 respectively, venous return from the celiac artery is through either the 【130†splenic vein】 emptying into the 【131†hepatic portal vein】 or via smaller tributaries of the portal venous system.
L184: ## Clinical significance
L185: 
L186: [【132†edit】]
L187: 
L188: 【133†Aneurysms】 in the celiac artery account for around 4% of visceral artery aneurysms.^{【134†[4]】}^{【135†[5]】} This may cause 【136†abdominal pain】.^{【135†[5]】}
L189: The celiac artery is vulnerable to compression from the 【99†crus of the diaphragm】 during 【137†ventilation】 where it originates from the 【77†abdominal aorta】.^{【97†[1]】} This is known as 【138†median arcuate ligament syndrome】.^{【139†[6]】} This may present no 【140†symptoms】, but can cause 【141†pain】 due to restricted blood flow to the 【93†superior mesenteric artery】.^{【97†[1]】}

L173: 【108†Anatomical terminology】
L174: The portal vein or hepatic portal vein (HPV) is a 【109†blood vessel】 that carries 【110†blood】 from the 【94†gastrointestinal tract】, 【111†gallbladder】, 【96†pancreas】 and 【95†spleen】 to the 【112†liver】. This blood contains 【113†nutrients】 and 【114†toxins】 extracted from digested contents. Approximately 75% of total liver blood flow is through the portal vein, with the remainder coming from the 【115†hepatic artery proper】. The blood leaves the liver to the heart in the 【116†hepatic veins】.
L175: The portal vein is not a true 【117†vein】, because it conducts blood to 【118†capillary】 beds in the liver and not directly to the heart. It is a major component of the 【93†hepatic portal system】, one of two 【89†portal venous systems】 in the human body; the other is the 【119†hypophyseal portal system】. Some reptiles have an additional 【120†renal portal system】 not present in mammals.
L176: The portal vein is usually formed by the confluence of the 【90†superior mesenteric】, 【91†splenic veins】, 【97†inferior mesenteric】, 【121†left】, 【122†right gastric veins】 and the 【98†pancreatic vein】.
L177: Conditions involving the portal vein cause considerable illness and death. An important example of such a condition is elevated 【123†blood pressure】 in the portal vein. This condition, called 【124†portal hypertension】, is a major complication of 【125†cirrhosis】.
L178: In 【126†abdominal obesity】, fats, inflammatory 【127†cytokines】 and other toxic substances are transported by the portal vein from 【128†visceral】 fat into the liver, leading to 【112†hepatic】 【129†insulin resistance】 and 【130†metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease】.^{【131†[1]】}^{【132†[2]】}
L179: ## Structure
L180: 
L181: [【133†edit】]
L182: 
L183: Measuring approximately 8 cm (3 inches) long in adults,^{【134†[3]】} the portal vein is located in the 【135†right upper quadrant】 of the abdomen, originating behind the neck of the 【96†pancreas】.^{【136†[4]】}
L184: In most individuals, the portal vein is formed by the union of the 【90†superior mesenteric vein】 and the 【91†splenic vein】.^{【137†[5]】} For this reason, the portal vein is occasionally called the splenic-mesenteric confluence.^{【136†[4]】} Occasionally, the portal vein also directly communicates with the 【97†inferior mesenteric vein】, although this is highly variable.
L185: Other tributaries of the portal vein include the 【138†cystic】 and the 【121†left】 and 【122†right gastric veins】^{【139†[6]】}, as well as the 【140†paraumbilical】 and 【141†prepyloric veins】.
L186: Tributaries of the hepatic portal vein^{【139†[6]】}
L187: 
L188:   * 【91†Splenic vein】
L189:   * 【90†Superior mesenteric vein】
L190:   * 【97†Inferior mesenteric vein】
L191:   * 【121†Left】 and 【122†right gastric veins】
L192:   * 【138†Cystic vein】
L193: Immediately before reaching the liver, the portal vein divides into right and left. It ramifies further, forming smaller venous branches and ultimately portal venules. Each portal venule courses alongside a hepatic arteriole and the two vessels form the vascular components of the 【142†portal triad】. These vessels ultimately empty into the 【143†hepatic sinusoids】 to supply blood to the liver.^{【139†[6]】}
L194: ### Portacaval anastomoses
L195: 
L196: [【144†edit】]
L197: 
L198: The 【89†portal venous system】 has several 【145†anastomoses】 with the 【146†systemic venous system】. In cases of 【124†portal hypertension】 these anastomoses may become engorged, dilated, or varicosed and subsequently rupture.
L199: ### Accessory hepatic portal veins
L200: 
L201: [【147†edit】]
L202: 
L203: Accessory hepatic portal veins are those veins that drain directly into the liver without joining the hepatic portal vein. These include the 【148†paraumbilical veins】 as well as veins of the 【149†lesser omentum】, 【150†falciform ligament】, and those draining the 【111†gallbladder】 wall.^{【136†[4]】}
L204: ## Function
L205: 
L206: [【151†edit】]
L207: 
L208: The portal vein and 【152†hepatic arteries】 form the liver's dual blood supply, with 90% of hepatic blood flow and 70% of oxygen supplied by the portal vein, and the remainder by hepatic arteries. Due to its double blood supply, the liver is far less affected by vascular disease compared to other major internal organs.^{【153†[7]】}
L209: Unlike most veins, the portal vein does not drain into the 【154†heart】. Rather, it is part of a 【89†portal venous system】 that delivers venous blood into another 【155†capillary system】, the 【143†hepatic sinusoids】 of the liver.
L210: In carrying venous blood from the 【156†gastrointestinal】 tract to the liver, the portal vein accomplishes two tasks: it supplies the liver with metabolic substrates and it ensures that substances ingested are first processed by the liver before reaching the 【157†systemic circulation】. This accomplishes two things. First, possible toxins that may be ingested can be detoxified by the hepatocytes before they are released into the systemic circulation.
L211: Second, the liver is the first organ to absorb nutrients just taken in by the 【158†intestines】. After draining into the liver 【159†sinusoids】, blood from the liver is drained by the 【160†hepatic vein】.
L212: ## Clinical significance
L213: 
L214: [【161†edit】]
L215: ### Portal hypertension
L216: 
L217: [【162†edit】]
L218: 
L219: Main article: 【124†Portal hypertension】
L220: Increased 【123†blood pressure】 in the portal vein, called 【124†portal hypertension】, is a major complication of liver disease, most commonly 【125†cirrhosis】.^{【163†[8]】} A dilated portal vein (diameter of greater than 13 or 15 mm) is a sign of portal hypertension, with a 【164†sensitivity】 estimated at 12.5% or 40%.^{【165†[9]】} On 【166†Doppler ultrasonography】, the main portal vein (MPV) peak systolic velocity normally ranges between 20 cm/s and 40 cm/s.^{【167†[10]】} A slow velocity of <16 cm/s in addition to dilatation in the MPV are diagnostic of portal hypertension.^{【167†[10]】}
L221: Clinical 【168†signs】 of portal hypertension include those of chronic liver disease: 【169†ascites】, 【170†esophageal varices】, 【171†spider nevi】, 【172†caput medusae】, and 【173†palmar erythema】.^{【174†[11]】}

L141: 【71†Anatomical terminology】
L142: The common hepatic artery is a short 【72†blood vessel】 that supplies oxygenated 【73†blood】 to the 【74†liver】, 【75†pylorus of the stomach】, 【76†duodenum】, 【77†pancreas】, and 【78†gallbladder】.^{【79†[1]】}
L143: 
L144: It arises from the 【58†celiac artery】^{【79†[1]】} and has the following branches:^{【80†[2]】}
L145: Branch  | Details
L146: --- | ---
L147: 【61†hepatic artery proper】  | supplies the 【78†gallbladder】 via the 【81†cystic artery】 and the 【74†liver】 via the left and right hepatic arteries
L148: 【62†gastroduodenal artery】  | branches into the 【82†right gastroepiploic artery】 and 【83†superior pancreaticoduodenal artery】
L149: 【84†right gastric artery】  | branches to supply the lesser curvature of the stomach inferiorly

L154: This article is about the vein of the liver. For portal veins in general, see 【88†Portal venous system】.
L155: Portal vein
L156: ---
L157: The portal vein (in light blue) and its tributaries. It is formed by the 【89†superior mesenteric vein】, inferior mesenteric vein, and 【90†splenic vein】. Lienal vein is an old term for splenic vein.

L171: 【107†Anatomical terminology】
L172: The portal vein or hepatic portal vein (HPV) is a 【108†blood vessel】 that carries 【109†blood】 from the 【93†gastrointestinal tract】, 【110†gallbladder】, 【95†pancreas】 and 【94†spleen】 to the 【111†liver】. This blood contains 【112†nutrients】 and 【113†toxins】 extracted from digested contents. Approximately 75% of total liver blood flow is through the portal vein, with the remainder coming from the 【114†hepatic artery proper】. The blood leaves the liver to the heart in the 【115†hepatic veins】.
L173: The portal vein is not a true 【116†vein】, because it conducts blood to 【117†capillary】 beds in the liver and not directly to the heart. It is a major component of the 【92†hepatic portal system】, one of two 【88†portal venous systems】 in the human body; the other is the 【118†hypophyseal portal system】. Some reptiles have an additional 【119†renal portal system】 not present in mammals.
L174: The portal vein is usually formed by the confluence of the 【89†superior mesenteric】, 【90†splenic veins】, 【96†inferior mesenteric】, 【120†left】, 【121†right gastric veins】 and the 【97†pancreatic vein】.
L175: Conditions involving the portal vein cause considerable illness and death. An important example of such a condition is elevated 【122†blood pressure】 in the portal vein. This condition, called 【123†portal hypertension】, is a major complication of 【124†cirrhosis】.
L176: In 【125†abdominal obesity】, fats, inflammatory 【126†cytokines】 and other toxic substances are transported by the portal vein from 【127†visceral】 fat into the liver, leading to 【111†hepatic】 【128†insulin resistance】 and 【129†metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease】.^{【130†[1]】}^{【131†[2]】}
L177: ## Structure
L178: 
L179: [【132†edit】]
L180: 
L181: Measuring approximately 8 cm (3 inches) long in adults,^{【133†[3]】} the portal vein is located in the 【134†right upper quadrant】 of the abdomen, originating behind the neck of the 【95†pancreas】.^{【135†[4]】}
L182: In most individuals, the portal vein is formed by the union of the 【89†superior mesenteric vein】 and the 【90†splenic vein】.^{【136†[5]】} For this reason, the portal vein is occasionally called the splenic-mesenteric confluence.^{【135†[4]】} Occasionally, the portal vein also directly communicates with the 【96†inferior mesenteric vein】, although this is highly variable.
L183: Other tributaries of the portal vein include the 【137†cystic】 and the 【120†left】 and 【121†right gastric veins】^{【138†[6]】}, as well as the 【139†paraumbilical】 and 【140†prepyloric veins】.
L184: Tributaries of the hepatic portal vein^{【138†[6]】}
L185: 
L186:   * 【90†Splenic vein】
L187:   * 【89†Superior mesenteric vein】
L188:   * 【96†Inferior mesenteric vein】
L189:   * 【120†Left】 and 【121†right gastric veins】
L190:   * 【137†Cystic vein】
L191: Immediately before reaching the liver, the portal vein divides into right and left. It ramifies further, forming smaller venous branches and ultimately portal venules. Each portal venule courses alongside a hepatic arteriole and the two vessels form the vascular components of the 【141†portal triad】. These vessels ultimately empty into the 【142†hepatic sinusoids】 to supply blood to the liver.^{【138†[6]】}
L192: ### Portacaval anastomoses
L193: 
L194: [【143†edit】]
L195: 
L196: The 【88†portal venous system】 has several 【144†anastomoses】 with the 【145†systemic venous system】. In cases of 【123†portal hypertension】 these anastomoses may become engorged, dilated, or varicosed and subsequently rupture.
L197: ### Accessory hepatic portal veins
L198: 
L199: [【146†edit】]
L200: 
L201: Accessory hepatic portal veins are those veins that drain directly into the liver without joining the hepatic portal vein. These include the 【147†paraumbilical veins】 as well as veins of the 【148†lesser omentum】, 【149†falciform ligament】, and those draining the 【110†gallbladder】 wall.^{【135†[4]】}
L202: ## Function
L203: 
L204: [【150†edit】]
L205: 
L206: The portal vein and 【151†hepatic arteries】 form the liver's dual blood supply, with 90% of hepatic blood flow and 70% of oxygen supplied by the portal vein, and the remainder by hepatic arteries. Due to its double blood supply, the liver is far less affected by vascular disease compared to other major internal organs.^{【152†[7]】}
L207: Unlike most veins, the portal vein does not drain into the 【153†heart】. Rather, it is part of a 【88†portal venous system】 that delivers venous blood into another 【154†capillary system】, the 【142†hepatic sinusoids】 of the liver.
L208: In carrying venous blood from the 【155†gastrointestinal】 tract to the liver, the portal vein accomplishes two tasks: it supplies the liver with metabolic substrates and it ensures that substances ingested are first processed by the liver before reaching the 【156†systemic circulation】. This accomplishes two things. First, possible toxins that may be ingested can be detoxified by the hepatocytes before they are released into the systemic circulation.
L209: Second, the liver is the first organ to absorb nutrients just taken in by the 【157†intestines】. After draining into the liver 【158†sinusoids】, blood from the liver is drained by the 【159†hepatic vein】.
L210: ## Clinical significance
L211: 
L212: [【160†edit】]
L213: ### Portal hypertension
L214: 
L215: [【161†edit】]
L216: 
L217: Main article: 【123†Portal hypertension】
L218: Increased 【122†blood pressure】 in the portal vein, called 【123†portal hypertension】, is a major complication of liver disease, most commonly 【124†cirrhosis】.^{【162†[8]】} A dilated portal vein (diameter of greater than 13 or 15 mm) is a sign of portal hypertension, with a 【163†sensitivity】 estimated at 12.5% or 40%.^{【164†[9]】} On 【165†Doppler ultrasonography】, the main portal vein (MPV) peak systolic velocity normally ranges between 20 cm/s and 40 cm/s.^{【166†[10]】} A slow velocity of <16 cm/s in addition to dilatation in the MPV are diagnostic of portal hypertension.^{【166†[10]】}
L219: Clinical 【167†signs】 of portal hypertension include those of chronic liver disease: 【168†ascites】, 【169†esophageal varices】, 【170†spider nevi】, 【171†caput medusae】, and 【172†palmar erythema】.^{【173†[11]】}
L220: ### Pulsatility
L221: 
L222: [【174†edit】]
L223: 
L224: 【165†Doppler ultrasonography】 of the portal vein over 5 seconds, showing peaks of maximal velocity, as well as points of minimal velocity.
L225: Portal vein pulsatility can be measured by Doppler ultrasonography. An increased pulsatility may be caused by 【124†cirrhosis】, as well as increased right atrial pressure (which in turn may be caused by right 【175†heart failure】 or 【176†tricuspid regurgitation】).^{【166†[10]】} Portal vein pulsatility can be quantified by pulsatility indices (PI), where an index above a certain cutoff indicates pathology:
L226: Pulsatility indices (PI)
L227: Index  | Calculation  | Cutoff
L228: --- | --- | ---
L229: Average-based  | (Max - Min) / Average^{【166†[10]】}  | 0.5^{【166†[10]】}
L230: Max-based  | (Max - Min) / Max^{【177†[12]】}  | 0.5^{【177†[12]】}^{【178†[13]】} - 0.54^{【178†[13]】}
L231: ### Infection
L232: 
L233: [【179†edit】]
L234: 
L235: Main article: 【180†Pylephlebitis】
L236: 
L237: 【180†Pylephlebitis】 is infection of the portal vein, usually arising from an infectious intra-abdominal process such as 【181†diverticulitis】.^{【182†[14]】}^{【183†[15]】}
L238: 
L239: ### Portal venous gas
L240: 
L241: [【184†edit】]
L242: 
L243: Hepatic portal venous gas is a rare finding on radiological exams. Gas is shown to enter the portal venous system. It is most commonly caused by intestinal ischemia but has also been associated with 【185†colon cancer】.^{【186†[16]】}

L137: 【71†Anatomical terminology】
L138: The thoracic aorta is a part of the 【55†aorta】 located in the 【72†thorax】. It is a continuation of the 【73†aortic arch】. It is located within the 【74†posterior mediastinal】 cavity, but frequently bulges into the left 【75†pleural cavity】. The descending thoracic aorta begins at the lower border of the fourth 【76†thoracic vertebra】 and ends in front of the lower border of the twelfth thoracic vertebra, at the 【77†aortic hiatus】 in the 【78†diaphragm】 where it becomes the 【60†abdominal aorta】.
L139: At its commencement, it is situated on the left of the vertebral column; it approaches the median line as it descends; and, at its termination, lies directly in front of the column.
L140: 
L141: The thoracic aorta has a curved shape that faces forward, and has small branches. It has a radius of approximately 1.16 cm.^{【79†[1]】}
L142: ## Structure
L143: 
L144: [【80†edit】]
L145: 
L146: Main article: 【55†Aorta】
L147: The thoracic aorta is part of the 【56†descending aorta】, which has different parts named according to their structure or location. The thoracic aorta is a continuation of the descending aorta and becomes the 【60†abdominal aorta】 when it passes through the 【81†diaphragm】. The initial part of the 【55†aorta】, the 【82†ascending aorta】, rises out of the left ventricle, from which it is separated by the 【83†aortic valve】.
L148: The two 【84†coronary arteries】 of the heart arise from the aortic root, just above the cusps of the 【83†aortic valve】. The aorta then arches back over the right 【85†pulmonary artery】. Three vessels come out of the 【73†aortic arch】: the 【86†brachiocephalic artery】, the left 【87†common carotid artery】, and the left 【88†subclavian artery】. These vessels supply blood to the 【89†head】, 【90†neck】, 【72†thorax】 and 【91†upper limbs】.
L149: Behind the descending thoracic aorta is the 【92†vertebral column】 and the 【93†hemiazygos vein】. To the right is the 【94†azygos veins】 and 【95†thoracic duct】, and to the left is the left 【96†pleura】 and lung. In front of the thoracic aorta lies the root of the left 【97†lung】, the 【98†pericardium】, the 【99†esophagus】, and the diaphragm.
L150: The 【99†esophagus】, which is covered by a nerve 【100†plexus】 lies to the right of the descending thoracic aorta. Lower, the esophagus passes in front of the aorta, and ultimately is situated on the left.
L151: ## Function
L152: 
L153: [【101†edit】]
L154: 
L155: The 【55†aorta】 is an 【102†artery】 that conveys oxygenated 【103†blood】 from the 【104†heart】 to other parts of the body. It is one of the largest arteries in the body.^{【105†[2]】} The aorta gives off several paired branches as it descends. In descending order, these include the
L156: 
L157:   * 【57†Bronchial arteries】
L158:   * 【106†Mediastinal arteries】
L159:   * 【58†Esophageal arteries】
L160:   * Pericardial arteries
L161:   * 【107†Superior phrenic arteries】

L158: 【73†Anatomical terminology】
L159: In 【92†human anatomy】, the abdominal aorta is the largest 【93†artery】 in the 【94†abdominal cavity】. As part of the 【74†aorta】, it is a direct continuation of the 【95†descending aorta】 (of the 【96†thorax】).^{【97†[1]】}
L160: ## Structure
L161: 
L162: [【98†edit】]
L163: The abdominal aorta begins at the level of the 【99†diaphragm】, crossing it via the 【100†aortic hiatus】, technically behind the diaphragm, at the vertebral level of T12.^{【97†[1]】} It travels down the posterior wall of the abdomen, anterior to the vertebral column. It thus follows the curvature of the lumbar vertebrae, that is, convex anteriorly. The peak of this convexity is at the level of the third lumbar vertebra (L3).
L164: It runs parallel to the 【83†inferior vena cava】, which is located just to the right of the abdominal aorta, and becomes smaller in diameter as it gives off branches. This is thought to be due to the large size of its principal branches. At the 11th rib, the diameter is 122mm long and 55mm wide and this is because of the constant pressure.^{【101†[2]】} The abdominal aorta is clinically divided into two segments:
L165:   1. The suprarenal abdominal or paravisceral segment, 【102†inferior】 to the 【103†diaphragm】 but superior to the renal arteries.
L166:   2. The Infrarenal segment, 【102†inferior】 to the renal arteries and 【102†superior】 to the iliac bifurcation.
L167: ### Branches
L168: 
L169: [【104†edit】]
L170: 
L171: The abdominal aorta supplies blood to much of the abdominal cavity. It begins at T12 and ends at L4 with its bifurcation into the common iliac arteries^{【97†[1]】} and usually has the following branches:

L175: 【106†celiac】  | T12  | Visceral  | no  | ant.  | Large anterior branch

L137: 【67†Anatomical terminology】
L138: In 【68†human anatomy】, the bronchial arteries supply the 【69†lungs】 with 【70†oxygenated blood】, and nutrition. Although there is much variation, there are usually two bronchial 【71†arteries】 that run to the 【72†left lung】, and one to the 【73†right lung】, and are a vital part of the respiratory system.
L139: ## Structure
L140: 
L141: [【74†edit】]
L142: 
L143: There are typically two left and one right bronchial arteries.^{【75†[1]】}
L144: 
L145: The left bronchial arteries (superior and inferior) usually arise directly from the 【55†thoracic aorta】.^{【76†[2]】}
L146: 
L147: The single right bronchial artery may arise from one of the following:
L148:   * 1) in typical anatomy, the 【55†thoracic aorta】 at a common trunk with the right-sided first 【77†posterior intercostal artery】 (known as the intercostobronchial trunk).
L149:   * 2) the superior bronchial artery on the left side.
L150:   * 3) any number of the right 【78†intercostal arteries】 mostly the third right posterior.
L151: ## Function
L152: 
L153: [【79†edit】]
L154: 
L155: The bronchial arteries supply blood to the bronchi and connective tissue of the lungs. They travel with and branch with the 【80†bronchi】, ending about at the level of the respiratory 【81†bronchioles】. They 【82†anastomose】 with the branches of the 【83†pulmonary arteries】, and together, they supply the visceral 【84†pleura】 of the lung in the process.
L156: Note that much of the oxygenated blood supplied by the bronchial arteries is returned via the 【85†pulmonary veins】 rather than the 【57†bronchial veins】. As a consequence, blood returning to the left heart is slightly less oxygenated than blood found at the level of the pulmonary capillary beds.
L157: 
L158: Each bronchial artery also has a branch that supplies the esophagus.
L159: ### Comparison with pulmonary arteries
L160: 
L161: [【86†edit】]
L162: 
L163: It is easy to confuse the bronchial arteries with the pulmonary arteries, because they both supply the lungs with blood, but there are important differences:
L164: artery  | function  | circulation  | diameter
L165: 【83†pulmonary arteries】  | supplies deoxygenated blood pumped from the 【87†right ventricle】  | 【88†pulmonary circulation】  | relatively large
L166: 【89†bronchial arteries】  | supplies oxygenated blood pumped from the 【90†left ventricle】  | 【91†systemic circulation】  | relatively small
L167: ## Clinical significance
L168: 
L169: [【92†edit】]
L170: 
L171: Bronchial artery is considered dilated when its diameter is more than 2 mm. Several causes of bronchial artery dilatations are: congenital heart or lung diseases, obstructions of 【93†pulmonary artery】, and lung inflammation.^{【75†[1]】}
L172: 
L173: The bronchial arteries are typically enlarged and 【94†tortuous†en.wiktionary.org】 in 【95†chronic】 【96†pulmonary thromboembolic hypertension】.^{【97†[3]】}
L174: With modern surgical techniques, bronchial 【98†anastomoses】 heal well without bronchial artery reconnection. Largely for this reason, bronchial artery circulation is usually sacrificed during 【99†lung transplants】, instead relying on the persistence of a microcirculation (presumably arising from the deoxygenated pulmonary circulation) to provide perfusion to the airways.^{【100†[4]】}

L121: Esophageal (oesophageal in British English) arteries are a group of 【57†arteries】 from disparate sources supplying the 【52†esophagus】. The blood supply to the esophagus can roughly be divided into thirds, with anastamoses between each area of supply.

L123: More specifically, it can refer to:
L124:   * 【58†Esophageal branches of inferior thyroid artery】 (top third) a branch of the thyrocervical trunk of the subclavian artery.
L125:   * 【59†Esophageal branches of thoracic part of aorta】 (middle third) sends esophageal arteries towards the thoracic part.
L126:   * 【60†Esophageal branches of left gastric artery】 (bottom third) a branch of the celiac trunk and the left inferior phrenic artery.^{【61†[1]】}

L135: The intercostal arteries are a group of 【68†arteries】 passing within an 【55†intercostal space】 (the space between two adjacent ribs). There are 9 anterior and 11 posterior intercostal arteries on each side of the body. The anterior intercostal arteries are branches of the 【69†internal thoracic artery】 and its terminal branch – the 【70†musculophrenic artery】. The posterior intercostal arteries are branches of the supreme intercostal artery and 【71†thoracic aorta】.
L136: Each anterior intercostal artery 【72†anastomoses】 with the corresponding posterior intercostal artery arising from the thoracic aorta.
L137: ## Anterior intercostal arteries
L138: 
L139: [【73†edit】]
L140: 
L141: ### Origin
L142: 
L143: [【74†edit】]
L144: 
L145: The upper six anterior intercostal arteries are branches of the 【69†internal thoracic artery】 (anterior intercostal branches of internal thoracic artery). The internal thoracic artery then divides into its two terminal branches, one of which - the 【70†musculophrenic artery】 - proceeds to issue anterior intercostal arteries to the remaining 7th, 8th, and 9th intercostal spaces; these diminish in size as the spaces decrease in length.
L146: ### Course and relations
L147: 
L148: [【75†edit】]
L149: 
L150: They are at first situated between the 【76†pleurae】 and the 【77†intercostales interni】, and then between the mm. intercostales interni et intimi.
L151: 
L152: ### Distribution
L153: 
L154: [【78†edit】]
L155: 
L156: They supply the 【79†intercostal muscles】 and, by branches which perforate the 【80†intercostales externi】, the 【81†pectoral muscles】 and the 【82†mamma】.
L157: ## Posterior intercostal arteries
L158: 
L159: [【83†edit】]
L160: 
L161: There are eleven posterior intercostal arteries on each side. Each artery divides into an anterior and a posterior ramus.
L162: ### Origin
L163: 
L164: [【84†edit】]
L165:   * The 1st and 2nd posterior intercostal arteries arise from the supreme intercostal artery, a branch of the 【85†costocervical trunk】 of the 【86†subclavian artery】. The SICA descends vertically. It passes lateral to the 【87†cervicothoracic ganglion】. It passes in between the pleural cupula, and anterior border of the neck of rib I. It then passes anterior to the necks of ribs II-III.^{【88†[1]】}
L166:   * The remaining nine arteries arise from (the posterior aspect of) the 【71†thoracic aorta】.
L167: ### Course and relations
L168: 
L169: [【89†edit】]
L170: 
L171: Each posterior intercostal artery travels along the bottom of the rib alongside its corresponding 【90†posterior intercostal vein】 and 【91†intercostal nerve】; the vein is superior to the artery, and the nerve is inferior to it. The mnemonic "VAN" is commonly used to recall their order from superior to inferior.
L172: The right aortic intercostals are longer than the left because of the position of the aorta on the left side of the vertebral column; they pass across the bodies of the 【92†vertebrae】 behind the 【93†esophagus】, 【94†thoracic duct】, and 【95†azygos vein】, and are covered by the right 【96†lung】 and 【97†pleura】.
L173: The left aortic intercostals run backward on the sides of the vertebrae and are covered by the left 【96†lung】 and 【97†pleura】; the upper two vessels are crossed by the left 【98†superior intercostal vein】, the lower vessels by the 【99†hemiazygos vein】.
L174: 
L175: The 【100†sympathetic trunk】 (opposite the heads of the ribs) and 【101†splanchnic nerves】 pass anterior to the arteries.

L135: 【65†Anatomical terminology】
L136: In 【66†human anatomy】, the superior epigastric artery is a terminal^{【67†[1]】} branch of the 【55†internal thoracic artery】 that provides arterial supply to the 【68†abdominal wall】, and upper 【69†rectus abdominis muscle】. It enters the 【70†rectus sheath】 to descend upon the inner surface of the 【69†rectus abdominis muscle】. It ends by 【71†anastomosing】 with the 【56†inferior epigastric artery】.
L137: ## Structure
L138: 
L139: [【72†edit】]
L140: 
L141: ### Origin
L142: 
L143: [【73†edit】]
L144: 
L145: The superior epigastric artery arises from the 【55†internal thoracic artery】 (referred to as the 【74†internal mammary artery】 in the accompanying diagram).^{【75†[2]】}^{【76†[3]】}
L146: ### Course and relations
L147: 
L148: [【77†edit】]
L149: 
L150: The superior epigastric artery pierces the 【78†diaphragm】^{【67†[1]】} through the foramen of Morgagni so as to enter the 【70†rectus sheath】 and descend upon the deep surface of the 【69†rectus abdominis】.^{【79†[4]】}
L151: 
L152: Along its course, it is accompanied by a similarly named 【57†vein】, the 【58†superior epigastric vein】.
L153: ### Anastomoses
L154: 
L155: [【80†edit】]
L156: 
L157: It 【81†anastomoses】 with the 【56†inferior epigastric artery】^{【79†[4]】}^{【75†[2]】} within the rectus abdominis muscle^{【79†[4]】}^{【67†[1]】} at the 【82†umbilicus】.^{【75†[2]】}
L158: 
L159: ### Distribution
L160: 
L161: [【83†edit】]
L162: 
L163: Where it anastomoses, the superior epigastric artery supplies the anterior part of the abdominal wall,^{【84†[5]】}^{【85†[6]】} upper rectus abdominis muscle,^{【84†[5]】} and some of the 【86†diaphragm】.
L164: 
L165: ## Collateralization in disease
L166: 
L167: [【87†edit】]
L168: ### Vascular disease
L169: 
L170: [【88†edit】]
L171: The superior epigastric arteries, 【56†inferior epigastric arteries】, 【55†internal thoracic arteries】 and left 【89†subclavian artery】 and right subclavian artery / 【90†brachiocephalic】 are 【91†collateral vessels】 to the 【92†thoracic aorta】 and 【93†abdominal aorta】. If the abdominal aorta develops a significant 【94†stenosis】 and/or blockage (as may be caused by 【95†atherosclerosis】), this collateral pathway may develop sufficiently, over time, to supply blood to the 【96†lower limbs】.^{【97†[7]】}
L172: ### Coarctation of the aorta
L173: 
L174: [【98†edit】]
L175: 
L176: A congenitally narrowed aorta, due to 【99†coarctation】, is often associated with a significant enlargement of the internal thoracic and epigastric arteries.^{【100†[8]】}

L147: The internal thoracic artery (ITA), also known as the internal mammary artery, is an 【78†artery】 that supplies the anterior 【79†chest wall】 and the 【80†breasts】.^{【81†[1]】} It is a paired artery, with one running along each side of the 【82†sternum】, to continue after its bifurcation as the 【65†superior epigastric】 and 【83†musculophrenic arteries】.
L148: ## Structure
L149: 
L150: [【84†edit】]
L151: 
L152: The internal thoracic artery arises from the anterior surface of the 【61†subclavian artery】 near its origin.^{【85†[2]】}^{【86†[3]】} It has a width of between 1–2 mm.^{【87†[4]】}
L153: 
L154: It travels downward on the inside of the 【88†rib cage】, approximately 1 cm from the sides of the 【82†sternum】,^{【86†[3]】} and thus 【89†medial】 to the 【90†nipple】. It is accompanied by the 【68†internal thoracic vein】.
L155: It runs deep to the 【91†abdominal external oblique muscle】, but superficial to the 【92†vagus nerve】.
L156: 
L157: In adults, the internal thoracic artery lies closest to the 【82†sternum】 at the first 【93†intercostal space】. The gap between the artery and lateral border of the sternum increases when going downwards, up to 1.1 cm to 1.3 cm at the sixth intercostal space. In children, the gap ranges from 0.5 cm to 1.0 cm.^{【94†[5]】}
L158: ### Branches
L159: 
L160: [【95†edit】]
L161:   * 【96†Mediastinal】 branches
L162:   * 【97†Thymic】 branches
L163:   * 【98†Pericardiacophrenic artery】 – travels with the 【99†phrenic nerve】
L164:   * 【82†Sternal】 branches
L165:   * 【66†Perforating branches】
L166:   * Twelve 【63†anterior intercostal branches】, two to each of the top six 【93†intercostal spaces】. In a given space, the upper branch travels laterally along the bottom of the rib until it 【100†anastomoses】 with its corresponding posterior intercostal artery. The lower branch of the space anastomoses with a collateral branch of the posterior intercostal artery.
L167: After passing the sixth intercostal space, the internal thoracic artery splits into the following two terminal branches:
L168: 
L169:   * 【101†Musculophrenic artery】 – roughly follows the costal margin and it again gives branch for 7,8,9 ribs
L170:   * 【65†Superior epigastric artery】 – continues the course of the internal thoracic artery, travelling downward into the abdominal wall and to the content of rectus sheath
L171: ## Function
L172: 
L173: [【102†edit】]
L174: 
L175: The internal thoracic artery supplies the chest wall and the 【103†breasts】.^{【81†[1]】}
L176: 
L177: ## Clinical significance
L178: 
L179: [【104†edit】]
L180: ### Use in bypass grafts
L181: 
L182: [【105†edit】]
L183: The internal thoracic artery is the 【106†cardiac surgeon】's 【107†blood vessel】 of choice for 【108†coronary artery bypass grafting】. The left ITA has a superior long-term patency to 【109†saphenous vein】 grafts^{【110†[6]】}^{【111†[7]】} and other arterial grafts^{【112†[8]】} (e.g. 【113†radial artery】, 【114†gastroepiploic artery】) when grafted to the 【115†left anterior descending coronary artery】, generally the most important vessel, clinically, to revascularize.^{【81†[1]】}

L134: 【70†Anatomical terminology】
L135: In the 【71†human body】, the lateral thoracic artery (or external mammary artery) is a 【72†blood vessel】 that supplies oxygenated 【73†blood】 to approximately one-third of the lateral structures of the 【74†thorax】 and 【75†breast】.
L136: It originates from the 【60†axillary artery】 and follows the lower border of the 【76†pectoralis minor muscle】^{【77†[1]】} to the side of the chest to supply the 【63†serratus anterior muscle】,^{【78†[2]】} 【79†pectoralis major muscle】^{【80†[3]】} and 【81†pectoralis minor】 muscle,^{【82†[4]】} and sends branches across the 【83†axilla】 to the 【84†axillary lymph nodes】 and 【85†subscapularis muscle】.
L137: It anastomoses with the 【86†internal thoracic artery】, 【87†subscapular】, and 【88†intercostal arteries】, and with the pectoral branch of the 【89†thoracoacromial artery】.^{【90†[5]】}
L138: 
L139: In the 【91†female】 it supplies an external mammary branch which turns round the free edge of the pectoralis major and supplies the 【75†breasts】.^{【90†[5]】}
L140: ## Variations
L141: 
L142: [【92†edit】]
L143: 
L144: Variations in the Axillary Artery are quite common.
L145: 
L146: Differences in its origin, course, branching pattern, and 【93†size】 may cause variations in the number or arrangement of branches arising from the 【94†artery】. Additionally, anatomical variations such as accessory or duplicated lateral thoracic arteries have been reported in 【95†medical literature】. These variations can impact 【96†surgical procedures】 and 【97†diagnostic imaging】 interpretations.
L147: In case it is absent the lateral perforating branches of 【98†Intercostal arteries】 take its place.^{【90†[5]】}

L135: The intercostal arteries are a group of 【68†arteries】 passing within an 【55†intercostal space】 (the space between two adjacent ribs). There are 9 anterior and 11 posterior intercostal arteries on each side of the body. The anterior intercostal arteries are branches of the 【69†internal thoracic artery】 and its terminal branch – the 【70†musculophrenic artery】. The posterior intercostal arteries are branches of the supreme intercostal artery and 【71†thoracic aorta】.
L136: Each anterior intercostal artery 【72†anastomoses】 with the corresponding posterior intercostal artery arising from the thoracic aorta.
L137: ## Anterior intercostal arteries
L138: 
L139: [【73†edit】]
L140: 
L141: ### Origin
L142: 
L143: [【74†edit】]
L144: 
L145: The upper six anterior intercostal arteries are branches of the 【69†internal thoracic artery】 (anterior intercostal branches of internal thoracic artery). The internal thoracic artery then divides into its two terminal branches, one of which - the 【70†musculophrenic artery】 - proceeds to issue anterior intercostal arteries to the remaining 7th, 8th, and 9th intercostal spaces; these diminish in size as the spaces decrease in length.
L146: ### Course and relations
L147: 
L148: [【75†edit】]
L149: 
L150: They are at first situated between the 【76†pleurae】 and the 【77†intercostales interni】, and then between the mm. intercostales interni et intimi.
L151: 
L152: ### Distribution
L153: 
L154: [【78†edit】]
L155: 
L156: They supply the 【79†intercostal muscles】 and, by branches which perforate the 【80†intercostales externi】, the 【81†pectoral muscles】 and the 【82†mamma】.
L157: ## Posterior intercostal arteries
L158: 
L159: [【83†edit】]
L160: 
L161: There are eleven posterior intercostal arteries on each side. Each artery divides into an anterior and a posterior ramus.
L162: ### Origin
L163: 
L164: [【84†edit】]
L165:   * The 1st and 2nd posterior intercostal arteries arise from the supreme intercostal artery, a branch of the 【85†costocervical trunk】 of the 【86†subclavian artery】. The SICA descends vertically. It passes lateral to the 【87†cervicothoracic ganglion】. It passes in between the pleural cupula, and anterior border of the neck of rib I. It then passes anterior to the necks of ribs II-III.^{【88†[1]】}
L166:   * The remaining nine arteries arise from (the posterior aspect of) the 【71†thoracic aorta】.
L167: ### Course and relations
L168: 
L169: [【89†edit】]
L170: 
L171: Each posterior intercostal artery travels along the bottom of the rib alongside its corresponding 【90†posterior intercostal vein】 and 【91†intercostal nerve】; the vein is superior to the artery, and the nerve is inferior to it. The mnemonic "VAN" is commonly used to recall their order from superior to inferior.
L172: The right aortic intercostals are longer than the left because of the position of the aorta on the left side of the vertebral column; they pass across the bodies of the 【92†vertebrae】 behind the 【93†esophagus】, 【94†thoracic duct】, and 【95†azygos vein】, and are covered by the right 【96†lung】 and 【97†pleura】.
L173: The left aortic intercostals run backward on the sides of the vertebrae and are covered by the left 【96†lung】 and 【97†pleura】; the upper two vessels are crossed by the left 【98†superior intercostal vein】, the lower vessels by the 【99†hemiazygos vein】.
L174: 
L175: The 【100†sympathetic trunk】 (opposite the heads of the ribs) and 【101†splanchnic nerves】 pass anterior to the arteries.

L128: 【56†Anatomical terminology】
L129: The subcostal arteries, so named because they lie below the last 【57†ribs】, constitute the lowest pair of branches derived from the 【47†thoracic aorta】, and are in series with the 【58†intercostal arteries】.
L130: ## Anatomy
L131: 
L132: [【59†edit】]
L133: ### Course and relations
L134: 
L135: [【60†edit】]
L136: 
L137: Each intercostal artery is accompanied by the corresponding (i.e. ipsilateral) 【49†subcostal vein】 and 【61†nerve】.^{【62†[1]】}^{: 276 } Each passes along the lower border of the 12th rib.^{【63†[2]】}
L138: Before entering the 【64†anterior abdominal wall】, each runs laterally upon the anterior surface of the 【65†lumbar fascia】 (and thus also anterior to the underlying 【66†quadratus lumborum muscle】 which the lumbar fascia envelops) posterior to the ipsilateral kidney.^{【62†[1]】}^{: 276 } It then pierces the posterior aponeurosis of the 【67†transversus abdominis】, thus entering the anterior abdominal wall to course in between the 【68†abdominal internal oblique muscle】 and 【69†transverse abdominal muscle】 (the neurovascular plane of the anterior abdominal wall).^{【62†[1]】}^{: 276 }
L139: ### Branches
L140: 
L141: [【70†edit】]
L142: 
L143: Each subcostal artery gives off a posterior branch which has a similar distribution to the 【71†posterior ramus】 of an intercostal artery.^{【63†[2]】}
L144: 
L145: ### Anastomoses
L146: 
L147: [【72†edit】]
L148: 
L149: It 【73†anastomoses】 with the 【74†superior epigastric】, 【75†lower intercostal】, and 【76†lumbar arteries】.^{【63†[2]】}

L135: The intercostal arteries are a group of 【68†arteries】 passing within an 【55†intercostal space】 (the space between two adjacent ribs). There are 9 anterior and 11 posterior intercostal arteries on each side of the body. The anterior intercostal arteries are branches of the 【69†internal thoracic artery】 and its terminal branch – the 【70†musculophrenic artery】. The posterior intercostal arteries are branches of the supreme intercostal artery and 【71†thoracic aorta】.
L136: Each anterior intercostal artery 【72†anastomoses】 with the corresponding posterior intercostal artery arising from the thoracic aorta.
L137: ## Anterior intercostal arteries
L138: 
L139: [【73†edit】]
L140: 
L141: ### Origin
L142: 
L143: [【74†edit】]
L144: 
L145: The upper six anterior intercostal arteries are branches of the 【69†internal thoracic artery】 (anterior intercostal branches of internal thoracic artery). The internal thoracic artery then divides into its two terminal branches, one of which - the 【70†musculophrenic artery】 - proceeds to issue anterior intercostal arteries to the remaining 7th, 8th, and 9th intercostal spaces; these diminish in size as the spaces decrease in length.
L146: ### Course and relations
L147: 
L148: [【75†edit】]
L149: 
L150: They are at first situated between the 【76†pleurae】 and the 【77†intercostales interni】, and then between the mm. intercostales interni et intimi.
L151: 
L152: ### Distribution
L153: 
L154: [【78†edit】]
L155: 
L156: They supply the 【79†intercostal muscles】 and, by branches which perforate the 【80†intercostales externi】, the 【81†pectoral muscles】 and the 【82†mamma】.
L157: ## Posterior intercostal arteries
L158: 
L159: [【83†edit】]
L160: 
L161: There are eleven posterior intercostal arteries on each side. Each artery divides into an anterior and a posterior ramus.
L162: ### Origin
L163: 
L164: [【84†edit】]
L165:   * The 1st and 2nd posterior intercostal arteries arise from the supreme intercostal artery, a branch of the 【85†costocervical trunk】 of the 【86†subclavian artery】. The SICA descends vertically. It passes lateral to the 【87†cervicothoracic ganglion】. It passes in between the pleural cupula, and anterior border of the neck of rib I. It then passes anterior to the necks of ribs II-III.^{【88†[1]】}
L166:   * The remaining nine arteries arise from (the posterior aspect of) the 【71†thoracic aorta】.
L167: ### Course and relations
L168: 
L169: [【89†edit】]
L170: 
L171: Each posterior intercostal artery travels along the bottom of the rib alongside its corresponding 【90†posterior intercostal vein】 and 【91†intercostal nerve】; the vein is superior to the artery, and the nerve is inferior to it. The mnemonic "VAN" is commonly used to recall their order from superior to inferior.
L172: The right aortic intercostals are longer than the left because of the position of the aorta on the left side of the vertebral column; they pass across the bodies of the 【92†vertebrae】 behind the 【93†esophagus】, 【94†thoracic duct】, and 【95†azygos vein】, and are covered by the right 【96†lung】 and 【97†pleura】.

L127: 【57†Anatomical terminology】
L128: The accessory hemiazygos vein, also called the superior hemiazygous vein,^{【58†[1]】} is a vein on the left side of the 【59†vertebral column】 that generally drains the fourth through eighth 【60†intercostal spaces】 on the left side of the body.^{【61†[2]】}
L129: ## Structure
L130: 
L131: [【62†edit】]
L132: 
L133: The accessory hemiazygos vein varies inversely in size with the left 【63†superior intercostal vein】.
L134: 
L135: It usually receives the 【64†posterior intercostal veins】 from the 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, and 8th 【65†intercostal spaces】 between the left 【63†superior intercostal vein】 and highest tributary of the 【49†hemiazygos vein】;^{【66†[3]】} the left 【67†bronchial vein】 sometimes opens into it.
L136: The vein usually crosses the body of the eighth 【68†thoracic vertebra】 to join the 【50†azygos vein】. Alternatively, it ends in the hemiazygos vein.^{【66†[3]】}
L137: 
L138: When this vein is small, or altogether absent, the left 【63†superior intercostal vein】 may extend as low as the fifth or sixth intercostal space.

L125: 【51†Anatomical terminology】
L126: The superior intercostal veins are two 【52†veins】 that drain the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th 【53†intercostal spaces】, one vein for each side of the body.
L127: ## Right superior intercostal vein
L128: 
L129: [【54†edit】]
L130: 
L131: The right superior intercostal vein drains the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th 【45†posterior intercostal veins】 on the right side of the body. It flows into the 【46†azygos vein】.^{【55†[1]】}^{【56†[2]】}
L132: ## Left superior intercostal vein
L133: 
L134: [【57†edit】]
L135: 
L136: The left superior intercostal vein drains the 2nd and 3rd 【45†posterior intercostal veins】 on the left side of the body. It usually drains into the left 【47†brachiocephalic vein】.^{【55†[1]】}^{【56†[2]】} It may also communicate with the 【58†accessory hemiazygos vein】.^{【56†[2]】}
L137: 
L138: As it passes posteriorly above the 【59†aortic arch】, it crosses deep to the 【60†phrenic nerve】 and the 【61†pericardiacophrenic】 vessels and then superficial to the 【62†vagus nerve】.

L120: 【49†Anatomical terminology】
L121: The subcostal vein is a 【50†vein】 in the human body that runs along the bottom of the 【51†twelfth rib】. It has the same essential qualities as the 【52†posterior intercostal veins】, except that it cannot be considered intercostal because it is not between two ribs.
L122: 
L123: Each subcostal vein gives off a posterior (dorsal) branch which has a similar distribution to the posterior ramus of an intercostal artery.

L133: 【62†Anatomical terminology】
L134: In 【63†human anatomy】, the internal thoracic vein (previously known as the internal mammary vein) is the 【64†vein】 that drains the 【65†chest wall】 and 【66†breasts】.^{【67†[1]】}
L135: ## Structure
L136: 
L137: [【68†edit】]
L138: 
L139: Bilaterally, the internal thoracic vein arises from the 【53†superior epigastric vein】, and accompanies the 【55†internal thoracic artery】 along its course.^{【67†[1]】} It drains the 【69†intercostal veins】, although the posterior drainage is often handled by the 【70†azygous veins】.^{【67†[1]】} It terminates in the 【52†brachiocephalic vein】.^{【71†[2]】} It has a width of 2-3 【72†mm】.^{【73†[3]】}
L140: There is either one or two internal thoracic veins 【74†accompanying the corresponding artery】 (【55†internal thoracic artery】). If internal thoracic vein is single, it usually runs medial to the artery. If there are double thoracic veins, they run on either side of the internal thoracic artery.^{【75†[4]】}
L141: ### Variations
L142: 
L143: [【76†edit】]
L144: 
L145: Bifurcation of each internal thoracic vein is common. The left internal thoracic vein may bifurcate between ribs 3-4 or remain as a single vein.^{【77†[5]】} The right internal thoracic vein may bifurcate between ribs 2-4 or remain as a single vein.^{【77†[5]】}
L146: 
L147: ## Function
L148: 
L149: [【78†edit】]
L150: 
L151: The internal thoracic vein drains the 【79†chest wall】 and the 【80†breasts】.^{【67†[1]】}
L152: ## Clinical significance
L153: 
L154: [【81†edit】]
L155: 
L156: Knowledge on the course of internal thoracic vein and artery is important during interventional procedures through the anterior chest wall such as biopsy and 【82†empyema】 drainage. This is to avoid puncturing the vessels and cause massive bleeding.^{【83†[6]】}
L157: 
L158: Accidental placement of 【84†central venous catheter】 in the internal thoracic vein can cause pleural effusions, chest wall abscess, pulmonary edema, shortness of breath and chest pain.^{【83†[6]】}
L159: ## Other animals
L160: 
L161: [【85†edit】]
L162: 
L163: Internal thoracic vein runs just lateral to the 【86†sternum】.^{【87†[7]】}
L164: 
L165: The internal thoracic vein can act as a collateral circulation for blood from the 【88†inferior vena cava】 to the 【89†superior vena cava】.^{【87†[7]】} This can work in either direction.^{【87†[7]】} It may partially compensate for disturbances to blood flow.^{【87†[7]】}

L171: 【101†Anatomical terminology】
L172: The renal arteries are paired arteries that supply the 【92†kidneys】 with 【102†blood】. Each is directed across the 【103†crus of the diaphragm】, so as to form nearly a right angle.
L173: 
L174: The renal arteries carry a large portion of total blood flow to the kidneys. Up to a third of total 【104†cardiac output】 can pass through the renal arteries to be filtered by the kidneys.
L175: ## Structure
L176: 
L177: [【105†edit】]
L178: In typical anatomy, the renal arteries arise perpendicularly from the sides of the 【87†abdominal aorta】, just below the origin of the 【106†superior mesenteric artery】 at the L1-L2 vertebral level.^{【107†[1]】} They have a radius of approximately 0.25 【108†cm】,^{【109†[2]】} 0.26 cm at the root.^{【110†[3]】} The measured mean diameter can differ depending on the imaging method used.
L179: For example, the diameter was found to be 5.04 ± 0.74 mm using ultrasound but 5.68 ± 1.19 mm using angiography.^{【111†[4]】}^{【112†[5]】}
L180: Due to the anatomical position of the 【113†aorta】, the 【114†inferior vena cava】, and the kidneys, the right renal artery is normally longer than the left renal artery.^{【107†[1]】}^{【115†[6]】}
L181:   * The right passes behind the 【114†inferior vena cava】, the right 【73†renal vein】, the 【116†head of the pancreas】, and the descending part of the 【117†duodenum】. It’s somewhat lower than the left one.
L182:   * Left artery lies behind the left renal vein, the 【118†body of the pancreas】 and the 【119†splenic vein】, and is crossed by the 【120†inferior mesenteric vein】.
L183: ### Branches
L184: 
L185: [【121†edit】]
L186: 
L187: Before reaching the 【74†hilus of the kidney】, each artery divides into four or five branches. The anterior branches (the upper, middle, lower and apical segmental arteries) lie between the renal vein and 【76†ureter】, the vein being in front, the ureter behind. The posterior branches, which are fewer in number and include the posterior segmental artery, are usually situated behind the ureter.^{【122†[7]】}
L188: Each vessel gives off some small 【123†inferior suprarenal branches】 to the 【124†suprarenal gland】, the 【76†ureter】, and the surrounding cellular tissue and muscles.
L189: 
L190: One or two accessory renal arteries are frequently found, especially on the left side since they usually arise from the aorta, and may come off above (more common) or below the main artery. Instead of entering the kidney at the hilus, they usually pierce the upper or lower part of the organ.
L191: ### Variation
L192: 
L193: [【125†edit】]
L194: 
L195: The arterial supply of the kidneys is variable and there may be one or more renal arteries supplying each kidney.^{【107†[1]】} It is located above the renal vein. Supernumerary renal arteries (two or more arteries to a single kidney) are the most common renovascular anomaly, occurrence ranging from 25% to 40% of kidneys.^{【126†[8]】} Aberrant renal arteries may be present, and may complicate surgical procedures.^{【127†[9]】}
L196: 
L197: ## Clinical significance
L198: 
L199: [【128†edit】]
L200: ### Stenosis
L201: 
L202: [【129†edit】]
L203: 
L204: 【130†Renal artery stenosis】, or narrowing of one or both renal arteries will lead to hypertension as the affected kidneys release 【131†renin】 to increase blood pressure to preserve perfusion to the kidneys. RAS is typically diagnosed with duplex ultrasonography of the renal arteries. It is treated with the use of balloon angioplasty and stents, if necessary.
L205: ### Atherosclerosis
L206: 
L207: [【132†edit】]
L208: 
L209: 【133†Atherosclerosis】 can also affect the renal arteries and can lead to poor perfusion of the kidneys leading to reduced kidney function and, possibly, 【134†renal failure】
L210: 
L211: ### Renal artery aneurysm
L212: 
L213: [【135†edit】]
L214: 
L215: A dilated renal artery measuring twice its normal size indicates a renal artery aneurysm.^{【111†[4]】}
L216: 
L217: ### Trauma
L218: 
L219: [【136†edit】]
L220: 
L221: A renal artery is damaged in 4% of 【137†blunt traumas】 and 7% of 【138†penetrating traumas】 to the 【139†abdomen】.^{【140†[10]】}

L134: 【63†Anatomical terminology】
L135: In 【64†human anatomy】, the dorsalis pedis artery (dorsal artery of foot) is a 【65†blood vessel】 of the 【66†lower limb】. It arises from the 【52†anterior tibial artery】, and ends at the first intermetatarsal space (as the 【53†first dorsal metatarsal artery】 and the 【54†deep plantar artery】). It carries oxygenated blood to the 【55†dorsal】 side of the 【56†foot】. It is useful for taking a 【67†pulse】. It is also at risk during 【68†anaesthesia】 of the 【69†deep peroneal nerve】.
L136: ## Structure
L137: 
L138: [【70†edit】]
L139: 
L140: The dorsalis pedis artery is located 1/3 from 【71†medial malleolus】 of the 【72†ankle】. It arises at the anterior aspect of the ankle joint and is a continuation of the 【52†anterior tibial artery】.^{【73†[1]】}^{【74†[2]】} It ends at the proximal part of the first intermetatarsal space. Here, it divides into two branches:^{【74†[2]】}
L141: 
L142:   * The 【53†first dorsal metatarsal artery】
L143:   * The 【54†deep plantar artery】
L144: 
L145: It is covered by skin and fascia, but is fairly superficial.^{【74†[2]】}
L146: The dorsalis pedis communicates with the plantar blood supply of the foot through the deep plantar artery. Along its course, it is accompanied by a 【75†deep vein】, the 【76†dorsalis pedis vein】.
L147: ## Function
L148: 
L149: [【77†edit】]
L150: 
L151: The dorsalis pedis artery supplies oxygenated blood to the 【78†dorsal】 side of the 【56†foot】.^{【73†[1]】}
L152: 
L153: ## Clinical significance
L154: 
L155: [【79†edit】]
L156: ### Pulse
L157: 
L158: [【80†edit】]
L159: The dorsalis pedis artery 【67†pulse】 can be 【81†palpated】 readily lateral to the 【82†extensor hallucis longus】 【83†tendon】 (or medially to the 【84†extensor digitorum longus】 tendon) on the dorsal surface of the 【56†foot】, distal to the dorsal most prominence of the 【85†navicular bone】 which serves as a reliable landmark for palpation.^{【86†[3]】} It is often examined, by 【87†physicians】, when assessing whether a given patient has 【88†peripheral vascular disease】.
L160: It is absent, unilaterally or bilaterally, in 2–3% of young healthy individuals.^{【89†[4]】}
L161: ### Ultrasound
L162: 
L163: [【90†edit】]
L164: 
L165: The dorsalis pedis artery may be studied using 【91†ultrasound】.^{【74†[2]】} 【92†Doppler ultrasound】 can be used to investigate blood flow.^{【74†[2]】}
L166: 
L167: ### Local anaesthesia
L168: 
L169: [【93†edit】]
L170: 
L171: The dorsalis pedis artery is at risk when injecting 【94†anaesthetic】 into the 【69†deep peroneal nerve】.^{【95†[5]】} 【91†Ultrasound】 can be used to help to avoid the artery.^{【95†[5]】} The injection site is just lateral to the artery.^{【95†[5]】}

L172: 【58†Anatomical terminology】
L173: In human male 【62†anatomy】, the dorsal veins of the penis are 【63†blood vessels】 that drain the 【64†shaft】 (【65†corpora cavernosa】, 【66†corpus spongiosum】), the skin and the 【67†glans】 of the 【68†human penis】. They are typically located in the midline on the
L174: 
L175: 【69†File:Video of frot.webm】
L176: dorsal aspect of the penis and they comprise the superficial dorsal vein of the penis, that lies in the subcutaneous tissue of the shaft, and the deep dorsal vein of the penis, that lies beneath the 【70†deep fascia】.^{【71†[1]】}
L177: ## Superficial dorsal vein
L178: 
L179: [【72†edit】]
L180: The superficial dorsal vein of the penis belongs to the superficial drainage system. It is located within the superficial 【73†dartos fascia】, a continuation of the 【74†Colles' fascia】, on the dorsal surface of the penis and, in contrast to the deep dorsal vein, it lies outside the deeper 【70†Buck's fascia】.^{【75†[2]】} It is formed by smaller superficial veins that merge on the dorsolateral aspect of the penis.
L181: It drains the 【76†prepuce】 and the skin of the shaft, and, running backward in the 【77†subcutaneous tissue】, inclines to the right or left, and opens into the corresponding 【78†superficial external pudendal vein】, a tributary of the 【79†great saphenous vein】.^{【71†[1]】}^{【80†[3]】}
L182: ## Deep dorsal vein
L183: 
L184: [【81†edit】]
L185: The deep dorsal vein of the penis belongs to the intermediate drainage system of the penis, along with the circumflex veins and their emissary veins.^{【71†[1]】} It runs directly beneath the superficial dorsal vein, with a layer of connective tissue, the 【82†deep fascia of the penis】, separating the two vessels. It receives oxygen-depleted blood from the glans and corpora cavernosa and courses backward in the middle line accompanied by the 【61†dorsal arteries】 on each side.
L186: Near the 【83†root of the penis】, it passes between the two parts of the 【84†suspensory ligament】 and then through an aperture between the 【85†arcuate pubic ligament】 and the 【86†transverse ligament of the pelvis】, and divides into two branches, which enter the 【87†vesical】 and 【59†prostatic plexuses】.
L187: From the prostatic plexus, the deoxygenated blood travels through the venal system until it arrives at the center of the 【88†circulatory system】 for resupply with oxygen in the lungs and recirculation through the left side of the heart.
L188: The deep vein also communicates below the 【89†pubic symphysis】 with the 【90†internal pudendal vein】.
L189: ## Clinical significance
L190: 
L191: [【91†edit】]
L192: 
L193: It is possible but rare for the superficial dorsal vein to rupture during intercourse, which presents in a manner similar to 【92†penile fracture】.^{【93†[4]】}
L194: 
L195: The dorsal veins of the penis can be used for 【94†intravenous injections】 in 【95†rats】.^{【96†[5]】}

L123: Details
L124: ---
L125: Source  | 【51†Deep femoral artery】

L128: 【52†Latin】  | arteria circumflexa femoris lateralis
L129: 【53†TA98】  | 【54†A12.2.16.027†ifaa.unifr.ch】

L132: 【58†Anatomical terminology】
L133: The lateral circumflex femoral artery (also known as the lateral femoral circumflex artery or the external circumflex artery^{【59†[1]】}) is an 【60†artery】 in the upper thigh. It is usually a branch of the 【61†profunda femoris artery】, and produces three branches. It is mostly distributed to the muscles of the lateral thigh, supplying arterial blood to muscles of the knee extensor group.
L134: ## Structure
L135: 
L136: [【62†edit】]
L137: 
L138: ### Origin
L139: 
L140: [【63†edit】]
L141: 
L142: The lateral femoral circumflex artery usually arises from the lateral side of the 【61†profunda femoris artery】, but may occasionally arise directly from the 【64†femoral artery】.^{【65†[2]】} It is the largest branch of the profunda femoris artery.^{【65†[2]】}
L143: ### Course and relations
L144: 
L145: [【66†edit】]
L146: 
L147: The lateral circumflex femoral artery usually courses anterior to the 【67†femoral neck】. It passes horizontally between the divisions of the 【68†femoral nerve】. It passes posterior to the 【69†sartorius muscle】 and 【70†rectus femoris muscle】.^{【71†[3]】} It passes laterally across the hip joint capsule.^{【72†[4]】}
L148: 
L149: It divides into ascending, transverse, and 【73†descending】 branches.^{【65†[2]】}
L150: ### Branches
L151: 
L152: [【74†edit】]
L153: 
L154: The lateral circumflex femoral artery has three branches:
L155:   1. The ascending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery passes upward, beneath the 【75†tensor fasciae latae muscle】, to the lateral aspect of the 【76†hip】, and 【77†anastomoses】 with the terminal branches of the 【78†superior gluteal】 and 【79†deep circumflex iliac artery】.
L156:   2. The descending branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery runs downward, behind the 【70†rectus femoris】, upon the 【80†vastus lateralis】, to which it gives offsets; one long branch descends in the muscle as far as the knee, and anastomoses with the 【81†superior lateral genicular artery】. It is accompanied by the branch of the 【68†femoral nerve】 to the 【80†vastus lateralis】 muscle.
L157:   3. The transverse branch of lateral circumflex femoral artery is a small 【60†artery】 in the 【82†thigh】.
L158: It is the smallest branch of the lateral circumflex femoral artery and passes lateralward over the 【83†vastus intermedius】, pierces the 【80†vastus lateralis】, and winds around the 【84†femur】, just below the 【85†greater trochanter】, anastomosing on the back of the thigh with the 【86†medial femoral circumflex artery】, the 【87†inferior gluteal artery】, and the 【88†perforating arteries】 of the 【61†profunda femoris artery】.
L159: ### Distribution
L160: 
L161: [【89†edit】]
L162: The lateral circumflex femoral artery mainly supplies muscles of the lateral thigh,^{【72†[4]】} supplying the 【90†vastus lateralis】, 【91†vastus intermedius】, and 【92†rectus femoris】 muscles.^{【93†[5]】} Due to the fact that it passes across the thickest part of the hip joint capsule, it is in a less suitable position to supply the proximal femur so that most of the arterial supply to the 【94†head】 and 【95†neck of the femur】 is instead afforded by the 【96†medial circumflex femoral artery】.^{【72†[4]】}
L163: ### Variation
L164: 
L165: [【97†edit】]
L166: 
L167: Origin
L168: 
L169: The lateral femoral circumflex artery has a variable origin.^{【65†[2]】}^{【98†[6]】} In 67% of people, it arises 1.5 【99†cm】 inferior to the origin of the profunda femoris artery, and in others it arises at different distances from this origin.^{【65†[2]】} In up to 20% of people, it arises directly from the 【64†femoral artery】.
L170: 
L171: Course
L172: A rare variant, where the lateral circumflex femoral artery passes posterior to the 【68†femoral nerve】, has also been reported (this is important in 【100†orthopaedic surgery】).^{【101†[7]】}

L123: 【50†Anatomical terminology】
L124: The dorsal venous arch of the foot is a 【51†superficial】 vein that connects the 【52†small saphenous vein】 and the 【41†great saphenous vein】. Anatomically, it is defined by where the dorsal 【53†veins】 of the first and fifth 【54†digit】, respectively, meet the great saphenous vein and small saphenous vein.
L125: It is usually fairly easy to 【55†palpate】 and visualize (if the patient is barefoot). It lies superior to the 【56†metatarsal】 【57†bones】 approximately midway between the 【58†ankle joint】 and 【56†metatarsal phalangeal joints】.

L138: 【68†Anatomical terminology】
L139: The anterior tibial artery is an artery of the 【69†leg】. It carries blood to the 【61†anterior compartment of the leg】 and 【70†dorsal】 surface of the 【71†foot】, from the 【52†popliteal artery】.
L140: ## Structure
L141: 
L142: [【72†edit】]
L143: 
L144: Back of left lower extremity, showing origin of anterior tibial artery before it continues on the anterior side.
L145: ### Course
L146: 
L147: [【73†edit】]
L148: 
L149: The anterior tibial artery is a branch of the 【52†popliteal artery】.^{【74†[1]】} It originates at the distal end of the 【75†popliteus】 muscle posterior to the tibia. The artery typically passes anterior to the popliteus muscle prior to passing between the tibia and fibula through an oval opening at the superior aspect of the interosseus membrane. The artery then descends between the 【76†tibialis anterior】 and 【77†extensor digitorum longus】 muscles.
L150: It is accompanied by the 【60†anterior tibial vein】, and the 【78†deep peroneal nerve】, along its course.
L151: 
L152: It crosses the anterior aspect of the 【79†ankle joint】, at which point it becomes the 【58†dorsalis pedis artery】.
L153: ### Branches
L154: 
L155: [【80†edit】]
L156: 
L157: The branches of the anterior tibial artery are:
L158: 
L159:   * 【53†posterior tibial recurrent artery】
L160:   * 【54†anterior tibial recurrent artery】
L161:   * 【55†muscular branches】
L162:   * 【56†anterior medial malleolar artery】
L163:   * 【57†anterior lateral malleolar artery】
L164:   * 【58†dorsalis pedis artery】^{【74†[1]】}
L165: 
L166: ## Clinical significance
L167: 
L168: [【81†edit】]
L169: 
L170: As the artery passes medial to the 【82†fibular neck】, it becomes vulnerable to damage during a tibial 【83†osteotomy】.

L123: The anterior tibial recurrent artery is a small 【49†artery】 in the 【50†leg】. L128: 
L129: The descending geniculate artery immediately divides into two branches: a saphenous branch (which classically 【54†joins with】 the 【55†medial inferior genicular artery】), and muscular and articular branches.^{【56†[1]】}
L130: ## Structure
L131: 
L132: [【57†edit】]
L133: 
L134: ### Branches
L135: 
L136: [【58†edit】]
L137: 
L138: #### Saphenous branch
L139: 
L140: [【59†edit】]
L141: 
L142: The saphenous branch pierces the aponeurotic covering of the 【60†adductor canal】, and accompanies the 【61†saphenous nerve】 to the medial side of the knee. It passes between the 【62†sartorius muscle】 and the 【63†gracilis muscle】, and, piercing the 【64†fascia lata】, is distributed to the integument of the upper and medial part of the leg, anastomosing with the 【55†medial inferior genicular artery】.
L143: #### Articular branches
L144: 
L145: [【65†edit】]
L146: 
L147: The articular branches descend within the 【66†vastus medialis muscle】, and in front of the tendon of the 【67†adductor magnus muscle】, to the medial side of the knee, where they join with the 【68†medial superior genicular】 and 【69†anterior recurrent tibial artery】.
L148: A branch from this vessel crosses above the 【70†patellar surface】 of the 【71†femur】, forming an anastomotic arch with the 【72†lateral superior genicular artery】, and supplying branches to the 【73†knee-joint】.

L157: 【93†Anatomical terminology】
L158: The femoral artery is a large 【94†artery】 in the 【95†thigh】 and the main arterial supply to the thigh and leg. The femoral artery gives off the 【80†deep femoral artery】 and descends along the anteromedial part of the thigh in the 【96†femoral triangle】. It enters and passes through the 【97†adductor canal】, and becomes the 【81†popliteal artery】 as it passes through the 【98†adductor hiatus】 in the 【99†adductor magnus】 near the junction of the middle and distal thirds of the thigh.^{【100†[1]】}
L159: The femoral artery 【101†proximal】 to the origin of the deep femoral artery is referred to as the common femoral artery, whereas the femoral artery 【102†distal】 to this origin is referred to as the superficial femoral artery.^{【103†[2]】}
L160: ## Structure
L161: 
L162: [【104†edit】]
L163: 
L164: Femoral artery showing common and superficial arteries, in common usage but not listed in 【88†TA】
L165: The femoral artery represents the continuation of the 【75†external iliac artery】 beyond the 【105†inguinal ligament】 underneath which the vessel passes^{【103†[2]】} to enter the thigh.^{【106†[3]】} The vessel passes under the inguinal ligament just medial of the midpoint of this ligament,^{【103†[2]】} midway between the 【107†anterior superior iliac spine】 and the 【108†symphysis pubis】 (mid-inguinal point).
L166: In common usage, in clinical practice including 【109†angiology】 and 【110†vascular surgery】, the femoral artery includes the common femoral artery, and the superficial femoral artery however, the 【88†Terminologia Anatomica】 (TA) only lists the femoral artery. (The TA is the international standard for 【111†human anatomical】 terminology developed by the 【112†Federative International Programme on Anatomical Terminology】).^{【113†[4]】}
L167:   * The common femoral artery (CFA) is located between the inferior margin of the 【105†inguinal ligament】, and the branching point of the 【80†profunda femoris artery】. Its first three or four centimetres are enclosed, with the 【83†femoral vein】, in the 【114†femoral sheath】.
L168: In typical anatomy , the common femoral artery lies anterior to the femoral vein in the upper thigh.^{【115†[5]】} The CFA is, after the 【81†popliteal artery】, the most common peripheral site of general dilatation or aneurysmal formation, at a frequency of 1/10 of the aorta.^{【116†[6]】} Highly calcific arterial stenosis in the CFA is very difficult to treat by endovascular intervention.^{【117†[7]】} Stent positioning in CFA may be limited by compressive or torsional forces, leading to stent fracture and/or restenosis.^{【117†[7]】} On the other hand, lithoplasty balloon angioplasty may represent a safe tool to treat CFA stenosis.^{【117†[7]】}
L169:   * The superficial femoral artery^{【118†[8]】} is a designation for the segment between the branching point of the profunda femoris and the 【98†adductor hiatus】, passing through the 【119†subsartorial canal】.
L170: However, this term is not listed in 【88†Terminologia Anatomica】, and usage of the term superficial femoral is discouraged by many 【120†physicians】 because it leads to confusion among general medical practitioners, at least for the 【83†femoral vein】 that courses next to the femoral artery.^{【121†[9]】} In particular, the adjacent femoral vein is clinically a 【122†deep vein】, where 【123†deep vein thrombosis】 indicates 【124†anticoagulant】 or 【125†thrombolytic therapy】, but the adjective "superficial" leads many physicians to falsely believe it is a 【126†superficial vein】, which has resulted in patients with femoral thrombosis being denied proper treatment.^{【127†[10]】}^{【128†[11]】}^{【129†[12]】} Therefore, the segment is alternatively termed the subsartorial artery.^{【130†[13]】} The segment enters the 【98†adductor hiatus】 and becomes the 【81†popliteal artery】 which goes through the 【131†popliteal fossa】.^{【132†[14]】}
L171: ### Relations
L172: 
L173: [【133†edit】]
L174: 
L175: The relations of the femoral artery are as follows:
L176:   * Anteriorly: In the upper part of its course, it is superficial and is covered by skin and fascia. In the lower part of its course, it passes behind the 【134†sartorius muscle】.
L177:   * Posteriorly: The artery lies on the 【135†psoas】, which separates it from the 【136†hip joint】, the 【137†pectineus】, and the 【138†adductor longus】. The femoral vein intervenes between the artery and the adductor longus.
L178:   * Medially: It is related to the femoral vein in the upper part of its course.
L179:   * Laterally: The 【139†femoral nerve】 and its branches.
L180: ### Branches
L181: 
L182: [【140†edit】]
L183: 
L184: Schema of arteries of the thigh, including femoral artery and branches.
L185: 
L186: Common femoral artery
L187:   * The 【141†superficial circumflex iliac artery】^{【132†[14]】} is a small branch that runs up to the region of the 【107†anterior superior iliac spine】.
L188:   * The 【76†superficial epigastric artery】^{【132†[14]】} is a small branch that crosses the inguinal ligament and runs to the region of the 【142†umbilicus】.
L189:   * The 【78†superficial external pudendal artery】^{【132†[14]】} is a small branch that runs medially to supply the skin of the scrotum or labium majus as.
L190:   * The 【79†deep external pudendal artery】 runs medially and supplies the skin of the scrotum or labium majus.
L191:   * The 【80†deep femoral artery】 is a large and important branch that arises from the lateral side of the femoral artery about 1.5 in. (4 cm) below the inguinal ligament. It passes medially behind the femoral vessels and enters the 【143†medial fascial compartment of the thigh】. It ends by becoming the fourth 【144†perforating artery】. At its origin, it gives off the 【145†medial】 and 【146†lateral circumflex femoral】 arteries, and during its course it gives off three perforating arteries.^{【132†[14]】}
L192: Superficial femoral artery
L193: 
L194:   * The 【147†descending genicular artery】 is a small branch that arises from the femoral artery near its termination within the adductor canal. It assists in supplying the knee joint.

L126: ## Course
L127: 
L128: [【58†edit】]
L129: 
L130: It runs lateralward above the head of the fibula to the front of the knee-joint, passing in its course beneath the lateral head of the 【59†gastrocnemius】, the fibular collateral ligament, and the tendon of the 【60†biceps femoris】.
L131: 
L132: ## Branching
L133: 
L134: [【61†edit】]
L135: 
L136: It ends by dividing into branches, which anastomose with the 【62†Inferior medial genicular】 and 【63†superior lateral genicular】 arteries, and with the 【64†anterior recurrent tibial artery】.

L127: ## Course
L128: 
L129: [【60†edit】]
L130: 
L131: It first descends along the upper margin of the 【49†popliteus】, to which it gives branches; it then passes below the medial condyle of the 【50†tibia】, beneath the 【61†tibial collateral ligament】, at the anterior border of which it ascends to the front and medial side of the joint, to supply the upper end of the 【50†tibia】 and the 【51†knee-joint】, anastomosing with the 【62†lateral inferior】 and 【63†medial superior genicular arteries】.

L119: 【44†Latin】  | arteria plantaris lateralis
L120: 【45†TA98】  | 【46†A12.2.16.064†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L121: 【45†TA2】  | 【47†4737†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】

L123: 【50†Anatomical terminology】
L124: The lateral plantar artery (external plantar artery), much larger than the medial, passes obliquely lateralward and forward to the base of the fifth 【51†metatarsal】 bone.
L125: 
L126: It then turns medialward to the interval between the bases of the first and second metatarsal bones, where it unites with the deep plantar branch of the 【52†dorsalis pedis artery】, thus completing the 【53†plantar arch】.
L127: As this artery passes lateralward, it is first placed between the 【54†calcaneus】 and 【55†Abductor hallucis】, and then between the 【56†Flexor digitorum brevis】 and 【57†Quadratus plantæ】 as it runs forward to the base of the 【58†little toe】 it lies more superficially between the 【56†Flexor digitorum brevis】 and 【59†Abductor digiti quinti】, covered by the 【60†plantar aponeurosis】 and integument.
L128: The remaining portion of the vessel is deeply situated; it extends from the base of the fifth to the proximal part of the first interosseous space, and forms the plantar arch; it is convex forward, lies below the bases of the second, third, and fourth metatarsal bones and the corresponding 【61†Interossei】, and upon the oblique part of the 【62†Adductor hallucis】.

L127: ## Anatomy
L128: 
L129: [【58†edit】]
L130: 
L131: ### Course and relations
L132: 
L133: [【59†edit】]
L134: 
L135: It passes above the lateral condyle of the femur. It runs deep to the tendon of the 【60†biceps femoris】.^{【61†[1]】}
L136: ### Branches
L137: 
L138: [【62†edit】]
L139: 
L140: It divides into a superficial and a deep branch; the superficial branch supplies the 【63†vastus lateralis】, and anastomoses with the descending branch of the 【64†lateral femoral circumflex】 and the 【65†lateral inferior genicular】 arteries; the deep branch supplies the lower part of the femur and 【66†knee-joint】, and forms an anastomotic arch across the front of the bone with the 【67†highest genicular】 and the 【68†medial inferior genicular】 arteries.

L121: 【58†Anatomical terminology】
L122: The lateral tarsal artery (tarsal artery) arises from the 【59†dorsalis pedis】, as that vessel crosses the 【60†navicular bone】; it passes in an arched direction lateralward, lying upon the 【61†tarsal bones】, and covered by 【62†extensor hallucis brevis】 and 【63†extensor digitorum brevis】; it supplies these muscles and the articulations of the tarsus, and receives the 【64†arcuate】 over the base of the fifth metatarsal.
L123: It may receive contributions from branches of the 【65†anterior lateral malleolar】 and the perforating branch of the 【66†peroneal artery】 directed towards the joint capsule, and from the 【67†lateral plantar】 arteries through perforating arteries of the foot.

L125: 【51†Anatomical terminology】
L126: The medial plantar artery (internal plantar artery), much smaller than the 【52†lateral plantar artery】, passes forward along the medial side of the 【53†foot】.
L127: 
L128: It is at first situated above the 【54†abductor hallucis】, and then between it and the 【55†flexor digitorum brevis】, both of which it supplies.
L129: 
L130: At the base of the first 【56†metatarsal】 bone, where it is much diminished in size, it passes along the medial border of the first toe, anastomosing with the 【57†first dorsal metatarsal artery】.
L131: Small superficial digital branches accompany the digital branches of the 【58†medial plantar nerve】 and join the plantar metatarsal arteries of the first three spaces.
L132: ## Branches
L133: 
L134: [【59†edit】]
L135: 
L136: A superficial branch which supplies a plantar digital artery to the medial side of the 1st toe, and a deep branch which assists in supplying blood to the plantar metatarsal arteries.

L111: Details
L112: ---
L113: Branches  | Branch to 【40†vastus medialis】, branch to surface of the femur and the knee-joint
L114: Identifiers
L115: ---
L116: 【41†Latin】  | arteria superior medialis genus
L117: 【42†TA98】  | 【43†A12.2.16.035†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L118: 【42†TA2】  | 【44†4701†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】
