L120: 【47†Anatomical terminology】
L121: The medial superior genicular artery is a branch of the 【48†popliteal artery】.^{【49†[1]】} It runs deep to the 【50†semimembranosus】, 【51†semitendinosus】, and tendon of the 【52†adductor magnus】,^{【53†[2]】} and superior to the medial head of the 【54†gastrocnemius】.
L122: It divides into two branches, one of which supplies the 【40†vastus medialis】, anastomosing with the 【55†highest genicular】 and 【56†medial inferior genicular】 arteries; the other ramifies close to the surface of the femur, supplying it and the knee-joint, and anastomosing with the 【57†lateral superior genicular artery】.
L123: 
L124: The medial superior genicular artery is frequently of small size, a condition which is associated with an increase in the size of the highest genicular.

L122: 【52†Anatomical terminology】
L123: 
L124: The middle genicular artery (azygos articular artery) is a small branch of the 【53†popliteal artery】. It supplies parts of the 【54†knee】 joint.
L125: ## Structure
L126: 
L127: [【55†edit】]
L128: The middle genicular artery (MGA) arises from the anterolateral surface of the 【53†popliteal artery】.^{【56†[1]】}^{【57†[2]】} This point of origin is distal to the 【58†superior genicular arteries】, and between, equidistantly, the 【59†medial condyle of femur】 and the 【60†lateral condyle of femur】.^{【57†[2]】} As a normal variation, the MGA may emerge from the popliteal artery at a common point of origin shared with the 【61†superior lateral genicular artery】, or both vessels may arise at separate, distinct points.
L129: The angle at which the middle genicular artery leaves the popliteal artery varies with flexion and extension of the knee.^{【56†[1]】} It may form a near 90° angle when the knee is flexed, but an angle of only between 15° and 30° when the knee is extended.^{【56†[1]】}
L130: The 【62†diameter】 of the MGA is between 2 and 4 【63†millimetres】, and its length between 3 and 5 【64†centimetres】. It has two 【65†venae comitantes】 along its length. It pierces the 【66†oblique popliteal ligament】 and the joint capsule of the 【54†knee】.^{【56†[1]】}
L131: ## Function
L132: 
L133: [【67†edit】]
L134: 
L135: The middle genicular artery supplies the 【68†anterior cruciate ligament】 and the 【69†posterior cruciate ligament】.^{【57†[2]】} It also supplies the 【44†synovial membrane】 at the bottom of the 【54†knee】.^{【57†[2]】}
L136: ## Clinical significance
L137: 
L138: [【70†edit】]
L139: 
L140: The middle genicular artery may be damaged during 【71†knee arthroscopy】, particularly using a posterior approach through the 【72†popliteal fossa】.^{【56†[1]】} It may also be damaged in 【73†traumatic injuries】 to the knee, often caused by 【74†sports】.^{【57†[2]】}

L119: 【48†Anatomical terminology】
L120: 
L121: The plantar arch is a 【49†circulatory anastomosis】 formed from:
L122:   * 【38†deep plantar artery】, from the 【50†dorsalis pedis】 - a.k.a. dorsal artery of the foot
L123:   * 【37†lateral plantar artery】
L124: 
L125: The plantar arch supplies the underside, or sole, of the foot.
L126: 
L127: The plantar arch runs from the 5th 【51†metatarsal】 and extends medially to the 1st 【51†metatarsal】 (of the big toe).
L128: The arch is formed when the 【37†lateral plantar artery】 turns medially to the interval between the bases of the first and second 【51†metatarsal】 bones, where it unites with the deep plantar branch of the 【52†dorsalis pedis artery】, thus completing the plantar arch (or deep plantar arch).

L142: 【81†Anatomical terminology】
L143: The popliteal artery is a deeply placed continuation of the 【60†femoral artery】 opening in the distal portion of the 【82†adductor magnus muscle】. It courses through the 【83†popliteal fossa】 and ends at the lower border of the 【84†popliteus muscle】, where it branches into the 【61†anterior】 and 【62†posterior】 tibial arteries.
L144: The deepest (most anterior) structure in the fossa, the popliteal artery runs close to the joint capsule of the knee as it spans the 【85†intercondylar fossa】. Five genicular branches of the popliteal artery supply the capsule and ligaments of the knee joint. The genicular arteries are the superior lateral, superior medial, middle, inferior lateral, and inferior medial genicular arteries.
L145: They participate in the formation of the periarticular genicular anastomosis, a network of vessels surrounding the knee that provides collateral circulation capable of maintaining blood supply to the leg during full knee flexion, which may kink the popliteal artery.^{【86†[1]】}
L146: ## Structure
L147: 
L148: [【87†edit】]
L149: 
L150: Popliteal and other leg arteries
L151: 
L152: The popliteal artery is the continuation of the 【60†femoral artery】.^{【88†[2]】} It exits the 【83†popliteal fossa】 under the fibrous arch of the 【89†soleus muscle】.^{【88†[2]】}
L153: ### Relations
L154: 
L155: [【90†edit】]
L156:   * Anteriorly: The popliteal surface of the femur, the knee joint, and the popliteus muscle.
L157:   * Posteriorly: The 【72†popliteal vein】 and the 【91†tibial nerve】, fascia, and skin.
L158:   * Laterally: The 【92†biceps femoris】 and the lateral condyle of femur in upper part, and 【93†plantaris】, lateral gastrocnemius in lower part.
L159:   * Medially: The 【94†semimembranosus】 and the medial condyle of femur in upper part, and 【91†tibial nerve】, 【72†popliteal vein】, medial head of gastrocnemius in lower part.
L160: ### Branches
L161: 
L162: [【95†edit】]
L163: 
L164: The branches of the popliteal artery are:
L165: 
L166:   * 【61†anterior tibial artery】.^{【88†[2]】}
L167:   * 【62†posterior tibial artery】.^{【88†[2]】}
L168:   * 【96†sural artery】.^{【88†[2]】}
L169:   * 【97†medial superior genicular artery】.^{【88†[2]】}
L170:   * 【98†lateral superior genicular artery】.^{【88†[2]】}
L171:   * 【67†middle genicular artery】.^{【88†[2]】}
L172:   * 【99†lateral inferior genicular artery】.^{【88†[2]】}
L173:   * 【100†medial inferior genicular artery】.^{【88†[2]】}
L174: Muscular branches of the popliteal artery supply the 【101†hamstring】, 【102†gastrocnemius】, 【103†soleus】, and 【93†plantaris】 muscles. The superior muscular branches of the popliteal artery have clinically important anastomoses with the terminal part of the 【104†deep femoral】 and 【105†gluteal arteries】. The cutaneous branches arise either directly by the popliteal artery or indirectly by the muscular branches. Genicular branches are five in number, two superior, two inferior, and one middle.
L175: The middle genicular artery supplies the cruciate ligaments and the synovial membrane of knee joint.
L176: ### Tibial-fibular trunk
L177: 
L178: [【106†edit】]
L179: 
L180: Main article: 【107†Tibial-fibular trunk】
L181: 
L182: The 【108†fibular artery】 typically arises from the 【62†posterior tibial artery】.^{【109†[3]】} Therefore, the posterior tibial artery proximal to the fibular artery origin is sometimes called the 【110†tibial-peroneal trunk】 or tibial-fibular trunk and it could be said that the popliteal artery bifurcates into the tibial-fibular trunk and anterior tibial artery.
L183: ## Clinical significance
L184: 
L185: [【111†edit】]
L186: 
L187: Popliteal aneurysm, 1869.
L188:   * Popliteal pulse: Because the popliteal artery is deep, it may be difficult to feel the popliteal 【112†pulse】. 【113†Palpation】 (checking) of this pulse is commonly performed with the person in the 【114†prone position】 with the knee flexed to relax the popliteal fascia and hamstrings. The pulsations are best felt in the inferior part of the fossa where the popliteal artery is related to the 【115†tibia】. Weakening or loss of the popliteal pulse is a sign of a femoral artery obstruction.

L120: Posterior tibial artery
L121: ---
L122: Back of left lower extremity, showing surface markings for bones, vessels, and nerves (posterior tibial artery labeled at bottom right).
L123: Details
L124: ---
L125: Source  | 【53†Popliteal artery】
L126: Branches  | 【54†Fibular artery】, 【55†medial plantar artery】, 【56†lateral plantar artery】
L127: 【57†Vein】  | 【58†Posterior tibial vein】
L128: Identifiers
L129: ---
L130: 【59†Latin】  | arteria tibialis posterior
L131: 【60†TA98】  | 【61†A12.2.16.055†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L132: 【60†TA2】  | 【62†4721†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】
L133: 【63†FMA】  | 【64†43895†bioportal.bioontology.org】
L134: 【65†Anatomical terminology】
L135: The posterior tibial artery of the 【66†lower limb】 is an 【67†artery】 that carries 【68†blood】 to the 【69†posterior compartment of the leg】 and 【70†plantar】 surface of the 【71†foot】. It branches from the 【53†popliteal artery】 via the 【72†tibial-fibular trunk】.
L136: ## Structure
L137: 
L138: [【73†edit】]
L139: 
L140: The posterior tibial artery arises from the 【53†popliteal artery】 in the 【74†popliteal fossa】.^{【75†[1]】} It is accompanied by a 【76†deep vein】, the 【58†posterior tibial vein】, along its course. It passes just posterior to the 【77†medial malleolus】 of the 【78†tibia】, but anterior to the 【79†Achilles tendon】.^{【75†[1]】} It passes into the 【71†foot】 deep to the 【80†flexor retinaculum of the foot】.^{【75†[1]】} It runs through the 【81†tarsal tunnel】.^{【82†[2]】}
L141: ### Branches
L142: 
L143: [【83†edit】]
L144: 
L145: The posterior tibial artery gives rise to:
L146: 
L147:   * 【55†medial plantar artery】.
L148:   * 【56†lateral plantar artery】.
L149:   * 【54†fibular artery】,^{【75†[1]】} which is said to rise from the bifurcation of the 【72†tibial-fibular trunk】 and the posterior tibial artery.
L150:   * calcaneal branch to the medial aspect of the 【84†calcaneus】.
L151: ## Function
L152: 
L153: [【85†edit】]
L154: 
L155: The posterior tibial artery supplies oxygenated 【68†blood】 to the 【86†posterior compartment of the leg】 and the plantar surface of the foot.^{【75†[1]】}
L156: 
L157: ## Clinical significance
L158: 
L159: [【87†edit】]
L160: ### Palpation of the posterior tibial artery pulse
L161: 
L162: [【88†edit】]
L163: The posterior tibial artery 【89†pulse】 can be readily 【90†palpated】 halfway between the posterior border of the 【77†medial malleolus】 and the 【79†Achilles tendon】.^{【75†[1]】} It is often examined by 【91†clinicians】 when assessing a patient for 【92†peripheral vascular disease】. It is very rarely absent in young and healthy individuals.^{【93†[3]】} In a study of 547 healthy individuals, seven did not have a palpable posterior tibial artery.^{【93†[3]】} It is easily palpated over 【94†Pimenta's Point】.
L164: ### Nerve block
L165: 
L166: [【95†edit】]
L167: 
L168: The posterior tibial artery is used as a landmark for the 【96†tibial nerve】 as both structures enter the 【71†foot】.^{【97†[4]】} 【98†Local anaesthetic】 is injected either side of the artery distal to the 【80†flexor retinaculum of the foot】, close to the 【84†calcaneus】.^{【97†[4]】}

L111: Perforating arteries
L112: ---
L113: The arteries of the gluteal and posterior femoral regions.
L114: The deep femoral artery and its major perforating branches (labeled at right center), as seen on right thigh, anterior view.
L115: Details
L116: ---
L117: Source  | 【43†Deep femoral artery】
L118: Identifiers
L119: ---
L120: 【44†Latin】  | arteriae perforantes
L121: 【45†TA98】  | 【46†A12.2.16.031†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L122: 【45†TA2】  | 【47†4696†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】
L123: 【48†FMA】  | 【49†69460†bioportal.bioontology.org】
L124: 【50†Anatomical terminology】
L125: The perforating arteries are branches of the 【51†deep artery of the thigh】,^{【52†[1]】} usually three in number, so named because they perforate the tendon of the 【53†adductor magnus】 to reach the back of the 【54†thigh】. They pass backward near the 【55†linea aspera】 of the 【56†femur】 underneath the small tendinous arches of the adductor magnus muscle.
L126: The first perforating artery arises from the deep artery of the thigh above the 【57†adductor brevis】, the second in front of this muscle, and the third immediately below it.
L127: ## First
L128: 
L129: [【58†edit】]
L130: 
L131: The first perforating artery (a. perforans prima) passes posteriorly between the p【59†ectineus】 and adductor brevis (sometimes it perforates the latter); it then pierces the 【53†adductor magnus】 close to the linea aspera.
L132: 
L133: It gives branches to the adductores brevis and magnus, 【60†biceps femoris】, and 【61†gluteus maximus】, and anastomoses with the inferior gluteal, medial and lateral femoral circumflex and second perforating arteries.
L134: ## Second
L135: 
L136: [【62†edit】]
L137: 
L138: The second perforating artery (a. perforans secunda), larger than the first, pierces the tendons of the adductores brevis and magnus, and divides into ascending and descending branches, which supply the 【63†posterior femoral muscles】, anastomosing with the first and third perforating.
L139: 
L140: The second artery frequently arises in common with the first.
L141: The 【64†nutrient artery of the femur】 is usually given off from the second perforating artery; when two nutrient arteries exist, they usually spring from the first and third perforating vessels.
L142: ## Third/fourth
L143: 
L144: [【65†edit】]
L145: 
L146: The third perforating artery (a. perforans tertia) is given off below the Adductor brevis; it pierces the Adductor magnus, and divides into branches which supply the posterior femoral muscles; anastomosing above with the higher perforating arteries, and below with the terminal branches of the profunda and the muscular branches of the 【66†popliteal】.
L147: 
L148: The nutrient artery of the femur may arise from this branch.
L149: The termination of the profunda artery, already described, is sometimes termed the fourth perforating artery of Elliott after the anatomist who first dissected its course.

L123: 【50†Anatomical terminology】
L124: The plantar metatarsal arteries (digital branches) are four in number, arising from the convexity of the plantar arch. They run forward between the 【51†metatarsal】 bones and in contact with the 【52†Interossei】. They are located in the fourth layer of the foot.
L125: 
L126: Each divides into a pair of 【53†plantar digital arteries】 which supply the four webs and the adjacent sides of the toes.
L127: Near their points of division each sends upward an anterior perforating branch to join the corresponding 【54†dorsal metatarsal artery】.
L128: 
L129: The first plantar metatarsal artery (arteria princeps hallucis) springs from the junction between the lateral plantar and 【55†deep plantar arteries】 and sends a digital branch to the medial side of the 【56†first toe】.
L130: 
L131: The digital branch for the lateral side of the fifth toe arise from the 【57†lateral plantar artery】 near the base of the 【58†fifth metatarsal bone】.

L124: 【51†Anatomical terminology】
L125: The anterior tibial vein is a 【52†vein】 in the 【53†lower leg】.
L126: 
L127: In 【54†human anatomy】, there are two anterior tibial veins. They originate and receive blood from the 【55†dorsal venous arch】, on the back of the 【56†foot】 and empties into the 【42†popliteal vein】.
L128: 
L129: The anterior tibial veins drain the 【57†ankle joint】, 【58†knee joint】, 【59†tibiofibular joint】, and the 【60†anterior portion】 of the lower leg.^{【61†[1]】}
L130: The two anterior tibial veins ascend in the 【62†interosseous membrane】 between the 【63†tibia】 and 【64†fibula】 and unite with the 【65†posterior tibial veins】 to form the popliteal vein.
L131: 
L132: Like most 【66†deep veins】 in legs, anterior tibial veins are accompanied by the homonym 【43†artery】, the 【44†anterior tibial artery】, along its course.^{【61†[1]】}

L128: 【55†Anatomical terminology】
L129: The deep femoral vein, deep vein of the thigh or profunda femoris vein is a large 【56†deep vein】 in the 【57†thigh】. It collects blood from the inner thigh, passing superiorly and medially alongside the 【58†deep femoral artery】 before emptying into the 【46†femoral vein】.^{【59†[1]】}
L130: ## Anatomy
L131: 
L132: [【60†edit】]
L133: 
L134: ### Fate
L135: 
L136: [【61†edit】]
L137: 
L138: The deep femoral vein drains into the 【46†femoral vein】 at approximately the level of the inferior-most portion of the 【62†ischial tuberosity】.^{【59†[1]】}
L139: 
L140: ## Function
L141: 
L142: [【63†edit】]
L143: 
L144: The deep femoral vein drains the inner thigh.^{【64†[2]】} It contributes the largest volume of blood entering the femoral vein.^{【59†[1]】}
L145: ## Clinical significance
L146: 
L147: [【65†edit】]
L148: The deep femoral vein is commonly affected by 【66†phlebitis】 which can be a dangerous condition in the case of a 【67†thrombus】, or blood clot, forming, as the thrombus may dislodge and travel to the lungs, causing 【68†pulmonary embolism】. Risk factors for 【69†deep vein thrombosis】 include prolonged bed rest following surgery, immobility due to disability or fracture, an excessively 【70†sedentary lifestyle】 or hereditary dispositions such as the factor V Leiden mutation.^{【71†[3]】}

L142: 【75†Anatomical terminology】
L143: In the 【76†human body】, the femoral vein is the 【77†vein】 that accompanies the 【66†femoral artery】 in the 【78†femoral sheath】. It is a 【79†deep vein】 that begins at the 【80†adductor hiatus】 (an opening in the 【81†adductor magnus】 muscle) as the continuation of the 【61†popliteal vein】. The 【63†great saphenous vein】 (a 【82†superficial vein】), and the 【83†deep femoral vein】 drain into the femoral vein in the 【60†femoral triangle】 when it becomes known as the common femoral vein.
L144: It ends at the inferior margin of the 【84†inguinal ligament】 where it becomes the 【64†external iliac vein】.^{【85†[1]】} Its major tributaries are the deep femoral vein, and the great saphenous vein. The femoral vein contains 【86†valves】.
L145: ## Structure
L146: 
L147: [【87†edit】]
L148: 
L149: The femoral vein bears valves which are mostly bicuspid and whose number is variable between individuals and often between left and right leg.^{【85†[1]】}
L150: ### Course
L151: 
L152: [【88†edit】]
L153: 
L154: Veins of the leg. Common femoral vein shown, in common usage but not listed in 【70†TA】.
L155: The femoral vein continues into the 【89†thigh】 as the continuation from the 【61†popliteal vein】 at the back of the knee.
L156: It drains blood from the deep thigh muscles and 【90†thigh bone】.^{【91†[2]】} Proximal to the confluence with the deep femoral vein, and the joining of the 【63†great saphenous vein】, the femoral vein is widely known as the common femoral vein.^{【92†[3]】} As the common femoral vein leaves the inguinal ligament region it becomes the 【64†external iliac vein】.^{【93†[4]】} Other tributaries of the femoral vein are lateral and medial circumflex femoral veins.
L157: The common femoral vein is the segment of the femoral vein between the branching point of the 【83†deep femoral vein】 and the inferior margin of the 【84†inguinal ligament】.^{【94†[5]】}^{【95†[6]】} It is not listed in 【70†Terminologia Anatomica】, which is the international standard for 【96†human anatomical】 terminology developed by the 【97†Federative International Programme on Anatomical Terminology】.
L158: However, it was thought to be due for inclusion in the next edition following consensus documents presented in 2001 at the 14th World Congress of the International Union of Phlebology, and in 2004 at the 21st World Congress of the International Union of Angiology.^{【98†[7]】}^{【99†[8]】} These consensus documents were brought about by the need felt for more clarity and expansion of terms.^{【100†[9]】}^{【101†[10]】}
L159: #### Distal segment
L160: 
L161: [【102†edit】]
L162: 
L163: Segments of the femoral vein.^{【103†[11]】}
L164: In the past, the femoral vein was seen to follow the 【104†superficial femoral artery】 a name used to distinguish the 【66†femoral artery】 from the 【105†deep femoral artery】; as per the norm of naming veins to match their artery the femoral vein was called the superficial femoral vein.
L165: This was a potentially harmful misnomer since the femoral vein is a 【79†deep vein】 and not a 【82†superficial vein】, and thus a possible site for a 【106†deep vein thrombosis】, that may be overlooked as a superficial vein for 【107†anticoagulant therapy】.^{【108†[12]】}
L166: Because of the widespread misunderstanding, and possible harmful results from the use of superficial femoral vein, a consensus was arrived at in 2001 during the World Congress of the International Union of Phlebology to change the name from superficial femoral vein simply to femoral vein.^{【109†[13]】} This has been widely recognised and adopted though the use of superficial femoral vein still persists in some sources.
L167: Its use is actively discouraged.^{【110†[14]】}^{【111†[15]】}^{【112†[16]】} It has been suggested that another term be used – the subsartorial vein.^{【113†[17]】}^{【114†[18]】} A previous usage of subsartorial artery was published to avoid the name superficial femoral vein from being used.^{【115†[19]】} As per the consensus of 2002, the superficial femoral artery was unchanged.^{【116†[20]】}
L168: ### Tributaries
L169: 
L170: [【117†edit】]
L171: 
L172: The 【63†great saphenous vein】, and the 【83†deep femoral vein】 are two large tributaries that drain into the femoral vein which then becomes known as the common femoral vein. Other smaller vein tributaries are the lateral and medial circumflex femoral veins.^{【118†[21]】} These circumflex veins follow the 【119†lateral circumflex femoral artery】, and the 【120†medial circumflex femoral artery】.
L173: ## Clinical significance
L174: 
L175: [【121†edit】]
L176: 
L177: The femoral vein is a common site for a 【106†deep vein thrombosis】. This can be a 【122†proximal DVT】 in the femoral vein, or more proximal as an 【123†iliofemoral DVT】 usually associated with the common femoral vein. An iliofemoral DVT carries a greater risk of a 【124†pulmonary embolism】 developing.^{【125†[22]】}
L178: The femoral vein is often used to place a 【126†central venous catheter】, or line for 【127†venous access】. 【128†Ultrasound imaging】 for locating the vein and catheter placement is advocated over the use of 【129†anatomical landmarks】 due to the possible presence of 【130†anatomical variants】.^{【131†[23]】}^{【132†[24]】}^{【133†[25]】} This is associated with a significant risk of 【134†infection】.^{【133†[25]】}^{【135†[26]】}
L179: The practice of delivering 【136†recreational drugs】 【137†intravenously】 using the femoral vein in the groin is relatively common amongst 【138†injecting drug users】.^{【139†[27]】}

L141: 【81†Anatomical terminology】
L142: This article uses 【81†anatomical terminology】.
L143: 
L144: The great saphenous vein (GSV; 【82†/səˈfiːnəs/】) or long saphenous vein is a large, subcutaneous, 【83†superficial vein】 of the 【84†leg】. It is the longest vein in the body, running along the length of the lower limb, returning blood from the 【85†foot】, 【84†leg】, and 【86†thigh】 to the 【87†deep femoral vein】 at the 【88†femoral triangle】.
L145: ## Structure
L146: 
L147: [【89†edit】]
L148: The great saphenous vein originates from where the dorsal vein of the 【90†big toe】 (the hallux) merges with the 【74†dorsal venous arch of the foot】. After passing in front of the 【91†medial malleolus】 (where it often can be visualized and 【92†palpated】), it runs up the 【93†medial】 side of the leg.^{【94†[1]】} At the 【95†knee】, it runs over the posterior border of the 【96†medial epicondyle of the femur】 bone.
L149: In the proximal anterior thigh 3–4 centimetres (1.2–1.6 in) inferolateral to the 【97†pubic tubercle】, the great saphenous vein dives down deep through the 【98†cribriform fascia】 of the saphenous opening to join the femoral vein. It forms an arch, the saphenous arch, to join the 【99†common femoral vein】 in the region of the 【88†femoral triangle】 at the sapheno-femoral junction.^{【94†[1]】}
L150: ### Tributaries
L151: 
L152: [【100†edit】]
L153: 
L154: Superficial veins draining into the great saphenous and femoral vein.
L155: 
L156: Several veins join the great saphenous vein, but may not all present in every individual. Most of them join it near its junction with the common 【71†femoral vein】 (CFV), at various average distances from this junction:^{【101†[2]】}
L157: Vein^{【101†[2]】}  | Presence^{【101†[2]】}  | Joins from direction^{【101†[2]】}  | Joins at average distance from CFV junction^{【101†[2]】}
L158: --- | --- | --- | ---
L159: 【102†Superficial circumflex iliac vein】  | 83%  | Lateral  | 10.8 mm
L160: 【103†Superficial epigastric vein】  | 78%  | Proximal  | 11.9 mm
L161: 【104†Superficial external pudendal vein】  | 90%  | Medial  | 16.9 mm
L162: 【105†Anterior accessory saphenous vein】  | 51%  | Lateral  | 20.5 mm
L163: 【106†Posterior accessory saphenous vein】  |  |  | 73.9 mm
L164: At the ankle, the great saphenous vein receives branches from the sole of the foot through the 【107†medial marginal vein】; in the lower leg it anastomoses freely with the 【108†small saphenous vein】, communicates by 【109†perforator veins】 (Cockett perforators) with the 【110†anterior】 and 【111†posterior tibial】 veins and receives many cutaneous veins; near the knee it communicates with the popliteal vein by the Boyd perforator, in the thigh it communicates with the 【71†femoral vein】 by perforator veins (Dodd perforator) and receives numerous tributaries; those from the medial and posterior parts of the 【86†thigh】 frequently unite to form a large 【112†accessory saphenous vein】 which joins the main vein near the sapheno-femoral junction.^{【113†[3]】}
L165: Near the 【72†fossa ovalis】 it is joined by the 【103†superficial epigastric】, 【102†superficial circumflex iliac vein】, and 【114†superficial external pudendal】 veins.
L166: 
L167: The 【115†thoracoepigastric vein】 runs along the lateral aspect of the trunk between the 【103†superficial epigastric vein】 below and the 【116†lateral thoracic vein】 above and establishes an important communication between the 【71†femoral vein】 and the 【117†axillary vein】.
L168: ## Clinical significance
L169: 
L170: [【118†edit】]
L171: 
L172: 【119†Pathology】 of the great saphenous vein is relatively common, but in isolation typically not life-threatening.^{【120†[4]】}
L173:   * 【121†Varicose veins】: The great saphenous vein, like other 【83†superficial veins】, can become varicose; swollen, twisted and lengthened, and generally considered to be unsightly. Varicose veins are not life-threatening and various treatment options are available.
L174: However, when the diameter of the vein is too large for the valves within it to coapt completely, the resulting condition, chronic venous insufficiency, can result in skin color changes in the calf and ulcers that may persist for years if the vein is not ablated.
L175:   * 【122†Thrombophlebitis】: The GSV can 【123†thrombose】. This type of 【124†phlebitis】 of the GSV is usually not life-threatening in isolation; however, if the blood clot is located near the sapheno-femoral junction or near a perforator vein, a clot fragment can migrate to the deep venous system and to the pulmonary circulation. Also it can be associated with, or progress to a 【125†deep vein thrombosis】 which must be treated promptly.
L176: So a GSV thrombosis is investigated by 【126†ultrasonography】 to detect if these complications are present.^{【120†[4]】}
L177: ### Use in cardiovascular procedures
L178: 
L179: [【127†edit】]
L180: 
L181: The vein is often removed (【128†phlebectomy】) by 【129†cardiac surgeons】 and used for 【130†autotransplantation】 in 【131†coronary artery bypass operations】, when arterial grafts are not available or many grafts are required, such as in a 【132†triple bypass】 or 【133†quadruple bypass】.
L182: The great saphenous vein is the conduit of choice for 【134†vascular surgeons】,^{【135†[5]】} when available, for performing peripheral arterial 【136†bypass】 operations. The saphenous vein may undergo 【137†vein graft failure】 after engraftment, but still it has superior long-term patency compared to synthetic grafts (【138†PTFE】, 【139†PETE】 (Dacron)), 【140†human umbilical vein grafts】 or biosynthetic grafts [Omniflow].
L183: Often, it is used 【141†in situ】 (in place), after tying off smaller tributaries and destruction of the 【142†venous valves】 with a device called 【143†valvulotome】, e.g. 【144†LeMaitre's valvulotome】.
L184: Removal of the saphenous vein will not materially hinder normal circulation in the leg. The blood that previously flowed through the saphenous vein will change its course of travel. This is known as 【145†collateral circulation】.
L185: 
L186: The 【146†saphenous nerve】 that runs with the upper part of the great saphenous vein is a branch of the 【147†femoral nerve】. It can be damaged in surgery on the vein.
L187: ### Use in emergency medicine
L188: 
L189: [【148†edit】]
L190: 
L191: When emergency resuscitation with fluids is necessary, and standard 【149†intravenous】 access cannot be achieved due to venous collapse, 【150†saphenous vein cutdown】 may be utilized.
L192: 
L193: ## Etymology
L194: 
L195: [【151†edit】]
L196: 
L197: The terms "saphaina" (Greek, meaning "manifest", "to be clearly seen") as well as "safin" (Arabic, "صَافِن" meaning "deep/embedded")^{【152†[6]】} have been claimed as the origin for the word "saphenous".^{【152†[6]】}

L119: The four 【47†plantar metatarsal veins】 run backward in the 【48†metatarsal spaces】, communicate, by means of perforating veins, with the veins on the dorsum of the 【49†foot】, and unite to form the plantar venous arch (or deep plantar venous arch) which lies alongside the 【50†plantar arterial arch】.

L137: 【69†Anatomical terminology】
L138: The popliteal vein is a 【70†vein】 of the 【71†lower limb】. It is formed from the 【55†anterior tibial vein】 and the 【56†posterior tibial vein】. It travels medial to the 【60†popliteal artery】, and becomes the 【58†femoral vein】. It drains blood from the 【72†leg】. It can be assessed using 【73†medical ultrasound】. It can be affected by popliteal vein entrapment.
L139: ## Structure
L140: 
L141: [【74†edit】]
L142: The popliteal vein is formed by the junction of the 【75†venae comitantes】 of the 【55†anterior tibial vein】 and the 【56†posterior tibial vein】 at the lower border of the 【76†popliteus muscle】. It travels on the medial side of the 【60†popliteal artery】.^{【77†[1]】} It is superficial to the popliteal artery.^{【78†[2]】} As it ascends through the fossa, it crosses behind the popliteal artery so that it comes to lie on its lateral side.
L143: It passes through the 【79†adductor hiatus】 (the opening in the 【80†adductor magnus muscle】) to become the 【58†femoral vein】.^{【77†[1]】}^{【81†[3]】}
L144: ### Tributaries
L145: 
L146: [【82†edit】]
L147: 
L148: The tributaries of the popliteal vein include:
L149: 
L150:   * Veins that correspond to branches given off by the popliteal artery (see 【60†popliteal artery】).
L151:   * the 【57†small saphenous vein】, which perforates the deep fascia and passes between the two heads of the 【83†gastrocnemius muscle】 to end in the popliteal vein.^{【77†[1]】}^{【78†[2]】}
L152:   * the 【84†fibular veins】.
L153: 
L154: ### Variation
L155: 
L156: [【85†edit】]
L157: 
L158: The popliteal vein may be doubled in up to 35% of people.^{【78†[2]】}
L159: ## Function
L160: 
L161: [【86†edit】]
L162: 
L163: The popliteal vein drains blood from the 【72†leg】.^{【78†[2]】}
L164: 
L165: ## Clinical significance
L166: 
L167: [【87†edit】]
L168: 
L169: The popliteal vein is readily palpated in the 【88†popliteal fossa】 adjacent to the 【80†adductor magnus muscle】.^{【89†[4]】}
L170: 
L171: The popliteal vein can be visualised using 【73†medical ultrasound】, including 【90†Doppler ultrasonography】.^{【78†[2]】} It may be affected by a 【91†thrombus】.^{【78†[2]】}
L172: ### Popliteal vein entrapment
L173: 
L174: [【92†edit】]
L175: 
L176: The popliteal vein may become trapped.^{【93†[5]】} This reduces the flow of blood out of the leg, causing 【94†oedema】, 【95†pain】, and 【96†venous ulcers】.^{【93†[5]】} Entrapment is usually caused by 【83†gastrocnemius muscle】.^{【93†[5]】} 【97†Venography】 (using an 【98†x-ray】) or 【99†magnetic resonance imaging】 can investigate it.^{【93†[5]】} Surgery can be used to remove tissue creating pressure.^{【93†[5]】}

L126: The posterior tibial veins are 【54†veins】 of the 【55†leg】 in 【56†humans】. They drain the 【57†posterior compartment】 of the leg and the 【58†plantar】 surface of the 【59†foot】 to the 【44†popliteal vein】.
L127: ## Structure
L128: 
L129: [【60†edit】]
L130: 
L131: The posterior tibial veins receive blood from the medial and lateral plantar veins.^{【61†[1]】} They drain the 【57†posterior compartment】 of the leg and the 【58†plantar】 surface of the 【59†foot】 to the 【44†popliteal vein】, which it forms when it joins with the 【62†anterior tibial vein】.^{【61†[1]】}
L132: The posterior tibial vein is accompanied by an homonym 【45†artery】, the 【46†posterior tibial artery】, along its course.^{【63†[2]】} It lies posterior to the 【64†medial malleolus】 in the 【65†ankle】.^{【63†[2]】}
L133: 
L134: They receive the most important 【66†perforator veins】: the Cockett perforators, superior, medial and inferior.^{【67†[3]】}

L139: The small saphenous vein (also short saphenous vein or lesser saphenous vein) is a relatively large 【68†superficial vein】 of the posterior 【69†leg】.
L140: ## Structure
L141: 
L142: [【70†edit】]
L143: 
L144: The origin of the small saphenous vein (SSV) is where the dorsal vein from the 【71†fifth digit】 (smallest toe) merges with the 【59†dorsal venous arch of the foot】, which attaches to the 【72†great saphenous vein】 (GSV). It is a 【68†superficial vein】, being 【73†subcutaneous】 (just under the skin).
L145: From its origin, it courses around the lateral aspect of the foot (inferior and posterior to the 【74†lateral malleolus】) and runs along the posterior aspect of the leg (with the 【75†sural nerve】), where it passes between the heads of the 【76†gastrocnemius muscle】.^{【77†[1]】}^{【78†[2]】} This vein presents a number of different draining points.^{【77†[1]】} Usually, it drains into the 【60†popliteal vein】, at or above the level of the 【79†knee】 joint.^{【77†[1]】}
L146: ### Variation
L147: 
L148: [【80†edit】]
L149: 
L150: Sometimes, the SSV joins the common gastrocnemius vein before draining in the 【60†popliteal vein】.^{【78†[2]】}
L151: 
L152: Sometimes, it does not make contact with the popliteal vein, but goes up to drain in the GSV at a variable level.^{【77†[1]】}
L153: 
L154: Instead of draining in the popliteal vein, it can merge with the 【81†Giacomini vein】 and drain in the GSV at the superior 1/3 of the thigh.^{【77†[1]】}^{【82†[3]】}
L155: 
L156: ## Clinical significance
L157: 
L158: [【83†edit】]
L159: ### Varicose veins
L160: 
L161: [【84†edit】]
L162: 
L163: The small saphenous vein may become 【85†varicose】.^{【86†[4]】} In 20% of cases, this is associated with 【87†chronic venous insufficiency】.^{【88†[5]】} 【89†Vein stripping】 is an effective treatment.^{【86†[4]】}
L164: ### Vein harvesting
L165: 
L166: [【90†edit】]
L167: 
L168: The small saphenous vein may be 【91†harvested】 for transplant to elsewhere in the body, such as in 【92†coronary artery bypass surgery】.^{【93†[6]】} 【94†Endoscopic vein harvesting】 can be used to extract the vein from the leg 【95†minimally invasively】.^{【93†[6]】}

L129: In 【65†anatomy】, the fibular veins (also known as peroneal veins) are accompanying veins (【66†venae comitantes】) of the 【57†fibular artery】.^{【67†[1]】}
L130: ## Structure
L131: 
L132: [【68†edit】]
L133: 
L134: The fibular veins are 【69†deep veins】 that help carry blood from the 【70†lateral compartment of the leg】. They drain into the 【71†posterior tibial veins】, which in turn drain into the 【72†popliteal vein】. The fibular veins accompany the 【57†fibular artery】.

L172: 【58†Anatomical terminology】
L173: In human male 【62†anatomy】, the dorsal veins of the penis are 【63†blood vessels】 that drain the 【64†shaft】 (【65†corpora cavernosa】, 【66†corpus spongiosum】), the skin and the 【67†glans】 of the 【68†human penis】. They are typically located in the midline on the
L174: 
L175: 【69†File:Video of frot.webm】
L176: dorsal aspect of the penis and they comprise the superficial dorsal vein of the penis, that lies in the subcutaneous tissue of the shaft, and the deep dorsal vein of the penis, that lies beneath the 【70†deep fascia】.^{【71†[1]】}
L177: ## Superficial dorsal vein
L178: 
L179: [【72†edit】]
L180: The superficial dorsal vein of the penis belongs to the superficial drainage system. It is located within the superficial 【73†dartos fascia】, a continuation of the 【74†Colles' fascia】, on the dorsal surface of the penis and, in contrast to the deep dorsal vein, it lies outside the deeper 【70†Buck's fascia】.^{【75†[2]】} It is formed by smaller superficial veins that merge on the dorsolateral aspect of the penis.
L181: It drains the 【76†prepuce】 and the skin of the shaft, and, running backward in the 【77†subcutaneous tissue】, inclines to the right or left, and opens into the corresponding 【78†superficial external pudendal vein】, a tributary of the 【79†great saphenous vein】.^{【71†[1]】}^{【80†[3]】}
L182: ## Deep dorsal vein
L183: 
L184: [【81†edit】]
L185: The deep dorsal vein of the penis belongs to the intermediate drainage system of the penis, along with the circumflex veins and their emissary veins.^{【71†[1]】} It runs directly beneath the superficial dorsal vein, with a layer of connective tissue, the 【82†deep fascia of the penis】, separating the two vessels. It receives oxygen-depleted blood from the glans and corpora cavernosa and courses backward in the middle line accompanied by the 【61†dorsal arteries】 on each side.
L186: Near the 【83†root of the penis】, it passes between the two parts of the 【84†suspensory ligament】 and then through an aperture between the 【85†arcuate pubic ligament】 and the 【86†transverse ligament of the pelvis】, and divides into two branches, which enter the 【87†vesical】 and 【59†prostatic plexuses】.

L120: Inferior thyroid artery
L121: ---
L122: 【54†Thyrocervical trunk】 and its branches, including inferior thyroid artery. Superficial dissection of the right side of the neck.
L123: Human 【55†parathyroid glands】
L124: Details
L125: ---
L126: Source  | 【54†Thyrocervical trunk】
L127: 【56†Vein】  | 【57†Inferior thyroid veins】
L128: Supplies  | 【58†Thyroid gland】
L129: Identifiers
L130: ---
L131: 【59†Latin】  | arteria thyreoidea inferior
L132: 【60†TA98】  | 【61†A12.2.08.043†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L133: 【60†TA2】  | 【62†4591†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】
L134: 【63†FMA】  | 【64†10662†bioportal.bioontology.org】
L135: 【65†Anatomical terminology】
L136: The inferior thyroid artery is an 【66†artery】 in the 【67†neck】. It arises from the 【54†thyrocervical trunk】 and passes upward, in front of the 【68†vertebral artery】 and 【69†longus colli muscle】. It then turns medially behind the 【70†carotid sheath】 and its contents, and also behind the 【71†sympathetic trunk】, the middle 【72†cervical ganglion】 resting upon the vessel.
L137: Reaching the lower border of the 【73†thyroid gland】 it divides into two branches, which supply the postero-inferior parts of the gland, and 【74†anastomose】 with the 【75†superior thyroid artery】, and with the corresponding artery of the opposite side.
L138: ## Structure
L139: 
L140: [【76†edit】]
L141: 
L142: The branches of the inferior thyroid artery are the inferior laryngeal, the oesophageal, the tracheal, the ascending cervical and the pharyngeal arteries.
L143: ### Branches
L144: 
L145: [【77†edit】]
L146: 
L147: Inferior laryngeal artery
L148: 
L149: The inferior laryngeal artery - accompanied by the 【78†recurrent laryngeal nerve】 - passes superior-ward upon the 【79†trachea】^{【80†[1]】} deep to the 【81†inferior pharyngeal constrictor muscle】 to reach the posterior surface of the 【82†larynx】. At the inferior border of the 【81†inferior pharyngeal constrictor muscle】, the artery enters the 【82†larynx】.^{【80†[1]】}
L150: 
L151: The artery supplies the muscles and mucosa of the larynx.^{【80†[1]】}
L152: It forms 【83†anastomoses】 with its contralateral partner, and the 【84†superior laryngeal branch】 of the 【75†superior thyroid artery】.^{【80†[1]】}
L153: 
L154: Tracheal branches
L155: 
L156: The tracheal branches are distributed on the trachea, and anastomose inferiorly with the 【85†bronchial arteries】.^{【80†[1]】}
L157: 
L158: Esophageal branches
L159: 
L160: The esophageal branches supply the 【86†esophagus】, and anastomose with the 【87†esophageal branches of the thoracic aorta】.^{【80†[1]】}
L161: 
L162: Ascending cervical artery
L163: The ascending cervical artery is a small branch which arises from the inferior thyroid artery as it turns medial-ward posterior to the 【70†carotid sheath】.^{【80†[1]】}
L164: 
L165: The artery ascends upon the anterior tubercles of the transverse processes of the 【88†cervical vertebrae】 between the 【89†anterior scalene muscle】 and 【90†longus capitis muscle】.^{【80†[1]】}
L166: The ascending cervical artery gives twigs to the neck muscles and these anastomose with branches of the 【91†vertebral arteries】. One or two spinal branches are sent into the 【92†spinal canal】, through the 【93†intervertebral foramina】 to be distributed to the 【94†spinal cord】 and its membranes, and to the bodies of the vertebrae. It then anastomoses with the ascending 【95†pharyngeal】 and 【96†occipital arteries】.
L167: 
L168: Pharyngeal branches
L169: The pharyngeal branches are distributed to the inferior portion of the 【97†pharynx】.^{【80†[1]】}
L170: 
L171: Glandular branches
L172: 
L173: The glandular branches are supply the inferior and posterior portions of the 【73†thyroid gland】. They anastomose with the ipsilateral 【75†superior thyroid artery】, and the contralateral inferior thyroid artery. The ascending branch supplies the 【55†parathyroid gland】 as well.^{【80†[1]】}
L174: ## Clinical significance
L175: 
L176: [【98†edit】]
L177: The relationship between the 【78†recurrent laryngeal nerve】 and inferior thyroid artery is highly variable.^{【99†[2]】} The 【78†recurrent laryngeal nerve】 passes upward generally behind, but occasionally in front of, the inferior thyroid artery. This makes it vulnerable to injury during surgery that involves ligating the inferior thyroid artery, such as excision of the lower pole of the 【73†thyroid gland】.

L133: 【62†Anatomical terminology】
L134: The thoracoacromial artery (acromiothoracic artery; thoracic axis) is a short trunk that arises from the second part of the 【53†axillary artery】, its origin being generally overlapped by the upper edge of the 【63†pectoralis minor】.
L135: ## Structure
L136: 
L137: [【64†edit】]
L138: 
L139: Projecting forward to the upper border of the 【63†Pectoralis minor】, it pierces the 【65†coracoclavicular fascia】 and divides into four branches—pectoral, acromial, clavicular, and deltoid.^{【66†[1]】}
L140: Branch  | Description
L141: --- | ---
L142: 【67†Pectoral†en.wiktionary.org】 branch  | Descends between the two 【68†pectorales】, and is distributed to them and to the 【69†mamma】, 【70†anastomosing】 with the 【71†intercostal branches】 of the 【72†internal thoracic artery】 and with the 【73†lateral thoracic】.
L143: 【74†Acromial】 branch  | Runs laterally over the 【75†coracoid】 process and under the 【76†deltoideus】, to which it gives branches; it then pierces that muscle and ends on the 【77†acromion】 in an arterial network formed by branches from the 【78†transverse scapular】 (a.k.a. 【79†suprascapular】), 【80†thoracoacromial】, and 【81†posterior humeral circumflex】 arteries.
L144: 【82†Clavicular】 branch  | Runs upward and medialward to the 【83†sternoclavicular joint】, supplying this articulation, and the 【84†subclavius】.
L145: 【85†Deltoid】 (【86†humeral】) branch  | Often arising with the acromial, it crosses over the 【63†pectoralis minor】 and passes in the same groove as the 【87†cephalic vein】, between the 【88†pectoralis major】 and 【76†deltoideus】, and gives branches to both muscles.

L133: 【59†Anatomical terminology】
L134: The anterior humeral circumflex artery (anterior circumflex artery, anterior circumflex humeral artery) is an 【60†artery】 in the 【61†arm】. It is one of two circumflexing arteries that branch from the 【52†axillary artery】, the other being the 【62†posterior humeral circumflex artery】. The anterior humeral circumflex artery is considerably smaller than the posterior and arises nearly opposite to it, from the lateral side of the axillary artery.^{【63†[1]】}
L135: ## Anatomy
L136: 
L137: [【64†edit】]
L138: ### Course and relations
L139: 
L140: [【65†edit】]
L141: The anterior humeral circumflex artery passes horizontally posterior to the 【66†coracobrachialis muscle】 and short head of the 【67†biceps brachii muscle】, in and anterior to of the 【68†surgical neck of the humerus】. Upon reaching the 【69†intertubercular sulcus】, it gives off an ascending branch^{【63†[1]】} which ascends along the sulcus to supply the head of the humerus and the 【70†shoulder-joint】.
L142: It continues laterally, deep to the long head of the biceps brachii and the 【71†deltoideus muscle】, before 【72†anastomosing】 with the posterior humeral circumflex artery.^{【63†[1]】}

L119: ---

L124: Identifiers

L128: 【58†TA98】  | 【59†A12.2.09.048†ifaa.unifr.ch】

L131: 【63†Anatomical terminology】
L132: The anterior interosseous artery (volar interosseous artery) is an 【64†artery】 in the forearm.^{【65†[1]】} It is a branch of the 【49†common interosseous artery】.
L133: ## Course
L134: 
L135: [【66†edit】]
L136: 
L137: It passes down the 【53†forearm】 on the 【67†palmar】 surface of the 【68†interosseous membrane】.^{【69†[2]】}
L138: 
L139: It is accompanied by the 【70†palmar interosseous branch of the】 【71†median nerve】, and overlapped by the contiguous margins of the 【55†flexor digitorum profundus】 and 【54†flexor pollicis longus】 muscles, giving off in this situation muscular branches, and the 【72†nutrient arteries】 of the 【50†radius】 and 【51†ulna】.
L140: At the upper border of the 【73†pronator quadratus muscle】 it pierces the interosseous membrane and reaches the back of the forearm, where it anastomoses with the 【74†dorsal interosseous artery】.
L141: 
L142: It then descends, in company with the terminal portion of the 【75†dorsal interosseous nerve】, to the back of the wrist to join the 【76†dorsal carpal network】.
L143: The anterior interosseous artery may give off a slender branch, the 【77†median artery】, which accompanies the 【71†median nerve】, and gives offsets to its substance; this artery is sometimes much enlarged, and runs with the nerve into the palm of the hand.
L144: 
L145: Before it pierces the interosseous membrane the anterior interosseous sends a branch downward behind the 【73†pronator quadratus muscle】 to join the 【52†palmar carpal network】.
L146: ## Function
L147: 
L148: [【78†edit】]
L149: 
L150: The anterior interosseous artery supplies the deep layer of the 【79†anterior compartment of the forearm】, including the 【55†flexor digitorum profundus】, 【54†flexor pollicis longus】, and 【56†pronator quadratus】 muscles.

L128: 【59†Anatomical terminology】
L129: The inferior ulnar collateral artery (anastomotica magna artery) is an 【60†artery】 in the 【61†arm】. It arises about 5 cm. above the 【49†elbow】 from the 【52†brachial artery】.
L130: ## Course
L131: 
L132: [【62†edit】]
L133: 
L134: It passes medialward upon the 【63†brachialis】, and piercing the medial intermuscular septum, winds around the back of the 【64†humerus】 between the 【65†triceps brachii】 and the bone, forming, by its junction with the 【66†profunda brachii】, an arch above the 【67†olecranon fossa】.
L135: ## Branches and anastomoses
L136: 
L137: [【68†edit】]
L138: 
L139: As the vessel lies on the brachialis, it gives off branches which ascend to join the 【69†superior ulnar collateral】: others descend in front of the 【70†medial epicondyle】, to anastomose with the 【71†anterior ulnar recurrent】.
L140: 
L141: Behind the medial epicondyle a branch anastomoses with the superior ulnar collateral and 【72†posterior ulnar recurrent】 arteries.

L134: Axillary artery
L135: ---
L136: Axillary artery and its branches—anterior view of right upper limb and thorax. Upper and lower limits labeled.
L137: The 【68†pectoralis minor muscle】 is used as a landmark for dividing the axillary artery into three parts.

L157: 【88†Anatomical terminology】
L158: In 【89†human anatomy】, the axillary artery is a large 【90†blood vessel】 that conveys oxygenated 【91†blood】 to the lateral aspect of the 【92†thorax】, the 【79†axilla】 (armpit) and the 【93†upper limb】. Its origin is at the lateral margin of the first 【94†rib】, before which it is called the 【69†subclavian artery】.
L159: 
L160: After passing the lower margin of 【95†teres major】 it becomes the 【76†brachial artery】.
L161: ## Structure
L162: 
L163: [【96†edit】]
L164: 
L165: The axillary artery is often referred to as having three parts,^{【97†[1]】} with these divisions based on its location relative to the 【98†pectoralis minor】 muscle, which is superficial to the artery.
L166: 
L167:   * First part – the part of the artery superior to the pectoralis minor
L168:   * Second part – the part of the artery posterior to the pectoralis minor
L169:   * Third part – the part of the artery inferior to the pectoralis minor.
L170: ### Relations
L171: 
L172: [【99†edit】]
L173: 
L174: The axillary artery is accompanied by the 【78†axillary vein】,^{【100†[2]】} which lies medial to the artery, along its length.
L175: 
L176: In the axilla, the axillary artery is surrounded by the 【101†brachial plexus】.^{【100†[2]】} The second part of the axillary artery is the reference for the locational descriptions of the cords in the 【101†brachial plexus】. For example, the 【102†posterior cord】 of the brachial plexus is so named because it lies posterior to the second part of the artery.
L177: ### Branches
L178: 
L179: [【103†edit】]
L180: 
L181: Branches of axillary artery
L182: The axillary artery has several smaller branches. The branches can be remembered, in order, when traveling from the heart, with the 【104†mnemonics】 "Seek The Lord, Serve All People", "Summertime: The Lakers Schedule Another Parade", "Some Traumas Leave Scars And Pain", or "She Tastes Like Sweet Apple Pie."^{【105†[3]】} The origin of these branches is highly variable (e.g. the posterior and anterior circumflex arteries often have a common trunk). An arterial branch is named for its course, not its origin.
L183:   * First part (1 branch)
L184:     * 【70†Superior thoracic artery】 (Supreme thoracic artery)^{【100†[2]】}
L185:   * Second part (2 branches)
L186:     * 【106†Thoraco-acromial artery】^{【100†[2]】}
L187:     * 【72†Lateral thoracic artery】.^{【100†[2]】} If the lateral thoracic artery is not branching from the axillary artery, will most likely branch from the following (in order of likelihood): (1) thoracoacromial, (2) third part of axillary artery, (3) suprascapular artery, (4) subscapular artery
L188:   * Third part (3 branches)

L138: 【71†Anatomical terminology】
L139: In 【72†human anatomy】, the axillary vein is a large 【73†blood vessel】 that conveys 【74†blood】 from the 【75†lateral】 aspect of the 【76†thorax】, 【58†axilla】 (armpit) and 【77†upper limb】 toward the 【78†heart】. There is one axillary vein on each side of the body.
L140: ## Structure
L141: 
L142: [【79†edit】]
L143: 
L144: Its origin is at the lower margin of the 【80†teres major muscle】 and a continuation of the 【81†brachial vein】.^{【82†[1]】}
L145: This large vein is formed by the 【81†brachial vein】 and the 【56†basilic vein】.^{【83†[2]】} At its terminal part, it is also joined by the 【57†cephalic vein】.^{【83†[2]】} Other tributaries include the 【84†subscapular vein】, 【85†circumflex humeral vein】, 【86†lateral thoracic vein】 and 【87†thoraco-acromial vein】.^{【88†[3]】} It terminates at the lateral margin of the first 【89†rib】, at which it becomes the 【60†subclavian vein】.^{【82†[1]】}
L146: It is accompanied along its course by a similarly named 【61†artery】, the 【62†axillary artery】, which lies laterally to the axillary vein.^{【90†[4]】}

L137: 【66†Anatomical terminology】
L138: The basilic vein is a large 【67†superficial vein】 of the 【56†upper limb】 that helps drain parts of the 【68†hand】 and 【69†forearm】.^{【70†[1]】} It originates on the medial (【71†ulnar】) side of the 【72†dorsal venous network of the hand】 and travels up the base of the 【69†forearm】, where its course is generally visible through the skin as it travels in the subcutaneous fat and 【73†fascia】 lying superficial to the muscles.
L139: The basilic vein terminates by uniting with the 【74†brachial veins】 to form the 【58†axillary vein】.^{【75†[2]】}
L140: ## Anatomy
L141: 
L142: [【76†edit】]
L143: 
L144: ### Course
L145: 
L146: [【77†edit】]
L147: 
L148: As it ascends the medial side of the 【78†biceps】 in the arm proper (between the elbow and shoulder), the basilic vein normally perforates the 【79†brachial fascia】 (【80†deep fascia】) in the middle of the 【81†medial bicipital groove】, and runs upwards medial to the brachial artery to the lower border of 【82†teres major】, continuing as the axillary vein.
L149: ### Tributaries and anastomoses
L150: 
L151: [【83†edit】]
L152: 
L153: Near the region anterior to the 【84†cubital fossa】 (in the bend of the 【85†elbow】 joint), the basilic vein usually communicates with the 【86†cephalic vein】 (the other large superficial vein of the upper extremity) via the 【59†median cubital vein】. The layout of superficial veins in the forearm is highly variable from person to person, and there is a profuse network of unnamed superficial veins that the basilic vein communicates with.
L154: Around the inferior border of the 【82†teres major】 muscle and just proximal to the basilic vein's termination, the anterior and posterior 【87†circumflex humeral veins】 drain into it.
L155: ## Clinical significance
L156: 
L157: [【88†edit】]
L158: 
L159: ### Venipuncture
L160: 
L161: [【89†edit】]
L162: 
L163: Along with other superficial veins in the forearm, the basilic vein is an acceptable site for 【90†venipuncture】. Nevertheless, 【91†IV nurses】 sometimes dub the basilic vein "the virgin vein", since with the arm typically 【92†supinated】 during 【93†phlebotomy】 the basilic vein below the elbow becomes awkward to access, and is therefore infrequently used.
L164: ### Venous grafts
L165: 
L166: [【94†edit】]
L167: 
L168: 【95†Vascular surgeons】 sometimes utilize the basilic vein to create an 【96†AV (arteriovenous) fistula】 or 【96†AV graft】 for 【96†hemodialysis access】 in patients with 【97†kidney failure】.^{【98†[3]】}

L159: 【96†Anatomical terminology】
L160: The brachial artery is the major 【97†blood vessel】 of the (upper) arm. It is the continuation of the 【77†axillary artery】 beyond the lower margin of 【98†teres major muscle】. It continues down the 【99†ventral】 surface of the arm until it reaches the 【100†cubital fossa】 at the 【76†elbow】.
L161: It then divides into the 【81†radial】 and 【82†ulnar】 【101†arteries】 which run down the 【102†forearm】.^{【103†[1]】}^{【104†[2]】} In some individuals, the bifurcation occurs much earlier and the ulnar and radial arteries extend through the upper arm.
L162: The 【105†pulse】 of the brachial artery is 【106†palpable】 on the anterior aspect of the elbow, medial to the 【107†tendon】 of the 【85†biceps】, and, with the use of a 【108†stethoscope】 and 【109†sphygmomanometer】 (blood pressure cuff), often used to measure the 【110†blood pressure】.^{【103†[1]】}
L163: The brachial artery is closely related to the 【111†median nerve】; in proximal regions, the median nerve is immediately lateral to the brachial artery.^{【112†[3]】} Distally, the median nerve crosses the medial side of the brachial artery and lies anterior to the elbow joint.^{【103†[1]】}^{【113†[4]】}
L164: ## Structure
L165: 
L166: [【114†edit】]
L167: 
L168: The brachial artery gives rise to the following branches:^{【113†[4]】}
L169: 
L170:   * 【115†Profunda brachii artery】 (deep brachial artery)
L171:   * 【79†Superior ulnar collateral artery】
L172:   * 【80†Inferior ulnar collateral artery】
L173:   * 【81†Radial artery】 (used to palpate radial pulse)(a terminal branch)
L174:   * 【82†Ulnar artery】 (a terminal branch)
L175:   * Nutrient branches to the 【116†humerus】
L176: 
L177: It also gives rise to important anastomotic networks of the elbow and (as the axillary artery) the shoulder.

L139: 【71†Anatomical terminology】
L140: In 【72†human anatomy】, the cephalic vein^{【73†[1]】} is a 【74†superficial vein】 in the arm. It is the longest vein of the upper limb. It starts at the 【75†anatomical snuffbox】 from the radial end of the 【60†dorsal venous network of hand】, and ascends along the radial (lateral) side of the arm before emptying into the 【61†axillary vein】. At the elbow, it communicates with the 【76†basilic vein】 via the 【62†median cubital vein】.
L141: It is provided with 13 pairs of valves, of which five occur in its antebrachial portion, seven in its brachial portion, and one at its union with the axillary vein.
L142: ## Anatomy
L143: 
L144: [【77†edit】]
L145: 
L146: The cephalic vein is situated within the superficial 【78†fascia】 along the anterolateral surface of the 【79†biceps】.
L147: 
L148: ### Origin
L149: 
L150: [【80†edit】]
L151: 
L152: The cephalic vein forms at the roof of the 【75†anatomical snuffbox】 at the radial end of the 【60†dorsal venous network of hand】.^{【81†[2]】}^{: 983 }
L153: ### Course and relations
L154: 
L155: [【82†edit】]
L156: 
L157: From its origin, it ascends up the lateral aspect of the 【83†radius】.^{【81†[2]】}
L158: 
L159: Near the 【84†shoulder】, the cephalic vein passes between the 【85†deltoid】 and 【86†pectoralis major】 【87†muscles】 (【88†deltopectoral groove】) through the 【89†clavipectoral triangle】, where it empties into the 【61†axillary vein】.^{【90†[3]】}
L160: 
L161: ### Anastomoses
L162: 
L163: [【91†edit】]
L164: 
L165: It communicates with the 【76†basilic vein】 via the 【62†median cubital vein】 at the 【92†elbow】.
L166: ## Clinical significance
L167: 
L168: [【93†edit】]
L169: The cephalic vein is often visible through the 【94†skin】, and its location in the deltopectoral groove is fairly consistent, making this site a good candidate for venous access. 【95†Permanent pacemaker】 leads are often placed in the cephalic vein in the deltopectoral groove. The vein may be used for 【96†intravenous access】, as large bore 【97†cannula】 may be easily placed. However, the cannulation of a vein as close to the radial nerve as the cephalic vein can sometimes lead to nerve damage.
L170: ## History
L171: 
L172: [【98†edit】]
L173: 
L174: Ordinarily the term 【99†cephalic】 refers to anatomy of the head, from the Greek term for the head, kephale. When the Persian Muslim physician 【100†Ibn Sīnā】's 【101†Canon】 was translated into 【102†medieval Latin】, the 【103†Arabic】 term al-kífal 'outer' was mistakenly translated as cephalic.^{【104†[4]】}^{【105†[5]】}

L126: 【58†Anatomical terminology】
L127: The circumflex scapular 【59†artery】 (scapular circumflex artery, dorsalis scapulae artery) is a branch of the 【51†subscapular artery】 and part of the scapular anastomoses.
L128: 
L129: It curves around the axillary border of the scapula, traveling through the anatomical "【60†triangular space】" made up of the 【61†teres minor】 superiorly, the 【62†teres major】 inferiorly, and the long head of the 【63†triceps】 laterally.
L130: It enters the 【64†infraspinatous fossa】 under cover of the 【61†teres minor】, and 【65†anastomoses】 with the 【66†transverse scapular artery】 (suprascapular) and the descending branch of the 【67†transverse cervical】 (a.k.a. 【68†dorsal scapular artery】).
L131: ## Branches
L132: 
L133: [【69†edit】]
L134: 
L135: In its course it gives off two branches:
L136:   * one (infrascapular) enters the 【70†subscapular fossa】 beneath the Subscapularis, which it supplies, anastomosing with the 【66†transverse scapular artery】 and the descending branch of the 【67†transverse cervical】.
L137:   * the other is continued along the axillary border of the scapula, between the 【62†teres major】 and minor, and at the dorsal surface of the 【71†inferior angle】 anastomosis with the descending branch of the transverse cervical (dorsal scapular).
L138: In addition to these, small branches are distributed to the back part of the 【72†deltoid】 and the long head of the Triceps brachii, anastomosing with an ascending branch of the 【73†deep artery of arm】.

L114: Circumflex scapular artery
L115: ---
L116: The scapular and circumflex arteries. (Scapular circumflex visible at center.)
L117: The axillary artery and its branches. (Scap. cir. visible near center.)
L118: Details
L119: ---
L120: Source  | 【52†Subscapular artery】
L121: Identifiers

L123: 【53†Latin】  | arteria circumflexa scapulae
L124: 【54†TA98】  | 【55†A12.2.09.015†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L125: 【54†TA2】  | 【56†4629†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】

L127: 【59†Anatomical terminology】
L128: The circumflex scapular 【60†artery】 (scapular circumflex artery, dorsalis scapulae artery) is a branch of the 【52†subscapular artery】 and part of the scapular anastomoses.
L129: 
L130: It curves around the axillary border of the scapula, traveling through the anatomical "【61†triangular space】" made up of the 【62†teres minor】 superiorly, the 【63†teres major】 inferiorly, and the long head of the 【64†triceps】 laterally.
L131: It enters the 【65†infraspinatous fossa】 under cover of the 【62†teres minor】, and 【66†anastomoses】 with the 【67†transverse scapular artery】 (suprascapular) and the descending branch of the 【68†transverse cervical】 (a.k.a. 【69†dorsal scapular artery】).
L132: ## Branches
L133: 
L134: [【70†edit】]
L135: 
L136: In its course it gives off two branches:
L137:   * one (infrascapular) enters the 【71†subscapular fossa】 beneath the Subscapularis, which it supplies, anastomosing with the 【67†transverse scapular artery】 and the descending branch of the 【68†transverse cervical】.
L138:   * the other is continued along the axillary border of the scapula, between the 【63†teres major】 and minor, and at the dorsal surface of the 【72†inferior angle】 anastomosis with the descending branch of the transverse cervical (dorsal scapular).
L139: In addition to these, small branches are distributed to the back part of the 【73†deltoid】 and the long head of the Triceps brachii, anastomosing with an ascending branch of the 【74†deep artery of arm】.

L113: Costocervical trunk
L114: ---
L115: Neck. Right side.
L116: Details
L117: ---
L118: Source  | 【45†Subclavian artery】
L119: Branches  | 【46†Deep cervical artery】 and
L120: 【47†superior intercostal artery】
L121: Identifiers
L122: ---
L123: 【48†Latin】  | truncus costocervicalis
L124: 【49†TA98】  | 【50†A12.2.08.059†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L125: 【49†TA2】  | 【51†4607†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】
L126: 【52†FMA】  | 【53†10636†bioportal.bioontology.org】
L127: 【54†Anatomical terminology】
L128: The costocervical trunk arises from the superior and posterior part of the second part of 【45†subclavian artery】, behind the 【55†scalenus anterior】 on the right side, and medial to that muscle on the left side.
L129: Passing backward, it splits into the 【46†deep cervical artery】 and the 【56†supreme intercostal artery】 (highest intercostal artery), which descends behind the 【57†pleura】 in front of the necks of the first and second 【58†ribs】, and 【59†anastomoses】 with the first 【60†aortic intercostal】 (3rd posterior intercostal artery).
L130: As it crosses the neck of the first rib it lies medial to the anterior division of the first 【61†thoracic nerve】, and lateral to the first thoracic ganglion of the 【62†sympathetic trunk】.
L131: 
L132: In the first intercostal space, it gives off a branch which is distributed in a manner similar to the distribution of the aortic intercostals.
L133: 
L134: The branch for the second intercostal space usually joins with one from the highest aortic intercostal artery.
L135: This branch is not constant, but is more commonly found on the right side; when absent, its place is supplied by an intercostal branch from the aorta.
L136: 
L137: Each intercostal gives off a posterior branch which goes to the posterior vertebral muscles, and sends a small spinal branch through the corresponding 【63†intervertebral foramen】 to the 【64†medulla spinalis】 and its membranes.

L141: 【70†Anatomical terminology】
L142: The deep artery of arm (also known as deep brachial artery) is a large artery of the arm which arises from the 【58†brachial artery】. It descends in the arm before ending by 【56†anastomosing】 with the 【71†radial recurrent artery】.
L143: ## Structure
L144: 
L145: [【72†edit】]
L146: 
L147: ### Origin
L148: 
L149: [【73†edit】]
L150: 
L151: The deep artery of arm arises from the posterolateral aspect of the 【58†brachial artery】, just below the lower border of the 【74†teres major】.
L152: ### Course
L153: 
L154: [【75†edit】]
L155: It follows closely the 【76†radial nerve】, running at first backward between the long and medial^{【77†[1]】} heads of the 【62†triceps brachii】, then along the groove for the 【76†radial nerve】 (the 【78†radial sulcus】), where it is covered by the lateral head of the triceps brachii, to the lateral side of the arm; there it pierces the 【79†lateral intermuscular septum】, and, descending between the 【80†brachioradialis】 and the 【81†brachialis】 to the front of the 【82†lateral epicondyle of the humerus】, ends by anastomosing with the 【71†radial recurrent artery】.
L156: ### Branches and anastomoses
L157: 
L158: [【83†edit】]
L159: 
L160: It gives branches to the 【61†deltoid muscle】 (which, however, primarily is supplied by the 【84†posterior circumflex humeral artery】) and to the muscles between which it lies; it supplies an occasional 【85†nutrient artery】 which enters the 【86†humerus】 behind the 【87†deltoid tuberosity】.
L161: A branch ascends between the long and lateral heads of the 【62†triceps brachii】 to anastomose with the 【88†posterior humeral circumflex artery】; the 【60†medial collateral artery】, a branch, descends in the middle head of the triceps brachii and assists in forming the anastomosis above the 【89†olecranon】 of the 【90†ulna】; and, lastly, a 【59†radial collateral artery】 runs down behind the 【79†lateral intermuscular septum】 to the back of the lateral epicondyle of the humerus, where it anastomoses with the 【91†interosseous recurrent】 and the 【92†inferior ulnar collateral】 arteries.

L127: The deep cervical artery (profunda cervicalis) is an 【55†artery】 of the neck.
L128: ## Course
L129: 
L130: [【56†edit】]
L131: 
L132: It arises, in most cases, from the 【45†costocervical trunk】, and is analogous to the posterior branch of an 【57†aortic intercostal artery】: occasionally it is a separate branch from the 【58†subclavian artery】.
L133: Passing backward, above the eighth cervical nerve and between the transverse process of the seventh 【59†cervical vertebra】 and the neck of the first rib, it runs up the back of the neck, between the 【60†semispinalis capitis】 and 【61†semispinalis cervicis】, as high as the axis vertebra, supplying these and adjacent muscles, and anastomosing with the deep division of the descending branch of the occipital, and with branches of the vertebral.
L134: It gives off a spinal twig which enters the canal through the 【62†intervertebral foramen】 between the seventh cervical and first 【63†thoracic vertebrae】.

L132: 【59†Anatomical terminology】
L133: The deep palmar arch (deep volar arch^{【60†[1]】}) is an arterial network found in the palm. It is usually primarily formed from the terminal part of the 【48†radial artery】. The 【61†ulnar artery】 also contributes through an 【62†anastomosis】. This is in contrast to the 【63†superficial palmar arch】, which is formed predominantly by the 【61†ulnar artery】.
L134: ## Structure
L135: 
L136: [【64†edit】]
L137: 
L138: The deep palmar arch is usually primarily formed from the radial artery.^{【60†[1]】} The ulnar artery also contributes through an anastomosis.^{【60†[1]】}
L139: 
L140: The deep palmar arch lies upon the bases of the 【65†metacarpal bones】 and on the 【66†interossei】 of the hand. It is deep to the oblique head of the 【67†adductor pollicis】 muscle, the flexor tendons of the fingers,^{【60†[1]】} and the 【68†lumbricals of the hand】.
L141: Alongside of it, but running in the opposite direction—toward the radial side of the hand—is the deep branch of the 【69†ulnar nerve】.
L142: The 【63†superficial palmar arch】 is more distally located than the deep palmar arch.^{【60†[1]】} If one were to fully extend the thumb and draw a line from the distal border of the thumb across the palm, this would be the level of the superficial palmar arch (Boeckel's line). The deep palmar arch is about a finger width proximal to this.
L143: The connection between the deep and superficial palmar arterial arches is an example of 【62†anastomosis】.^{【60†[1]】} This anastomosis can be tested for using 【70†Allen's test】.
L144: The 【50†palmar metacarpal arteries】 arise from the deep palmar arch.^{【60†[1]】}
L145: ## Function
L146: 
L147: [【71†edit】]
L148: 
L149: The deep palmar arch supplies the 【72†thumb】 and the lateral side of the 【73†index finger】.^{【60†[1]】}

L123: 【51†Anatomical terminology】
L124: The dorsal venous network of the hand is a venous network on the 【52†dorsum (backside)】 of hand. It is formed by the 【42†dorsal metacarpal veins】 (three in number), a dorsal digital vein from the radial (lateral) side of the index finger and one from the ulnar (medial) side of the little finger, and both dorsal digital veins of the thumb. The venous network gives rise to the 【43†cephalic vein】 and the 【44†basilic vein】; an 【53†accessory cephalic vein】 may arise from it as well.^{【54†[1]】}

L171: In 【98†human anatomy】, the radial artery is the main 【99†artery】 of the lateral aspect of the 【77†forearm】.
L172: ## Structure
L173: 
L174: [【100†edit】]
L175: The radial artery arises from the bifurcation of the 【76†brachial artery】 in the 【101†antecubital fossa】. It runs distally on the anterior part of the forearm. There, it serves as a landmark for the division between the 【102†anterior】 and 【103†posterior compartments of the forearm】, with the posterior compartment beginning just lateral to the artery.
L176: The artery winds laterally around the 【81†wrist】, passing through the 【104†anatomical snuff box】 and between the heads of the first 【105†dorsal interosseous muscle】. It passes anteriorly between the heads of the 【106†adductor pollicis】, and becomes the 【85†deep palmar arch】, which joins with the deep branch of the 【75†ulnar artery】.
L177: Along its course, it is accompanied by a similarly named 【86†vein】, the 【87†radial vein】.
L178: ### Branches
L179: 
L180: [【107†edit】]
L181: 
L182: The named branches of the radial artery may be divided into three groups, corresponding with the three regions in which the vessel is situated.
L183: #### In the forearm
L184: 
L185: [【108†edit】]
L186:   * 【78†Radial recurrent artery】 - arises just after the radial artery comes off the brachial artery. It travels superiorly to anastomose with the 【109†radial collateral artery】 around the elbow joint
L187:   * 【79†Palmar carpal branch of radial artery】 - a small vessel which arises near the lower border of the 【110†pronator quadratus】
L188:   * 【80†Superficial palmar branch of the radial artery】 - arises from the radial artery, just where this vessel is about to wind around the lateral side of the wrist.
L189: #### At the wrist
L190: 
L191: [【111†edit】]
L192: 
L193: Transverse section through the left wrist, showing the radial artery at the gouttière du pouls. (After Hughes.)
L194:   * 【82†Dorsal carpal branch of radial artery】 - a small vessel which arises beneath the extensor tendons of the thumb
L195:   * First dorsal metacarpal artery - arises just before the radial artery passes between the two heads of the first dorsal interosseous muscle and divides almost immediately into two branches which supply the adjacent sides of the thumb and index finger; the lateral side of the thumb receives a branch directly from the radial artery.
L196: #### In the hand
L197: 
L198: [【112†edit】]
L199: 
L200:   * 【83†Princeps pollicis artery】 - arises from the radial artery just as it turns medially to the deep part of the hand.
L201:   * 【84†Radialis indicis】 - arises close to the princeps pollicis. The two arteries may arise from a common trunk, the first palmar metacarpal artery.
L202:   * 【85†Deep palmar arch】 - terminal part of radial artery.

L137: 【68†Anatomical terminology】
L138: The transverse cervical artery (transverse artery of neck or transversa colli artery) is an artery in the neck and a branch of the 【56†thyrocervical trunk】, running at a higher level than the 【69†suprascapular artery】.
L139: ## Structure
L140: 
L141: [【70†edit】]
L142: 
L143: It passes transversely below the inferior belly of the 【71†omohyoid muscle】 to the anterior margin of the 【72†trapezius】, beneath which it divides into a superficial and a deep branch.
L144: 
L145: It crosses in front of the 【73†phrenic nerve】 and the 【74†scalene muscles】, and in front of or between the divisions of the 【75†brachial plexus】, and is covered by the 【76†platysma】 and 【77†sternocleidomastoid】 muscles, and crossed by the 【78†omohyoid】 and 【72†trapezius】.
L146: The transverse cervical artery originates from the thyrocervical trunk, it passes through the 【79†posterior triangle of the neck】 to the anterior border of the 【80†levator scapulae muscle】, where it divides into deep and superficial branches.
L147:   * 【57†Superficial branch】
L148:     * Ascending branch
L149:     * Descending branch (also known as 【81†superficial cervical artery】, which supplies the middle and lateral portions of the 【60†trapezius】)
L150:   * Deep branch (also called the 【52†dorsal scapular artery】). Descending branch in older literature. Most often, however, this artery branches directly from the 【55†subclavian artery】.
L151: ## Function
L152: 
L153: [【82†edit】]
L154: ### Superficial branch
L155: 
L156: [【83†edit】]
L157: Upon entering the 【60†trapezius】 muscle, the superficial branch divides again into an ascending and descending branch. The ascending branch distributes branches to 【60†trapezius】, and to the neighboring muscles and lymph glands in the neck, and anastomoses with the superficial branch of the descending branch of the 【84†occipital artery】.
L158: The descending branch which is also called as superficial cervical artery,^{【85†[1]】} anastomoses with the deep and 【52†dorsal scapular artery】 which in turn links to the 【86†subscapular artery】. This anastomosis is a ring circulation around the scapula where it continues to the 【69†suprascapular artery】 via the 【87†circumflex scapular artery】.^{【88†[2]】}
L159: ### Deep branch
L160: 
L161: [【89†edit】]
L162: 
L163: The dorsal scapular artery (or descending scapular artery^{【90†[3]】}) is a blood vessel which supplies the 【91†levator scapulae】, 【92†rhomboids】,^{【93†[4]】} and 【72†trapezius】.
L164: It most frequently arises from the 【55†subclavian artery】 (the second or third part),^{【90†[3]】} but a quarter of the time it arises from the transverse cervical artery.^{【94†[5]】} In that case, the artery is also known as the deep branch of the transverse cervical artery, and the junction of those two is called cervicodorsal trunk.
L165: It passes beneath the 【91†levator scapulae】 to the superior angle of the 【95†scapula】, and then descends under the 【92†rhomboid muscles】 along the vertebral border of the scapula as far as the inferior angle.
L166: 
L167: It anastomoses with the 【69†suprascapular】 and 【87†circumflex scapular】 arteries.

L123: The lateral thoracic vein (sometimes debatably referred to as the long thoracic vein) is a tributary of the 【41†axillary vein】. It runs with the 【43†lateral thoracic artery】 and drains the 【51†serratus anterior muscle】 and the 【52†pectoralis major muscle】.

L124: The median antebrachial vein, also known as median vein of forearm, is a 【40†superficial vein】 of the (anterior) 【51†forearm】.
L125: It arises from - and drains - the 【52†superficial palmar venous arch】, ascending superficially along the anterior forearm before ending by opening into the 【43†median cubital vein】 near the junction with the 【42†basilic vein】 within the 【53†cubital fossa】; alternately, it may fork distal to the elbow and proceed to drain into both aforementioned veins.^{【54†[1]】} A bifurcation of the median antebrachial vein produces the (medial) intermediate basilic vein^{【55†[2]】} and the (lateral) intermediate cephalic vein;^{【56†[3]】} the two veins produced by such a split may replace the 【57†median cubital vein】.^{【58†[4]】}^{【55†[2]】}^{【56†[3]】}

L132: 【61†Anatomical terminology】
L133: In 【62†human anatomy】, the median cubital vein (or median basilic vein) is a 【51†superficial vein】 of the 【52†arm】 on the anterior aspect of the elbow. It classically shunts blood from the 【54†cephalic】 to the 【55†basilic vein】 at the roof of the 【63†cubital fossa】. It is typically the most prominent superficial vein in the human body, and is visible when all other veins are hidden by fat or collapsed during a shock.
L134: It arises from the cephalic vein 2.5 cm (one inch) below the lateral epicondyle of the humerus, runs obliquely upward and medially, and empties into the basilic vein 2.5 cm (one inch) above the medial epicondyle.
L135: ## Structure
L136: 
L137: [【64†edit】]
L138: 
L139: The median cubital vein is a 【51†superficial vein】 of the 【52†arm】.^{【65†[1]】} It lies on the anterior aspect of the elbow,^{【66†[2]】} in the 【63†cubital fossa】 superficial to the 【67†bicipital aponeurosis】. It bridges the 【54†cephalic vein】 and the 【55†basilic vein】.^{【68†[3]】}
L140: 
L141: The median cubital vein receives a number of tributaries from the anterior forearm. The 【69†median antebrachial vein】 may or may not drain into the median cubital vein.^{【68†[3]】}
L142: The median cubital vein issues a branch - the perforating vein of the elbow - which pierces the fascial roof of the cubital fossa to join the paired 【70†brachial veins】.^{【68†[3]】}
L143: ### Variations
L144: 
L145: [【71†edit】]
L146: The arrangement of the basilic, cephalic, median cubital, and median antebrachial veins exhibits a wide range of variations. In typical anatomy, the median cubital vein bridges the cephalic and basilic veins across the midline to form a H-pattern.
L147: However, in 【72†variant anatomy】, the median cubial vein is absent, instead replaced by a dominant 【69†median antebrachial vein】 that splits into intermediate cephalic and basilic veins to drain in the cephalic and basilic veins, respectively, forming a M-pattern.
L148: Several other alternative patterns exist, including ones where no anastomosis occurs between the basilic and cephalic veins, and ones where the median cubital vein is doubled.^{【73†[4]】} When the median cubital vein is large, it transfers most or all blood from the cephalic vein to the basilic vein, so that the cephalic vein is either significantly diminished or altogether absent.^{【68†[3]】}
L149: ## Clinical significance
L150: 
L151: [【74†edit】]
L152: 
L153: The median cubital vein is routinely used for 【75†phlebotomy】 and 【76†venipuncture】 (taking blood), and as a site for an intravenous 【77†cannula】.^{【78†[5]】} This is due to its particularly wide 【79†lumen】, and its tendency to remain stationary upon needle insertion.^{【78†[5]】} It becomes prominent when pressure is applied downstream, which makes needle insertion easier.^{【80†[6]】} Such pressure is created using a 【81†tourniquet】.^{【80†[6]】}
