L157: 【93†Anatomical terminology】
L158: The ulnar artery is the main 【94†blood vessel】, with oxygenated 【95†blood】, of the 【96†medial】 aspects of the 【97†forearm】. It arises from the 【71†brachial artery】 and terminates in the superficial palmar arch, which joins with the superficial branch of the 【98†radial artery】. It is palpable on the anterior and medial aspect of the 【99†wrist】.
L159: 
L160: Along its course, it is accompanied by a similarly named 【83†vein】 or veins, the 【84†ulnar vein】 or ulnar veins.
L161: The ulnar artery, the larger of the two terminal branches of the brachial, begins a little below the bend of the 【100†elbow】 in the 【101†cubital fossa】, and, passing obliquely downward, reaches the ulnar side of the forearm at a point about midway between the elbow and the wrist.
L162: It then runs along the ulnar border to the wrist, crosses the 【102†transverse carpal ligament】 on the radial side of the 【103†pisiform bone】, and immediately beyond this bone divides into two branches, which enter into the formation of the 【104†superficial】 and 【105†deep】 volar arches.
L163: ## Branches
L164: 
L165: [【106†edit】]
L166: 
L167: Forearm: 【72†Anterior ulnar recurrent artery】, 【73†Posterior ulnar recurrent artery】, 【107†Common interosseous】 is very short, around 1 cm, and gives rise to the anterior, posterior, and recurrent interosseous arteries and close to the wrist it gives off the 【108†palmar carpal branch】 which is the ulnar contribution to the 【109†palmar carpal arch】 and it also gives a 【110†dorsal carpal branch】 which is the ulnar contribution to 【111†dorsal carpal arch】.
L168: Hand: 【112†Deep palmar branch of ulnar artery】 which passes through the hypothenar muscles to anastomose with the 【105†deep palmar arch】 which is formed predominantly by the 【98†radial artery】 and the terminal branch of the ulnar artery is then to form the 【104†superficial palmar arch】.
L169: ## Relations
L170: 
L171: [【113†edit】]
L172: 
L173: In its upper half, it is deeply seated, being covered by the 【114†Pronator teres】, 【115†Flexor carpi radialis】, 【116†Palmaris longus】, and 【117†Flexor digitorum superficialis】; it lies upon the 【118†Brachialis】 and 【119†Flexor digitorum profundus】.
L174: 
L175: The 【120†median nerve】 is in relation with the medial side of the artery for about 2.5 cm. and then crosses the vessel, being separated from it by the ulnar head of the 【114†Pronator teres】.
L176: In the lower half of the forearm, it lies upon the 【119†Flexor digitorum profundus】, being covered by the integument and the superficial and deep fasciæ, and placed between the 【121†Flexor carpi ulnaris】 and 【117†Flexor digitorum superficialis】.

L127: The palmar metacarpal arteries (volar metacarpal arteries, palmar interosseous arteries) are three or four arteries that arise from the convexity of the 【46†deep palmar arch】.
L128: ## Structure
L129: 
L130: [【56†edit】]
L131: 
L132: The palmar metacarpal arteries arise from the convexity of the 【46†deep palmar arch】.^{【57†[1]】}
L133: 
L134: They run distally upon the 【58†palmar interossei muscles】. They 【59†anastomose】 at the clefts of the 【60†fingers】 with the 【61†common palmar digital arteries】 which arise from the 【62†superficial palmar arch】.^{【57†[1]】}

L136: The posterior humeral circumflex artery (posterior circumflex artery or posterior circumflex humeral artery) arises from the third part of the 【54†axillary artery】 at the distal border of the 【62†subscapularis】.^{【63†[1]】}
L137: ## Anatomy
L138: 
L139: [【64†edit】]
L140: 
L141: ### Course and relations
L142: 
L143: [【65†edit】]
L144: 
L145: It passes posteriorward with the 【66†axillary nerve】 through the 【67†quadrangular space】. It winds laterally around the 【68†surgical neck of the humerus】.^{【63†[1]】}
L146: 
L147: ### Distribution
L148: 
L149: [【69†edit】]
L150: 
L151: It is distributed to the 【70†shoulder joint】,^{【63†[1]】} 【71†teres major】, 【72†teres minor】, 【73†deltoid】,^{【63†[1]】}^{【74†[2]】} and (long and lateral heads of) 【75†triceps brachii】.^{【63†[1]】}
L152: ### Anastomoses
L153: 
L154: [【76†edit】]
L155: 
L156: It forms anastomoses with the 【77†anterior humeral circumflex artery】, (deltoid branch of) 【78†profunda brachii artery】, (acromial branches of) 【79†suprascapular artery】, (acromial branches of) and 【80†thoracoacromial artery】.^{【63†[1]】}

L123: 【50†Anatomical terminology】
L124: The posterior ulnar recurrent artery is an 【51†artery】 in the 【40†forearm】. It is one of two 【52†recurrent arteries】 that arises from the 【42†ulnar artery】, the other being the 【53†anterior ulnar recurrent artery】. The posterior ulnar recurrent artery being much larger than the 【53†anterior】 and also arises somewhat lower than it.
L125: It passes backward and medialward on the 【54†flexor digitorum profundus】, behind the 【55†flexor digitorum superficialis muscle】, and ascends behind the 【56†medial epicondyle】 of the 【57†humerus】.
L126: In the interval between this process and the 【58†olecranon】, it lies beneath the 【59†flexor carpi ulnaris】, and ascending between the heads of that muscle, in relation with the 【60†ulnar nerve】, it supplies the neighboring muscles and the 【61†elbow-joint】, and 【62†anastomoses】 with the 【63†superior】 and 【64†inferior ulnar collateral arteries】 and the 【65†interosseous recurrent】 arteries.

L131: 【63†Anatomical terminology】
L132: The subscapular artery, the largest branch of the 【53†axillary artery】,^{【64†[1]】} arises from the third part of the axillary artery at the lower border of the 【65†subscapularis muscle】, which it follows to the inferior angle of the 【66†scapula】, where it 【67†anastomoses】 with the 【68†lateral thoracic】 and 【69†intercostal arteries】, and with the descending branch of the 【70†dorsal scapular artery】 (a.k.a.
L133: deep branch of the transverse cervical artery if it arises from the cervical trunk), and ends in the neighboring muscles.
L134: About 4 cm from its origin it gives off two branches, first the 【71†scapular circumflex artery】 and then the 【55†thoracodorsal artery】.
L135: 
L136: From the 【55†thoracodorsal artery】, it supplies 【72†latissimus dorsi】, while the 【71†scapular circumflex artery】 participates in the 【73†scapular anastamosis】. It terminates in an anastomosis with the 【70†dorsal scapular artery】.^{【74†[2]】}

L118: Subscapular artery
L119: ---
L120: Axillary artery and its branches, including subscapular artery - anterior view of right upper limb and thorax.
L121: The scapular and circumflex arteries.
L122: Details
L123: ---
L124: Source  | 【54†Axillary artery】
L125: Branches  | 【55†Circumflex scapular artery】, 【56†thoracodorsal artery】
L126: Supplies  | 【57†Latissimus dorsi】
L127: Identifiers
L128: ---
L129: 【58†Latin】  | arteria subscapularis
L130: 【59†TA98】  | 【60†A12.2.09.013†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L131: 【59†TA2】  | 【61†4627†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】
L132: 【62†FMA】  | 【63†22677†bioportal.bioontology.org】
L133: 【64†Anatomical terminology】
L134: The subscapular artery, the largest branch of the 【54†axillary artery】,^{【65†[1]】} arises from the third part of the axillary artery at the lower border of the 【66†subscapularis muscle】, which it follows to the inferior angle of the 【67†scapula】, where it 【68†anastomoses】 with the 【69†lateral thoracic】 and 【70†intercostal arteries】, and with the descending branch of the 【71†dorsal scapular artery】 (a.k.a.
L135: deep branch of the transverse cervical artery if it arises from the cervical trunk), and ends in the neighboring muscles.
L136: About 4 cm from its origin it gives off two branches, first the 【72†scapular circumflex artery】 and then the 【56†thoracodorsal artery】.
L137: 
L138: From the 【56†thoracodorsal artery】, it supplies 【73†latissimus dorsi】, while the 【72†scapular circumflex artery】 participates in the 【74†scapular anastamosis】. It terminates in an anastomosis with the 【71†dorsal scapular artery】.^{【75†[2]】}

L125: 【53†Anatomical terminology】
L126: The suprascapular vein is a vein running above the 【54†scapula】. It drains into the 【45†external jugular vein】. It drains the posterior region around the 【54†scapula】.
L127: ## Structure
L128: 
L129: [【55†edit】]
L130: 
L131: The suprascapular vein runs above the scapula. It runs above the anterior coracospinal ligament.^{【56†[1]】} It lies close to the 【44†suprascapular artery】.^{【57†[2]】}^{【58†[3]】} It drains into the 【45†external jugular vein】.^{【58†[3]】}
L132: ### Variation
L133: 
L134: [【59†edit】]
L135: 
L136: The course of the suprascapular vein is not very variable.^{【56†[1]】} In nearly 20% of people, there may be 2 suprascapular veins lying next to each other.^{【56†[1]】} In a very small minority, there may be three.^{【56†[1]】}
L137: 
L138: ## Function
L139: 
L140: [【60†edit】]
L141: 
L142: The suprascapular vein drains the posterior region around the 【54†scapula】.^{【58†[3]】}

L126: Supplies  | 【55†Supraspinatus muscle】, 【56†infraspinatus muscle】,(【57†sternocleidomastoid】), (【58†subclavius】)

L134: 【65†Anatomical terminology】
L135: The suprascapular artery is a branch of the 【52†thyrocervical trunk】 on the 【66†neck】.^{【67†[1]】}
L136: ## Structure
L137: 
L138: [【68†edit】]
L139: At first, it passes downward and laterally across the 【69†scalenus anterior】 and 【70†phrenic nerve】, being covered by the 【71†sternocleidomastoid muscle】; it then crosses the 【72†subclavian artery】 and the 【73†brachial plexus】, running behind and parallel with the 【74†clavicle】 and 【75†subclavius muscle】 and beneath the inferior belly of the 【76†omohyoid】 to the superior border of the 【77†scapula】.
L140: It passes over the 【78†superior transverse scapular ligament】 in most of the cases while below it through the 【79†suprascapular notch】 in some cases.^{【80†[2]】}^{【81†[3]】}^{【82†[4]】}
L141: The artery then enters the 【83†supraspinous fossa】 of the scapula. It travels close to the bone, running through the 【84†suprascapular canal】 underneath the 【55†supraspinatus muscle】,^{【82†[4]】} to which it supplies branches.
L142: It then descends behind the 【85†neck of the scapula】, through the 【86†great scapular notch】 and under cover of the 【87†inferior transverse ligament】, to reach the 【88†infraspinatous fossa】, where it supplies 【56†infraspinatus】^{【89†[5]】} and anastomoses with the 【90†scapular circumflex artery】 and the descending branch (aka 【91†dorsal scapular artery】) of the 【92†transverse cervical artery】.
L143: ## Function
L144: 
L145: [【93†edit】]
L146: Besides distributing branches to the 【57†sternocleidomastoid】 (which, however, mainly is supplied by the 【94†occipital artery】 and the 【95†superior thyroid artery】), 【58†subclavius】 (which mainly is supplied by the 【96†thoracoacromial artery】), and neighboring muscles, it gives off a suprasternal branch, which crosses over the sternal end of the clavicle to the skin of the upper part of the chest; and an acromial branch, which pierces the 【97†trapezius】 and supplies the skin over the 【98†acromion】, 【99†anastomosing】 with the 【96†thoracoacromial artery】.
L147: Just after supplying the subclavius muscle, it anastomoses with the thoracoacromial artery in supplying skin areas.
L148: As the artery passes over the 【78†superior transverse scapular ligament】, it sends a branch into the 【100†subscapular fossa】, where it ramifies beneath the 【101†subscapularis】, and anastomoses with the 【102†subscapular artery】 and with the 【91†dorsal scapular artery】.
L149: 
L150: It also sends articular branches to the 【103†acromioclavicular joint】 and the 【104†shoulder joint】, and a nutrient artery to the clavicle.

L133: 【62†Anatomical terminology】
L134: The thyrocervical trunks are very small 【63†arteries】 of the neck arising from the 【64†subclavian arteries】, lateral to the 【65†vertebral arteries】.^{【66†[1]】} They divide into branches: the 【53†inferior thyroid artery】, 【54†suprascapular artery】, and the 【55†transverse cervical artery】.
L135: 
L136: The thyrocervical trunks supply the 【67†thyroid gland】 and some scapular muscles.^{【66†[1]】}
L137: ## Structure
L138: 
L139: [【68†edit】]
L140: 
L141: The thyrocervical trunk is a branch of the 【52†subclavian artery】.^{【66†[1]】} It arises from the first portion of this vessel, between the origin of the subclavian artery and the inner border of the 【69†anterior scalene muscle】. It is located distally to the 【70†vertebral artery】 and proximally to the 【71†costocervical trunk】. It is short and wide artery.^{【72†[2]】}
L142: ### Branches
L143: 
L144: [【73†edit】]
L145: 
L146: The thyrocervical trunk soon divides into branches: the 【53†inferior thyroid artery】, the 【54†suprascapular artery】, and the 【55†transverse cervical artery】.^{【72†[2]】}
L147: 
L148: The transverse cervical artery is present in about 2/3 of cases. In a third of cases the superficial cervical artery and the dorsal scapular artery arise as the transverse cervical artery.^{【74†[3]】}
L149: The 【54†suprascapular artery】 and 【55†transverse cervical artery】 both head laterally and cross in front of (anterior to) the anterior scalene muscle and the 【75†phrenic nerve】. The inferior thyroid artery runs superiorly from the thyrocervical trunk to the inferior portion of the thyroid gland. There is significant variation in the origin of these vessels.^{【76†[4]】}

L137: 【68†Anatomical terminology】
L138: The transverse cervical artery (transverse artery of neck or transversa colli artery) is an artery in the neck and a branch of the 【56†thyrocervical trunk】, running at a higher level than the 【69†suprascapular artery】.
L139: ## Structure
L140: 
L141: [【70†edit】]
L142: 
L143: It passes transversely below the inferior belly of the 【71†omohyoid muscle】 to the anterior margin of the 【72†trapezius】, beneath which it divides into a superficial and a deep branch.
L144: 
L145: It crosses in front of the 【73†phrenic nerve】 and the 【74†scalene muscles】, and in front of or between the divisions of the 【75†brachial plexus】, and is covered by the 【76†platysma】 and 【77†sternocleidomastoid】 muscles, and crossed by the 【78†omohyoid】 and 【72†trapezius】.
L146: The transverse cervical artery originates from the thyrocervical trunk, it passes through the 【79†posterior triangle of the neck】 to the anterior border of the 【80†levator scapulae muscle】, where it divides into deep and superficial branches.
L147:   * 【57†Superficial branch】
L148:     * Ascending branch
L149:     * Descending branch (also known as 【81†superficial cervical artery】, which supplies the middle and lateral portions of the 【60†trapezius】)
L150:   * Deep branch (also called the 【52†dorsal scapular artery】). Descending branch in older literature. Most often, however, this artery branches directly from the 【55†subclavian artery】.
L151: ## Function
L152: 
L153: [【82†edit】]
L154: ### Superficial branch
L155: 
L156: [【83†edit】]
L157: Upon entering the 【60†trapezius】 muscle, the superficial branch divides again into an ascending and descending branch. The ascending branch distributes branches to 【60†trapezius】, and to the neighboring muscles and lymph glands in the neck, and anastomoses with the superficial branch of the descending branch of the 【84†occipital artery】.
L158: The descending branch which is also called as superficial cervical artery,^{【85†[1]】} anastomoses with the deep and 【52†dorsal scapular artery】 which in turn links to the 【86†subscapular artery】. This anastomosis is a ring circulation around the scapula where it continues to the 【69†suprascapular artery】 via the 【87†circumflex scapular artery】.^{【88†[2]】}
L159: ### Deep branch
L160: 
L161: [【89†edit】]
L162: 
L163: The dorsal scapular artery (or descending scapular artery^{【90†[3]】}) is a blood vessel which supplies the 【91†levator scapulae】, 【92†rhomboids】,^{【93†[4]】} and 【72†trapezius】.
L164: It most frequently arises from the 【55†subclavian artery】 (the second or third part),^{【90†[3]】} but a quarter of the time it arises from the transverse cervical artery.^{【94†[5]】} In that case, the artery is also known as the deep branch of the transverse cervical artery, and the junction of those two is called cervicodorsal trunk.
L165: It passes beneath the 【91†levator scapulae】 to the superior angle of the 【95†scapula】, and then descends under the 【92†rhomboid muscles】 along the vertebral border of the scapula as far as the inferior angle.
L166: 
L167: It anastomoses with the 【69†suprascapular】 and 【87†circumflex scapular】 arteries.

L136: 【67†Anatomical terminology】
L137: The transverse cervical artery (transverse artery of neck or transversa colli artery) is an artery in the neck and a branch of the 【55†thyrocervical trunk】, running at a higher level than the 【68†suprascapular artery】.
L138: ## Structure
L139: 
L140: [【69†edit】]
L141: 
L142: It passes transversely below the inferior belly of the 【70†omohyoid muscle】 to the anterior margin of the 【71†trapezius】, beneath which it divides into a superficial and a deep branch.
L143: 
L144: It crosses in front of the 【72†phrenic nerve】 and the 【73†scalene muscles】, and in front of or between the divisions of the 【74†brachial plexus】, and is covered by the 【75†platysma】 and 【76†sternocleidomastoid】 muscles, and crossed by the 【77†omohyoid】 and 【71†trapezius】.
L145: The transverse cervical artery originates from the thyrocervical trunk, it passes through the 【78†posterior triangle of the neck】 to the anterior border of the 【79†levator scapulae muscle】, where it divides into deep and superficial branches.
L146:   * 【56†Superficial branch】
L147:     * Ascending branch
L148:     * Descending branch (also known as 【80†superficial cervical artery】, which supplies the middle and lateral portions of the 【59†trapezius】)
L149:   * Deep branch (also called the 【51†dorsal scapular artery】). Descending branch in older literature. Most often, however, this artery branches directly from the 【54†subclavian artery】.
L150: ## Function
L151: 
L152: [【81†edit】]
L153: ### Superficial branch
L154: 
L155: [【82†edit】]
L156: Upon entering the 【59†trapezius】 muscle, the superficial branch divides again into an ascending and descending branch. The ascending branch distributes branches to 【59†trapezius】, and to the neighboring muscles and lymph glands in the neck, and anastomoses with the superficial branch of the descending branch of the 【83†occipital artery】.
L157: The descending branch which is also called as superficial cervical artery,^{【84†[1]】} anastomoses with the deep and 【51†dorsal scapular artery】 which in turn links to the 【85†subscapular artery】. This anastomosis is a ring circulation around the scapula where it continues to the 【68†suprascapular artery】 via the 【86†circumflex scapular artery】.^{【87†[2]】}
L158: ### Deep branch
L159: 
L160: [【88†edit】]
L161: 
L162: The dorsal scapular artery (or descending scapular artery^{【89†[3]】}) is a blood vessel which supplies the 【90†levator scapulae】, 【91†rhomboids】,^{【92†[4]】} and 【71†trapezius】.
L163: It most frequently arises from the 【54†subclavian artery】 (the second or third part),^{【89†[3]】} but a quarter of the time it arises from the transverse cervical artery.^{【93†[5]】} In that case, the artery is also known as the deep branch of the transverse cervical artery, and the junction of those two is called cervicodorsal trunk.
L164: It passes beneath the 【90†levator scapulae】 to the superior angle of the 【94†scapula】, and then descends under the 【91†rhomboid muscles】 along the vertebral border of the scapula as far as the inferior angle.
L165: 
L166: It anastomoses with the 【68†suprascapular】 and 【86†circumflex scapular】 arteries.

L124: 【52†Anatomical terminology】
L125: The anterior ulnar recurrent artery is an 【53†artery】 in the 【54†forearm】. It is one of two 【55†recurrent arteries】 that arises from the 【43†ulnar artery】, the other being the 【56†posterior ulnar recurrent artery】.
L126: It arises from the 【43†ulnar artery】 immediately below the 【42†elbow-joint】, runs upward between the 【57†brachialis】 and 【58†pronator teres muscle】 and supplies twigs to those muscles. In front of the 【59†medial epicondyle】 it 【41†anastomoses】 with the 【60†superior】 and 【45†Inferior ulnar collateral arteries】.

L131: The ulnar veins are 【59†venae comitantes】 of the 【51†ulnar artery】. They drain the 【60†superficial venous palmar arch】.^{【61†[1]】} They arise in the 【62†hand】 and terminate by uniting with the 【63†radial veins】 to form the 【64†brachial veins】. They mostly drain the medial aspect of the 【65†forearm】. They receive the venae comitantes of the 【66†anterior】 and 【67†posterior interosseous】 arteries near the elbow, as well as a large branch from the 【68†median cubital vein】.
L132: The ulnar veins are larger than the 【63†radial veins】.^{【61†[1]】}
L133: They follow the same course as the 【51†ulnar artery】.

L112: Radial artery of index finger
L113: ---
L114: Palm of left hand, showing position of skin creases and bones, and surface markings for the volar arches.
L115: 【43†Ulnar】 and 【44†radial】 arteries. Deep view. (Vol. ind. radialis labeled at lower left.)
L116: Details
L117: ---
L118: Source  | 【45†Deep palmar arch】
L119: Supplies  | 【46†Index finger】
L120: Identifiers
L121: ---
L122: 【47†Latin】  | arteria radialis indicis
L123: 【48†TA98】  | 【49†A12.2.09.037†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L124: 【48†TA2】  | 【50†4651†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】
L125: 【51†FMA】  | 【52†22763†bioportal.bioontology.org】
L126: 【53†Anatomical terminology】
L127: The radialis indicis artery (radial artery of index finger) is a branch of the 【44†radial artery】 that provides blood to the 【46†index finger】.
L128: 
L129: It arises close to the 【54†princeps pollicis artery】, and descends between the first 【55†dorsal interosseous muscle】 and the transverse head of the 【56†adductor pollicis】, and runs along the lateral side of the index finger to its extremity, where it anastomoses with the proper digital artery, supplying the medial side of the finger.
L130: At the lower border of the transverse head of the 【56†adductor pollicis】, this vessel anastomoses with the 【57†princeps pollicis】, and gives a communicating branch to the 【58†superficial palmar arch】.
L131: 
L132: The princeps pollicis and radialis indicis may arise from a common trunk termed the first palmar metacarpal artery.

L113: Princeps pollicis artery
L114: ---
L115: Palm of left hand, showing position of skin creases and bones, and surface markings for the volar arches.
L116: Details
L117: ---
L118: Source  | 【44†Dorsal carpal branch of radial artery】
L119: Supplies  | 【45†Thumb】
L120: Identifiers
L121: ---
L122: 【46†Latin】  | arteria princeps pollicis
L123: 【47†TA98】  | 【48†A12.2.09.036†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L124: 【47†TA2】  | 【49†4650†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】
L125: 【50†FMA】  | 【51†22762†bioportal.bioontology.org】
L126: 【52†Anatomical terminology】
L127: The princeps pollicis artery, or principal artery of the thumb, arises from the 【53†radial artery】 just as it turns medially towards the deep part of the hand; it descends between the first 【54†dorsal interosseous muscle】 and the oblique head of the 【55†adductor pollicis】, along the medial side of the 【56†first metacarpal】 bone to the base of the 【57†proximal phalanx】, where it lies beneath the tendon of the 【58†flexor pollicis longus】 muscle and divides into two branches.
L128: These make their appearance between the medial and lateral insertions of the adductor pollicis, and run along the sides of the thumb, forming an arch on the palmar surface of the distal phalanx, from which branches are distributed to the 【59†integument】 and subcutaneous tissue of the thumb.
L129: The princeps pollicis has a particularly strong 【60†pulse】 and can be used for ascertaining one's heart rate. For this reason, the pulse of the thumb is substantially stronger than that of the other digit, and thus it should not be used to read the pulses of others, as it may produce 【61†false positives】.

L110: Dorsal metacarpal arteries
L111: ---
L112: Arteries of the back of the forearm and hand. (Dorsal metacarpal visible at bottom center.)
L113: Details
L114: ---
L115: Source  | 【42†Dorsal carpal arch】
L116: Branches  | 【43†Dorsal digital arteries】
L117: 【44†Vein】  | 【45†Dorsal metacarpal veins】
L118: Identifiers
L119: ---
L120: 【46†Latin】  | arteriae metacarpales dorsales
L121: 【47†TA98】  | 【48†A12.2.09.034†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L122: 【47†TA2】  | 【49†4648†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】
L123: 【50†FMA】  | 【51†70800†bioportal.bioontology.org】
L124: 【52†Anatomical terminology】
L125: Most of the dorsal metacarpal arteries arise from the dorsal carpal arch and run downward on the second, third, and fourth 【53†dorsal interossei of the hand】 and bifurcate into the 【43†dorsal digital arteries】. Near their origin, they anastomose with the 【54†deep palmar arch】 by perforating arteries. They also anastomose with 【55†common palmar digital arteries】 (from the 【56†superficial palmar arch】), also via perforating arteries.
L126: The first dorsal metacarpal artery arises directly from the 【57†radial artery】 before it crosses through the two heads of the first 【53†dorsal interosseous muscle】.

L116: Details
L117: ---
L118: Source  | 【48†Brachial artery】, 【49†inferior ulnar collateral artery】
L119: Branches  | 【50†posterior ulnar recurrent artery】
L120: Identifiers

L126: 【57†Anatomical terminology】
L127: The superior ulnar collateral artery (inferior profunda artery), of small size, arises from the 【48†brachial artery】 a little below the middle of the arm; it frequently springs from the upper part of the 【58†a. profunda brachii】.
L128: It pierces the 【59†medial intermuscular septum】, and descends on the surface of the 【60†medial head】 of the 【61†Triceps brachii】 to the space between the 【62†medial epicondyle】 and 【63†olecranon】, accompanied by the 【64†ulnar nerve】, and ends under the 【65†Flexor carpi ulnaris】 by anastomosing with the 【66†posterior ulnar recurrent】, and 【67†inferior ulnar collateral】.
L129: 
L130: It sometimes sends a branch in front of the medial epicondyle, to anastomose with the 【68†anterior ulnar recurrent】.

L145: 【77†Anatomical terminology】
L146: In 【78†human anatomy】, the hepatic veins are the 【79†veins】 that drain venous 【80†blood】 from the 【81†liver】 into the 【66†inferior vena cava】 (as opposed to the 【82†hepatic portal vein】 which conveys blood from the gastrointestinal organs to the liver^{【83†[1]】}^{: 1212 }). There are usually three large upper hepatic veins draining from the left, middle, and right parts of the liver, as well as a number (6-20) of lower hepatic veins.^{【84†[2]】} All hepatic veins are valveless.^{【85†[3]】}
L147: ## Structure
L148: 
L149: [【86†edit】]
L150: 
L151: All the hepatic veins drain into the 【66†inferior vena cava】. The hepatic veins are divided into an upper and a lower group.^{【84†[2]】}
L152: ### Upper group
L153: 
L154: [【87†edit】]
L155: 
L156: The upper group consists of three hepatic veins^{【84†[2]】} - the right, middle, and left hepatic veins^{【83†[1]】}^{: 1212 } - draining the central veins from the right, middle, and left regions of the liver and are larger than the lower group of veins.^{【84†[2]】} The veins of the upper group drain into the suprahepatic part of the inferior vena cava (i.e. part superior to the liver).^{【83†[1]】}^{: 1212 }
L157: #### Right hepatic vein
L158: 
L159: [【88†edit】]
L160: The right hepatic vein is the longest and largest of all the hepatic veins. It drains the liver segments VI and VII in their entirety, and variably participates in the drainage of segments V and VIII; the extent of drainage of the latter two segments by the right hepatic veins as opposed to the middle hepatic vein and possible variant accessory veins determines the calibre of the right hepatic vein.
L161: It arises anteriorly near the inferior border of the liver, coursing along the right portal fissure to drain into the inferior vena cava near the superior margin of the caudate lobe. It usually reaches the inferior vena cava as a single vessel, but sometimes drains into it as two separate trunks.^{【83†[1]】}^{: 1212 }
L162: #### Middle hepatic vein
L163: 
L164: [【89†edit】]
L165: 
L166: The middle hepatic vein drains the central portion of the liver, draining segments IV, V, and VIII. The middle hepatic vein most often joins the left hepatic vein to form a short common trunk to drain jointly into the inferior vena cava; the middle hepatic vein drains into the inferior vena cava as a separate vessel in less than 10% of individuals.^{【83†[1]】}^{: 1212 }
L167: #### Left hepatic vein
L168: 
L169: [【90†edit】]
L170: 
L171: The left hepatic vein usually drains liver segments II and III, and occasionally also segment IV. The umbilical fissure vein is a major tributary of the left hepatic vein.^{【83†[1]】}^{: 1213 } The left hepatic vein most often forms a short common trunk with the middle hepatic vein before these jointly drain into the inferior vena cava.^{【83†[1]】}^{: 1212 }
L172: ### Lower group
L173: 
L174: [【91†edit】]
L175: 
L176: The lower group consists of 6-20 smaller hepatic veins which drain the 【92†right lobe】 and the 【93†caudate lobe】, are in contact with the hepatic tissue, and are valveless.^{【84†[2]】} All veins of the lower group drain into the retrohepatic part of the inferior vena cava (i.e. part posterior to the liver).^{【83†[1]】}^{: 1212 }
L177: The lower group consists of 1-5 veins draining the liver segment I, and may consist of (inconsistently present) accessory inferior hepatic vein, accessory middle right hepatic vein, and several smaller retrohepatic veins draining the right lobe of the liver.^{【83†[1]】}^{: 1213 }
L178: ## Clinical significance
L179: 
L180: [【94†edit】]
L181: 
L182: The hepatic veins (and their variant anatomy) are relevant in liver resection and transplantation, and in 【95†Budd–Chiari syndrome】.^{【83†[1]】}
L183: Budd–Chiari syndrome is a condition caused by blockage of the hepatic veins, such as by a 【96†blood clot】. It presents with a "classical triad" of abdominal pain, ascites, and liver enlargement. It occurs in 1 out of a million individuals. The syndrome can be fulminant, acute, chronic, or asymptomatic.
L184: The independent lower veins draining the liver segment I directly into the inferior vena cava are unaffected by obstruction of the large hepatic veins, leading to compensatory hypertrophy.^{【83†[1]】}^{: 1213 }

L150: 【80†Anatomical terminology】
L151: In 【81†human anatomy】, the splenic artery or lienal artery, an older term, is the 【82†blood vessel】 that supplies oxygenated 【83†blood】 to the 【71†spleen】. It branches from the 【62†celiac artery】, and follows a course 【84†superior】 to the 【85†pancreas】. It is known for its tortuous path to the spleen.
L152: ## Structure
L153: 
L154: [【86†edit】]
L155: 
L156: The splenic artery, the largest branch of the celiac trunk, gives off branches to the 【87†stomach】 and pancreas before reaching the spleen.
L157: Branch  | Description
L158: --- | ---
L159: 【63†branches to the pancreas】  | multiple branches serving the 【85†pancreas】 including 【88†greater pancreatic artery】 and 【89†dorsal pancreatic artery】.
L160: 【66†short gastric】  | upper part of 【90†greater curvature of the stomach】 and fundus of the stomach
L161: 【65†left gastroepiploic】  | middle of greater curvature of the 【87†stomach】
L162: 【91†posterior gastric】  | posterior of 【87†stomach】, gastric region superior to the splenic artery
L163: Note that the branches of the splenic artery do not reach all the way to the lower part of the greater curvature of the stomach. Instead, that region is supplied by the 【92†right gastroepiploic artery】, a branch of the 【93†gastroduodenal artery】. The two gastroepiploic arteries 【94†anastomose】 with each other at that point.
L164: ### Relations
L165: 
L166: [【95†edit】]
L167: 
L168: The splenic artery passes between the layers of the 【96†lienorenal ligament】. Along its course, it is accompanied by a similarly named vein, the 【70†splenic vein】, which drains into the 【97†hepatic portal vein】.
L169: ## Clinical significance
L170: 
L171: [【98†edit】]
L172: 
L173: Free fluid seen on 【99†ultrasound】 from a ruptured splenic artery aneurysm^{【100†[1]】}
L174: Splenic artery 【101†aneurysms】 are rare,^{} but still the third most common abdominal aneurysm, after aneurysms of the 【102†abdominal aorta】 and 【103†iliac arteries】.^{}^{} They may occur in pregnant women in the third trimester and rupture carries a maternal mortality of greater than 50% and a fetal mortality of 70 to 90%.
L175: Risk factors include 【104†smoking】 and 【105†hypertension】.^{} For the treatment of patients who represent a high surgical risk, 【106†percutaneous】 【107†endovascular】 treatment may be considered.^{}

L146: 【84†MeSH】  | 【85†D054326†meshb.nlm.nih.gov】
L147: 【86†TA98】  | 【87†A12.3.01.002†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L148: 【86†TA2】  | 【88†4158†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】

L150: 【91†Anatomical terminology】
L151: The coronary sinus (from 【92†Latin】 corona 'crown') is the largest vein of the 【93†heart】.^{【94†[1]】}^{【95†[2]】} It drains over half of the deoxygenated blood from the heart muscle into the 【82†right atrium】. It begins on the backside of the heart, in between the 【96†left atrium】, and 【97†left ventricle】; it begins at the junction of the 【77†great cardiac vein】, and 【81†oblique vein of the left atrium】. It receives multiple tributaries.
L152: It passes across the backside of the heart along a 【98†groove between left atrium and left ventricle】, then drains into the right atrium at the orifice of the coronary sinus (which is usually guarded by the 【99†valve of coronary sinus】).
L153: ## Structure
L154: 
L155: [【100†edit】]
L156: 
L157: ### Origin
L158: 
L159: [【101†edit】]
L160: 
L161: The coronary sinus arises upon the posterior aspect of the heart between the 【96†left atrium】, and 【97†left ventricle】.^{【94†[1]】} The coronary sinus commences at the union of the 【77†great cardiac vein】, and the 【81†oblique vein of the left atrium】.^{【94†[1]】}^{【102†[3]】}^{【103†[4]】} The origin of the coronary sinus is marked by the 【104†Vieussens valve of the coronary sinus】 which is situated at the endpoint of the great cardiac vein.^{【94†[1]】}
L162: ### Course
L163: 
L164: [【105†edit】]
L165: 
L166: The coronary sinus runs transversely in the left 【98†atrioventricular groove (coronary sulcus)】 on the posterior aspect of the heart.^{【106†[5]】} The sinus, before entering the right atrium, is considerably dilated - nearly to the size of the end of the little finger.
L167: ### Fate
L168: 
L169: [【107†edit】]
L170: The coronary sinus drains through the posterior wall of right atrium at the orifice of the coronary sinus.^{【108†[6]】}^{【94†[1]】} This orifice is located at the posteroinferior aspect of the right atrium, just medial^{【94†[1]】} and to the left of the orifice of 【109†inferior vena cava】,^{【108†[6]】} and between the inferior vena cava and the 【110†right atrioventricular orifice】/tricuspid valve.
L171: The orifice is usually guarded by the 【111†valve of coronary sinus】 (a thin, crescent-shaped valve located on the anteroinferior part of the opening into the right atrium).^{【102†[3]】}
L172: ### Tributaries
L173: 
L174: [【112†edit】]
L175: 
L176: The coronary sinus receives blood mainly from the 【79†small】, 【78†middle】, 【77†great】,^{【95†[2]】} and 【113†oblique cardiac veins】. It also receives blood from the 【114†left marginal vein】 and the 【115†left posterior ventricular vein】.
L177:   * 【77†Great cardiac vein】 (run upwards in the 【116†anterior interventricular sulcus】 to the left 【117†atrioventricular groove】 to form the coronary sinus;^{【108†[6]】}
L178:   * 【78†Middle cardiac vein】 (ascends 【118†posterior interventricular sulcus】 to drain into coronary sinus);^{【108†[6]】}
L179:   * 【79†Small cardiac vein】 (accompanies 【119†right coronary artery】 in the right atrioventricular groove to drain into the right side of the coronary sinus;^{【108†[6]】}
L180:   * 【120†Posterior vein of left ventricle】 (accompanies the 【121†left marginal artery】, ascends the posterior wall of left ventricle to drain into the coronary sinus);^{【108†[6]】}
L181:   * 【122†Oblique vein of left atrium】.^{【94†[1]】}
L182: All veins that empty into the coronary sinus except for the oblique vein of the left atrium have valves at their junction with the coronary sinus.^{【94†[1]】}
L183: 
L184: The 【123†anterior cardiac veins】 do not drain into the coronary sinus but drain directly into the right atrium. Some small veins known as 【124†Thebesian veins】 drain directly into any of the four chambers of the heart.
L185: ### Microanatomy
L186: 
L187: [【125†edit】]
L188: 
L189: The wall of the coronary sinus is partly muscular.
L190: 
L191: ## Function
L192: 
L193: [【126†edit】]
L194: 
L195: The coronary sinus is responsible for venous return of about 55% of the cardiac blood supply.^{【94†[1]】}
L196: ## Clinical significance
L197: 
L198: [【127†edit】]
L199: 【128†Electrodes】 can be inserted into and through the coronary sinus to study the 【129†electrophysiology】 of the heart. This includes for a coronary sinus electrogram.^{【106†[5]】} The coronary sinus connects directly with the right atrium.
L200: It will dilate as a result of any condition that causes elevated right atrial pressure, such as pulmonary hypertension.^{【130†[7]】} Dilated coronary sinus is also seen in some congenital cardiovascular conditions, such as persistent left superior vena cava,^{【131†[8]】} and total anomalous pulmonary venous return.^{【132†[9]】}
L201: In 【133†Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy (CRT)】 procedures, a critical step involves the insertion of a pacing lead into the coronary vein system. However, the anatomical configuration of the coronary sinus (CS) exhibits significant variability, necessitating that cardiologists assess and evaluate its characteristics during the procedure.
L202: Complications may arise when tactical decisions must be made before the endovascular implantation of the left ventricular electrode, which can be challenging due to the unique anatomical features of the CS.

L131: 【57†Anatomical terminology】
L132: The great cardiac vein (left coronary vein) is a vein of the heart. It begins at the 【58†apex of the heart】 and ascends along the 【59†anterior interventricular sulcus】^{【60†[1]】} before joining the 【61†oblique vein of the left atrium】 to form the 【50†coronary sinus】^{【62†[2]】} upon the posterior surface of the heart.
L133: ## Anatomy
L134: 
L135: [【63†edit】]
L136: 
L137: ### Course
L138: 
L139: [【64†edit】]
L140: 
L141: The great cardiac vein ascends along the 【59†anterior interventricular sulcus】^{【60†[1]】} to the base of the 【65†ventricles】. It then curves around the left margin of the heart to reach the posterior surface.^{【62†[2]】}
L142: ### Fate
L143: 
L144: [【66†edit】]
L145: 
L146: Upon reaching the posterior surface of the heart,^{【67†[3]】} the great cardiac vein merges with the 【61†oblique vein of the left atrium】 to form the 【50†coronary sinus】.^{【62†[2]】}^{【67†[3]】} At the junction of the great cardiac vein and the coronary sinus, there is typically a valve present. This is the 【68†Vieussens valve of the coronary sinus】.^{【62†[2]】}
L147: ### Tributaries
L148: 
L149: [【69†edit】]
L150: 
L151: The great cardiac vein receives tributaries from the 【70†left atrium】 and from both ventricles: one, the 【71†left marginal vein】, is of considerable size, and ascends along the left margin of the heart.

L157: 【85†Anatomical terminology】
L158: The coronary arteries are the 【86†arterial blood vessels】 of 【87†coronary circulation】, which transport 【88†oxygenated blood】 to the 【89†heart muscle】. The 【90†heart】 requires a continuous supply of oxygen to function and survive, much like any other tissue or organ of the body.^{【91†[1]】}
L159: The coronary arteries wrap around the entire heart. The two main branches are the 【92†left coronary artery】 and 【93†right coronary artery】. The arteries can additionally be categorized based on the area of the heart for which they provide circulation. These categories are called epicardial (above the 【94†epicardium】, or the outermost tissue of the heart) and microvascular (close to the 【95†endocardium】, or the innermost tissue of the heart).^{【96†[2]】}
L160: Reduced function of the coronary arteries can lead to decreased flow of oxygen and nutrients to the heart. Not only does this affect supply to the heart muscle itself, but it also can affect the ability of the heart to pump blood throughout the body. Therefore, any disorder or disease of the coronary arteries can have a serious impact on health, possibly leading to 【97†angina】, a 【98†heart attack】, and even death.^{【99†[3]】}
L161: ## Structure
L162: 
L163: [【100†edit】]
L164: 
L165: The coronary arteries are mainly composed of the left and right coronary arteries, both of which give off several branches, as shown in the 'coronary artery flow' figure.
L166:   * Coronary artery flow【101†Aorta】
L167:     * 【92†Left coronary artery】
L168:       * 【102†Left anterior descending artery】
L169:       * 【103†Left circumflex artery】
L170:       * 【104†Posterior descending artery】
L171:       * Ramus or intermediate artery
L172:     * 【93†Right coronary artery】
L173:       * 【105†Right marginal artery】
L174:       * 【104†Posterior descending artery】
L175: The 【92†left coronary artery】 arises from the 【101†aorta】 within the left cusp of the 【106†aortic valve】 and feeds blood to the left side of the 【90†heart】. It branches into two arteries, the 【102†left anterior descending】 and the 【107†left circumflex】. The left anterior descending artery perfuses the 【108†interventricular septum】 and anterior wall of the 【109†left ventricle】. The left circumflex artery perfuses the left ventricular free wall.
L176: In approximately 33% of individuals, the left coronary artery gives rise to the 【104†posterior descending artery】^{【110†[4]】} which perfuses the posterior and inferior walls of the left ventricle. Sometimes a third branch is formed at the fork between left anterior descending and left circumflex arteries, known as a ramus or intermediate artery.^{【111†[5]】}
L177: The 【93†right coronary artery】 (RCA) originates within the right cusp of the aortic valve. It travels down the right 【112†coronary sulcus】, towards the 【113†crux of the heart】. The RCA primarily branches into the 【114†right marginal arteries】, and, in 67% of individuals, gives place to the posterior descending artery.^{【110†[4]】} The right marginal arteries perfuse the right ventricle and the posterior descending artery perfuses the left ventricular posterior and inferior walls.
L178: There is also the conus artery, which is only present in about 45 percent of the human population, and which provides collateral blood flow to the heart when the left anterior descending artery is occluded.^{【115†[6]】}^{【116†[7]】}
L179: ## Clinical significance
L180: 
L181: [【117†edit】]
L182: 
L183: Main article: 【118†Coronary artery disease】
L184: 
L185: Atherosclerosis
L186: Narrowing of the arteries can be caused by a process known as 【119†atherosclerosis】 (most common), 【120†arteriosclerosis】, or 【121†arteriolosclerosis】. This occurs when 【122†plaques】 (made up of deposits of 【123†cholesterol】 and other substances) build up over time in the walls of the arteries. 【118†Coronary artery disease】 (CAD) or ischemic heart disease are the terms used to describe narrowing of the coronary arteries.^{【124†[8]】}
L187: As the disease progresses, plaque buildup can partially block blood flow to the heart muscle. Without enough blood supply (【125†ischemia】), the heart is unable to work properly, especially under increased stress. 【97†Stable angina】 is chest pain on exertion that improves with rest. 【126†Unstable angina】 is chest pain that can occur at rest, feels more severe, and/or last longer than stable angina. It is caused by more severe narrowing of the arteries.^{【127†[9]】}
L188: 
L189: Heart attack
L190: A 【98†heart attack】 results from a sudden plaque rupture and formation of a 【128†thrombus】 (blood clot) that completely blocks blood flow to a portion of the heart, leading to tissue death (【129†infarct】).
L191: 
L192: CAD can also result in 【130†heart failure】 or 【131†arrhythmias】. Heart failure is caused by chronic oxygen deprivation due to reduced blood flow, which weakens the heart over time. Arrhythmias are caused by inadequate blood supply to the heart that interferes with the heart's electric impulse.
L193: The coronary arteries can constrict as a response to various stimuli, mostly chemical. This is known as a 【132†coronary reflex】.
L194: There is also a rare condition known as 【133†spontaneous coronary artery dissection】, in which the wall of one of the coronary arteries tears, causing severe pain.^{【134†[10]】} Unlike CAD, spontaneous coronary artery dissection is not due to plaque buildup in arteries, and tends to occur in younger individuals, including women who have recently given birth or men who do intense exercise.^{【135†[11]】}
L195: Coronary artery dominance is described as the coronary artery that give branches to supply the right posterior descending artery and supplies the inferior wall of the heart. In 80 to 85% of the population, the right coronary artery supplies the posterior descending artery, making it right heart dominant while in 7 to 13% of the population, the left coronary artery supplies the posterior descending artery, making it left heart dominant.
L196: In 7 to 8% of the population, both right and left coronary arteries supplies the posterior descending artery, making it right and left co-dominance. Narrowing of coronary arteries is more frequent in those who are left dominant when compared to those who have right dominant or co-dominant hearts.^{【136†[12]】}
L197: ## Name etymology
L198: 
L199: [【137†edit】]
L200: 
L201: 【138†Radiant crown】
L202: 
L203: Model of human heart
L204: 
L205: The word corona is a 【139†Latin】 word that means "crown", from the 【140†Ancient Greek】 κορώνη (korōnè, "garland, wreath"). It was applied to the coronary arteries because of a notional resemblance (compare the photos).
L206: 
L207: The word arterie in Anglo-French (artaire in 【141†Old French】, and artērium in Latin) means "windpipe" and "an artery". It was applied to the coronary arteries because the arteries do not contain blood after death.

L148: The middle cardiac vein commences at the 【70†apex of the heart】. It passes posteriorly along the 【71†inferior interventricular sulcus】 to end at the 【61†coronary sinus】 near the sinus' termination.^{【72†[1]】}
L149: ## Structure
L150: 
L151: [【73†edit】]
L152: 
L153: ### Origin
L154: 
L155: [【74†edit】]
L156: 
L157: The middle cardiac vein commences at the 【70†cardiac apex】 (here, it is contiguous with the 【60†great cardiac vein】, thus forming - along with the 【61†coronary sinus】 - a complete venous circle).^{【72†[1]】}
L158: 
L159: ### Variation
L160: 
L161: [【75†edit】]
L162: 
L163: The middle cardiac vein has a constant location on the surface of the 【76†ventricles】.^{【77†[2]】}
L164: ## Clinical significance
L165: 
L166: [【78†edit】]
L167: 
L168: The middle cardiac vein is useful for epicardial access to the inferior side of the ventricles.^{【79†[3]】}

L145: 【70†Anatomical terminology】
L146: The small cardiac vein, also known as the right coronary vein,^{【71†[1]】} is a 【72†coronary vein】 that drains parts of the 【73†right atrium】 and 【74†right ventricle】 of the 【49†heart】.^{【75†[2]】} Despite its size, it is one of the major drainage vessels for the heart.^{【76†[3]】}
L147: ## Anatomy
L148: 
L149: [【77†edit】]
L150: 
L151: ### Course
L152: 
L153: [【78†edit】]
L154: 
L155: The small cardiac vein runs in the 【79†coronary sulcus】 between the right atrium and right ventricle, and opens into the right extremity of the 【63†coronary sinus】.^{【71†[1]】}^{【75†[2]】}
L156: 
L157: ### Territory
L158: 
L159: [【80†edit】]
L160: 
L161: The small cardiac vein receives 【81†blood】 from the posterior portion of the right atrium and ventricle.^{【75†[2]】}
L162: ### Variation
L163: 
L164: [【82†edit】]
L165: 
L166: The small cardiac vein may empty into the 【63†coronary sinus】, 【83†right atrium】, or 【62†middle cardiac vein】. It may be absent.^{【84†[4]】}

L143: 【65†Anatomical terminology】
L144: The anterior cardiac veins (or anterior veins of right ventricle) are a variable number of small 【66†veins】 (usually 2-5)^{【67†[1]】} which drain blood from the anterior portion of the 【68†right ventricle】 into the 【58†right atrium】.^{【67†[1]】}^{【69†[2]】}
L145: ## Anatomy
L146: 
L147: [【70†edit】]
L148: 
L149: The 【71†right marginal vein】 frequently opens into the right atrium,^{【67†[1]】} and is therefore sometimes regarded as belonging to this group.
L150: 
L151: ### Fate
L152: 
L153: [【72†edit】]
L154: 
L155: Unlike most 【73†cardiac veins】, the anterior cardiac veins do not end in the 【57†coronary sinus】; instead, they drain directly into^{【69†[2]】} the anterior wall of the 【58†right atrium】.^{【69†[2]】}

L136: 【63†Anatomical terminology】
L137: The left anterior descending artery (LAD), also called the anterior interventricular artery (IVA, or anterior interventricular branch of the left coronary artery)^{【64†[1]】} is a branch of the 【65†left coronary artery】. It supplies the anterior portion of the 【66†left ventricle】.^{【67†[2]】} It provides about half of the arterial supply to the left ventricle and is thus considered the most important vessel supplying the left ventricle.
L138: 【68†Blockage】 of the proximal LAD is often dubbed the "widow-maker" infarction due to its poor prognosis.^{【69†[3]】}
L139: ## Anatomy
L140: 
L141: [【70†edit】]
L142: ### Course
L143: 
L144: [【71†edit】]
L145: 
L146: The LAD arises from the left main coronary artery just beyond the 【72†pulmonary artery】. It advances to the 【73†anterior interventricular sulcus】, along which it descends to the 【74†notch of cardiac apex】. A common variant of the LAD, the "wraparound LAD", wraps around the apex and terminates on the posterior wall.^{【75†[4]】}
L147: Although rare, multiple anomalous courses of the LAD have been described. These include the origin of the artery from the right 【76†aortic sinus】.^{【77†[5]】}
L148: ### Branches
L149: 
L150: [【78†edit】]
L151: 
L152: The LAD gives off two types of branches: diagonal branches and septal perforators.
L153: 
L154:   * Septal perforators originate from the LAD, normal to the surface of the heart, perforating and supplying the anterior 2/3 of the 【55†interventricular septum】.
L155:   * Diagonals run along the surface of the heart and supply the lateral wall of the 【56†left ventricle】 and the anterolateral 【79†papillary muscle】.
L156: ### Segments
L157: 
L158: [【80†edit】]
L159:   * Proximal: from LAD origin to, and including, the origin of the first septal branch^{【81†[6]】}^{【82†[7]】} (according to some definitions, to the first diagonal, or to whichever comes first).
L160:   * Middle: from proximal segment to halfway of remaining distance to apex.^{【81†[6]】}^{【82†[7]】} A more technical definition is from the proximal segment to the point where the LAD forms an angle, as seen from a right anterior oblique view on 【83†angiography】, which is often close to the origin of the second diagonal branch.^{【84†[8]】}
L161:   * Distal: from middle segment to apex,^{【81†[6]】}^{【82†[7]】} or in some cases beyond.^{【84†[8]】}
L162: ## Function
L163: 
L164: [【85†edit】]
L165: 
L166: The artery supplies the anterior region of the left ventricle, including: the anterolateral 【54†myocardium】, apex, anterior 【55†interventricular septum】, and anterolateral 【79†papillary muscle】.^{【86†[9]】} The LAD typically supplies 45–55% of the 【56†left ventricle】 and is therefore considered the most critical vessel in terms of myocardial blood supply.
L167: Left: Critical stenosis (95%) of the proximal LAD in a patient with 【87†Wellens syndrome】.
L168: Right: The same patient after 【88†reperfusion】.
L169: ## Disease
L170: 
L171: [【89†edit】]
L172: 
L173:  | This section does not 【90†cite】 any 【91†sources】. Please help 【92†improve this section】 by 【93†adding citations to reliable sources】. Unsourced material may be challenged and 【94†removed】. (September 2026) (【95†Learn how and when to remove this message】)
L174: Pathologies associated with the LAD include 【96†atherosclerosis】, which can lead to plaque rupture, artery occlusion and subsequent 【97†myocardial infarction】 (MI). The "widowmaker" heart attack is an MI in which the proximal LAD becomes occluded. This type of occlusion is severe given the large territory of myocardium supplied by the LAD, especially in patients with anomalous or wraparound LADs.
L175: 
L176: LAD occlusion is best diagnosed by 12-lead 【98†electrocardiogram】 (ECG).

L142: 【66†Anatomical terminology】
L143: In the 【67†coronary circulation】, the posterior descending artery (PDA), also called the posterior interventricular artery (PIV, PIA, or PIVA), is an 【68†artery】 running in the 【69†posterior interventricular sulcus】 to the 【70†apex of the heart】 where it meets with the 【71†left anterior descending artery】 also known as the anterior interventricular artery. The PDA supplies the posterior third of the 【59†interventricular septum】.
L144: The remaining anterior two-thirds is supplied by the 【71†left anterior descending artery】, which is a branch of 【46†left coronary artery】.
L145: It is typically a branch of the 【42†right coronary artery】 (70%, known as right dominance). Alternately, the PDA can be a branch of the 【72†circumflex coronary artery】 (10%, known as left dominance) which itself is a branch of the left coronary artery. It can also be supplied by an 【73†anastomosis】 of the left and right coronary artery (20%, known as co-dominance).^{【74†[2]】}
L146: 
L147: Variants have been reported.^{【75†[3]】}
L148: The anatomical position of the artery is not really posterior, but inferior. The terminology posterior is based on viewing the heart from the "Valentine" position, not by the heart's actual position in the body.^{【76†[4]】}

L174: 【107†Anatomical terminology】
L175: A pulmonary artery is an 【108†artery】 in the 【109†pulmonary circulation】 that carries deoxygenated 【110†blood】 from the right side of the 【111†heart】 to the 【112†lungs】. The largest pulmonary artery is the main pulmonary artery or pulmonary trunk from the 【111†heart】, and the smallest ones are the 【113†arterioles】, which lead to the 【114†capillaries】 that surround the 【115†pulmonary alveoli】.
L176: ## Structure
L177: 
L178: [【116†edit】]
L179: The pulmonary arteries are 【117†blood vessels】 that carry 【118†systemic venous blood】 from the right ventricle of the heart to the 【114†microcirculation】 of the lungs. Unlike in other organs where arteries supply oxygenated blood, the blood carried by the pulmonary arteries is deoxygenated, as it is venous blood returning to the lungs.
L180: The main pulmonary arteries emerge from the right side of the heart and then split into smaller arteries that progressively divide and become 【113†arterioles】, eventually narrowing into the capillary microcirculation of the lungs where gas exchange occurs.
L181: ### Pulmonary trunk
L182: 
L183: [【119†edit】]
L184: 
L185: 【120†Volume rendering】 of a 【121†high resolution】 【122†CT scan】 of the 【123†thorax】. The anterior thoracic wall, the airways and the pulmonary vessels anterior to the 【124†root of the lung】 have been digitally removed to visualize the different levels of the pulmonary circulation.
L186: In order of blood flow, the pulmonary arteries start as the pulmonary trunk that leaves the fibrous pericardium (【125†parietal pericardium】) of the 【126†ventricular outflow tract】 of 【99†right ventricle】 (also known as 【127†infundibulum or conus arteriosus】.^{【128†[1]】} The outflow track runs superiorly and to the left, posterior to the 【129†pulmonary valve】.^{【128†[1]】} The pulmonary trunk bifurcates into right and left pulmonary arteries below the 【130†arch of aorta】 and in front of the left main bronchus.^{【128†[1]】} Pulmonary trunk is short and wide – approximately 5 centimetres (2.0 in) in length^{【131†[2]】} and 2 centimetres (0.79 in)-3 centimetres (1.2 in) in diameter.^{【132†[3]】}^{【133†[4]】}
L187: The pulmonary trunk splits into the right and the left main pulmonary artery.^{【134†[5]】} The left main pulmonary artery is shorter than the right,^{【128†[1]】} passes behind and downwards the descending aorta and above the left main bronchus to the root of the left lung.
L188: Above, the left main pulmonary artery is connected to the concavity of the proximal 【135†descending aorta】 by the 【136†ligamentum arteriosum】.^{【131†[2]】} The right pulmonary artery passes across the midline of the body, below the 【137†carina of trachea】, and comes in front of the right main bronchus.^{【128†[1]】}
L189: ### Branches
L190: 
L191: [【138†edit】]
L192: 
L193: At the far end, pulmonary arteries (labelled at the bottom) become capillaries at the 【115†pulmonary alveoli】.
L194: 
L195: The left main pulmonary artery then divides into two lobar arteries, one for each lobe of the left lung.^{【139†[6]】}
L196: At the right 【124†root of the lung】, it bifurcates into artery that supplies the right upper lobe of the lung, in front of the right upper lobe bronchus, and interlobar artery that supplies the right middle and inferior lobes of the lung, running together with bronchus intermedius.^{【128†[1]】}
L197: The right and left main pulmonary (lungs) arteries give off branches that supplies the corresponding 【140†lung lobes】. In such cases it is termed lobar arteries.^{【141†[7]】} The lobar arteries branch into segmental arteries (roughly 1 for each segment).
L198: Segmental arteries run together with segmental bronchi, at the posterolateral surfaces of the bronchi.^{【141†[7]】} These in turn branch into subsegmental pulmonary arteries.^{【141†[7]】} These eventually form intralobular arteries.^{【142†[8]】} The pulmonary arteries supply the alveoli of the lungs. In contrast, 【143†bronchial arteries】, that has different origins, supply the bronchi of the lungs.^{【128†[1]】}
L199: ## Development
L200: 
L201: [【144†edit】]
L202: 
L203: The pulmonary arteries originate from the 【95†truncus arteriosus】 and the sixth 【145†pharyngeal arch】. The truncus arteriosus is a structure that forms during the 【146†development of the heart】 as a successor to the 【147†conus arteriosus】.^{【148†[9]】}^{: 157 }
L204: By the third week of 【149†development】, the 【150†endocardial tubes】 have developed a swelling in the part closest to the heart.
L205: The swelling is known as the 【151†bulbus cordis】 and the upper part of this swelling develops into the 【95†truncus arteriosus】.^{【148†[9]】}^{: 159–160 } The structure is ultimately mesodermal in origin.^{【148†[9]】}^{: 157 } During 【146†development of the heart】, the heart tissues undergo folding, and the truncus arteriosus is exposed to what will eventually be both the left and right ventricles.
L206: As a 【152†septum】 develops between the two ventricles of the heart, two bulges form on either side of the truncus arteriosus. These progressively enlarge until the trunk splits into the 【153†aorta】 and pulmonary arteries.^{【148†[9]】}^{: 176–179 } Failure of these processes can lead to 【154†pulmonary artery agenesis】.
L207: During 【155†early development】, the 【156†ductus arteriosus】 connects the pulmonary trunk and the 【157†aortic arch】, allowing blood to bypass the fetus's 【158†amniotic fluid-filled】 non-functioning lungs.^{【159†[10]】}^{: 791 }Because the fetus develops within the fluid-filled 【160†amniotic sac】, hence it relies on the 【161†placenta】 for respiratory gas exchange rather than the lungs.^{【162†[11]】}
L208: ## Function
L209: 
L210: [【163†edit】]
L211: 
L212: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the 【99†right ventricle】 to the lungs.^{【164†[12]】} The blood here passes through 【165†capillaries】 adjacent to 【115†alveoli】 and becomes 【166†oxygenated】 as part of the process of 【167†respiration】.^{【168†[13]】}
L213: 
L214: In contrast to the pulmonary arteries, the 【143†bronchial arteries】 supply nutrition to the lungs themselves.^{【159†[10]】}^{: 790 }
L215: ### Pressure
L216: 
L217: [【169†edit】]
L218: The pulmonary artery pressure (PA pressure) is a measure of the 【170†blood pressure】 found in the main pulmonary artery. This is measured by inserting a 【171†catheter】 into the main pulmonary artery.^{【172†[14]】} ^{: 190–191 } The mean pressure is typically 9–18 mmHg,^{【173†[15]】} and the 【174†wedge pressure】 measured in the 【175†left atrium】 may be 6–12 mmHg.
L219: The wedge pressure may be elevated in 【176†left heart failure】,^{【172†[14]】}^{: 190–191 } 【177†mitral valve stenosis】, and other conditions, such as 【178†sickle cell disease】.^{【179†[16]】}
L220: ## Clinical significance
L221: 
L222: [【180†edit】]
L223: The pulmonary artery is relevant in a number of clinical states.

L160: 【91†Anatomical terminology】
L161: The pulmonary veins are the 【92†veins】 that transfer 【93†oxygenated blood】 from the 【94†lungs】 to the 【95†heart】. The largest pulmonary veins are the four main pulmonary veins, two from each lung that drain into the 【80†left atrium】 of the heart. The pulmonary veins are part of the 【96†pulmonary circulation】.
L162: ## Structure
L163: 
L164: [【97†edit】]
L165: 
L166: There are four main pulmonary veins, two from each lung – an inferior and a superior main vein, emerging from each 【98†hilum】. The main pulmonary veins receive blood from three or four feeding veins in each lung, and drain into the 【80†left atrium】. The peripheral feeding veins do not follow the bronchial tree. They run between the pulmonary segments from which they drain the blood.^{【99†[1]】}
L167: At the root of the lung, the right superior pulmonary vein lies in front of and a little below the pulmonary artery; the inferior is situated at the lowest part of the lung hilum. Behind the pulmonary artery is the 【100†bronchus】.^{【101†[2]】} The right main pulmonary veins (contains oxygenated blood) pass behind the 【102†right atrium】 and 【103†superior vena cava】; the left in front of the descending 【104†thoracic aorta】.
L168: ### Variation
L169: 
L170: [【105†edit】]
L171: 
L172: Occasionally the three lobar veins on the right side remain separate, and not infrequently the two left lobar veins end by a common opening into the left atrium. Therefore, the number of pulmonary veins opening into the left atrium can vary between three and five in the healthy 【106†population】.
L173: 
L174: The two left lobar veins may be united as a single pulmonary vein in about 25% of people; the two right veins may be united in about 3%.^{【101†[2]】}
L175: ## Function
L176: 
L177: [【107†edit】]
L178: 
L179: Further information: 【96†Pulmonary circulation】
L180: 
L181: The pulmonary veins play an essential role in 【108†respiration】, by receiving blood that has been oxygenated in the 【109†alveoli】 and returning it to the left atrium.
L182: ## Clinical significance
L183: 
L184: [【110†edit】]
L185: 
L186: As part of the pulmonary circulation they carry oxygenated blood back to the heart, as opposed to the veins of the 【111†systemic circulation】 which carry deoxygenated blood. By definition, a 【92†vein】 is a blood vessel that carries blood to the heart, whether oxygenated or deoxygenated.
L187: A groundbreaking study published in 1998 identified the pulmonary vein as the predominant trigger for 【112†atrial fibrillation】.^{【113†[3]】} Atrial fibrillation frequently results from bursts of 【114†tachycardia】 that originate in muscle bundles extending from the 【115†atrium】 to the pulmonary veins.^{【116†[4]】} Pulmonary vein anatomy is highly variable among atrial fibrillation patients.^{【117†[5]】} Pulmonary vein isolation by 【118†transcatheter ablation】 can restore 【119†sinus rhythm】.^{【116†[4]】} As atrial fibrillation becomes more persistent, the junction between the pulmonary veins and the 【120†left atrium】 becomes less of an initiator and the left atrium becomes an independent source of arrhythmias.^{【121†[6]】} Pulmonary vein isolation ablation technology has used thermal methods (【122†radiofrequency ablation】 or 【123†cryoablation】), which can damage adjacent tissues, notably the 【124†esophagus】, lung or 【125†phrenic nerve】.^{【126†[7]】} 【127†Electroporation】, however, eliminates the risk of thermal damage.^{【126†[7]】} Atrial fibrillation most often recurs after ablation because of pulmonary vein reconnection.^{【128†[8]】}
L188: On chest X-ray, the diameters of pulmonary veins increases from upper to lower lobes, from 3 mm at the first intercoastal space, to 6 mm just above the diaphragm.^{【129†[9]】}
L189: 
L190: A rare 【130†genetic defect】 of the pulmonary veins can cause them to drain into the pulmonary circulation in whole or in part, this is known as a total 【131†anomalous pulmonary venous connection】 (or drainage), or partial anomalous pulmonary connection, respectively.

L160: 【91†Anatomical terminology】
L161: The pulmonary veins are the 【92†veins】 that transfer 【93†oxygenated blood】 from the 【94†lungs】 to the 【95†heart】. The largest pulmonary veins are the four main pulmonary veins, two from each lung that drain into the 【80†left atrium】 of the heart. The pulmonary veins are part of the 【96†pulmonary circulation】.
L162: ## Structure
L163: 
L164: [【97†edit】]
L165: 
L166: There are four main pulmonary veins, two from each lung – an inferior and a superior main vein, emerging from each 【98†hilum】. The main pulmonary veins receive blood from three or four feeding veins in each lung, and drain into the 【80†left atrium】. The peripheral feeding veins do not follow the bronchial tree. They run between the pulmonary segments from which they drain the blood.^{【99†[1]】}
L167: At the root of the lung, the right superior pulmonary vein lies in front of and a little below the pulmonary artery; the inferior is situated at the lowest part of the lung hilum. Behind the pulmonary artery is the 【100†bronchus】.^{【101†[2]】} The right main pulmonary veins (contains oxygenated blood) pass behind the 【102†right atrium】 and 【103†superior vena cava】; the left in front of the descending 【104†thoracic aorta】.
L168: ### Variation
L169: 
L170: [【105†edit】]
L171: 
L172: Occasionally the three lobar veins on the right side remain separate, and not infrequently the two left lobar veins end by a common opening into the left atrium. Therefore, the number of pulmonary veins opening into the left atrium can vary between three and five in the healthy 【106†population】.
L173: 
L174: The two left lobar veins may be united as a single pulmonary vein in about 25% of people; the two right veins may be united in about 3%.^{【101†[2]】}
L175: ## Function
L176: 
L177: [【107†edit】]
L178: 
L179: Further information: 【96†Pulmonary circulation】
L180: 
L181: The pulmonary veins play an essential role in 【108†respiration】, by receiving blood that has been oxygenated in the 【109†alveoli】 and returning it to the left atrium.
L182: ## Clinical significance
L183: 
L184: [【110†edit】]
L185: 
L186: As part of the pulmonary circulation they carry oxygenated blood back to the heart, as opposed to the veins of the 【111†systemic circulation】 which carry deoxygenated blood. By definition, a 【92†vein】 is a blood vessel that carries blood to the heart, whether oxygenated or deoxygenated.
L187: A groundbreaking study published in 1998 identified the pulmonary vein as the predominant trigger for 【112†atrial fibrillation】.^{【113†[3]】} Atrial fibrillation frequently results from bursts of 【114†tachycardia】 that originate in muscle bundles extending from the 【115†atrium】 to the pulmonary veins.^{【116†[4]】} Pulmonary vein anatomy is highly variable among atrial fibrillation patients.^{【117†[5]】} Pulmonary vein isolation by 【118†transcatheter ablation】 can restore 【119†sinus rhythm】.^{【116†[4]】} As atrial fibrillation becomes more persistent, the junction between the pulmonary veins and the 【120†left atrium】 becomes less of an initiator and the left atrium becomes an independent source of arrhythmias.^{【121†[6]】} Pulmonary vein isolation ablation technology has used thermal methods (【122†radiofrequency ablation】 or 【123†cryoablation】), which can damage adjacent tissues, notably the 【124†esophagus】, lung or 【125†phrenic nerve】.^{【126†[7]】} 【127†Electroporation】, however, eliminates the risk of thermal damage.^{【126†[7]】} Atrial fibrillation most often recurs after ablation because of pulmonary vein reconnection.^{【128†[8]】}
L188: On chest X-ray, the diameters of pulmonary veins increases from upper to lower lobes, from 3 mm at the first intercoastal space, to 6 mm just above the diaphragm.^{【129†[9]】}
L189: 
L190: A rare 【130†genetic defect】 of the pulmonary veins can cause them to drain into the pulmonary circulation in whole or in part, this is known as a total 【131†anomalous pulmonary venous connection】 (or drainage), or partial anomalous pulmonary connection, respectively.

L176: 【108†Anatomical terminology】
L177: A pulmonary artery is an 【109†artery】 in the 【110†pulmonary circulation】 that carries deoxygenated 【111†blood】 from the right side of the 【112†heart】 to the 【113†lungs】. The largest pulmonary artery is the main pulmonary artery or pulmonary trunk from the 【112†heart】, and the smallest ones are the 【114†arterioles】, which lead to the 【115†capillaries】 that surround the 【116†pulmonary alveoli】.
L178: ## Structure
L179: 
L180: [【117†edit】]
L181: The pulmonary arteries are 【118†blood vessels】 that carry 【119†systemic venous blood】 from the right ventricle of the heart to the 【115†microcirculation】 of the lungs. Unlike in other organs where arteries supply oxygenated blood, the blood carried by the pulmonary arteries is deoxygenated, as it is venous blood returning to the lungs.
L182: The main pulmonary arteries emerge from the right side of the heart and then split into smaller arteries that progressively divide and become 【114†arterioles】, eventually narrowing into the capillary microcirculation of the lungs where gas exchange occurs.
L183: ### Pulmonary trunk
L184: 
L185: [【120†edit】]
L186: 
L187: 【121†Volume rendering】 of a 【122†high resolution】 【123†CT scan】 of the 【124†thorax】. The anterior thoracic wall, the airways and the pulmonary vessels anterior to the 【125†root of the lung】 have been digitally removed to visualize the different levels of the pulmonary circulation.
L188: In order of blood flow, the pulmonary arteries start as the pulmonary trunk that leaves the fibrous pericardium (【126†parietal pericardium】) of the 【127†ventricular outflow tract】 of 【100†right ventricle】 (also known as 【128†infundibulum or conus arteriosus】.^{【129†[1]】} The outflow track runs superiorly and to the left, posterior to the 【130†pulmonary valve】.^{【129†[1]】} The pulmonary trunk bifurcates into right and left pulmonary arteries below the 【131†arch of aorta】 and in front of the left main bronchus.^{【129†[1]】} Pulmonary trunk is short and wide – approximately 5 centimetres (2.0 in) in length^{【132†[2]】} and 2 centimetres (0.79 in)-3 centimetres (1.2 in) in diameter.^{【133†[3]】}^{【134†[4]】}
L189: The pulmonary trunk splits into the right and the left main pulmonary artery.^{【135†[5]】} The left main pulmonary artery is shorter than the right,^{【129†[1]】} passes behind and downwards the descending aorta and above the left main bronchus to the root of the left lung.
L190: Above, the left main pulmonary artery is connected to the concavity of the proximal 【136†descending aorta】 by the 【137†ligamentum arteriosum】.^{【132†[2]】} The right pulmonary artery passes across the midline of the body, below the 【138†carina of trachea】, and comes in front of the right main bronchus.^{【129†[1]】}
L191: ### Branches
L192: 
L193: [【139†edit】]
L194: 
L195: At the far end, pulmonary arteries (labelled at the bottom) become capillaries at the 【116†pulmonary alveoli】.
L196: 
L197: The left main pulmonary artery then divides into two lobar arteries, one for each lobe of the left lung.^{【140†[6]】}
L198: At the right 【125†root of the lung】, it bifurcates into artery that supplies the right upper lobe of the lung, in front of the right upper lobe bronchus, and interlobar artery that supplies the right middle and inferior lobes of the lung, running together with bronchus intermedius.^{【129†[1]】}
L199: The right and left main pulmonary (lungs) arteries give off branches that supplies the corresponding 【141†lung lobes】. In such cases it is termed lobar arteries.^{【142†[7]】} The lobar arteries branch into segmental arteries (roughly 1 for each segment).
L200: Segmental arteries run together with segmental bronchi, at the posterolateral surfaces of the bronchi.^{【142†[7]】} These in turn branch into subsegmental pulmonary arteries.^{【142†[7]】} These eventually form intralobular arteries.^{【143†[8]】} The pulmonary arteries supply the alveoli of the lungs. In contrast, 【144†bronchial arteries】, that has different origins, supply the bronchi of the lungs.^{【129†[1]】}
L201: ## Development
L202: 
L203: [【145†edit】]
L204: 
L205: The pulmonary arteries originate from the 【96†truncus arteriosus】 and the sixth 【146†pharyngeal arch】. The truncus arteriosus is a structure that forms during the 【147†development of the heart】 as a successor to the 【148†conus arteriosus】.^{【149†[9]】}^{: 157 }
L206: By the third week of 【150†development】, the 【151†endocardial tubes】 have developed a swelling in the part closest to the heart.
L207: The swelling is known as the 【152†bulbus cordis】 and the upper part of this swelling develops into the 【96†truncus arteriosus】.^{【149†[9]】}^{: 159–160 } The structure is ultimately mesodermal in origin.^{【149†[9]】}^{: 157 } During 【147†development of the heart】, the heart tissues undergo folding, and the truncus arteriosus is exposed to what will eventually be both the left and right ventricles.
L208: As a 【153†septum】 develops between the two ventricles of the heart, two bulges form on either side of the truncus arteriosus. These progressively enlarge until the trunk splits into the 【154†aorta】 and pulmonary arteries.^{【149†[9]】}^{: 176–179 } Failure of these processes can lead to 【155†pulmonary artery agenesis】.
L209: During 【156†early development】, the 【157†ductus arteriosus】 connects the pulmonary trunk and the 【158†aortic arch】, allowing blood to bypass the fetus's 【159†amniotic fluid-filled】 non-functioning lungs.^{【160†[10]】}^{: 791 }Because the fetus develops within the fluid-filled 【161†amniotic sac】, hence it relies on the 【162†placenta】 for respiratory gas exchange rather than the lungs.^{【163†[11]】}
L210: ## Function
L211: 
L212: [【164†edit】]
L213: 
L214: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the 【100†right ventricle】 to the lungs.^{【165†[12]】} The blood here passes through 【166†capillaries】 adjacent to 【116†alveoli】 and becomes 【167†oxygenated】 as part of the process of 【168†respiration】.^{【169†[13]】}
L215: 
L216: In contrast to the pulmonary arteries, the 【144†bronchial arteries】 supply nutrition to the lungs themselves.^{【160†[10]】}^{: 790 }
L217: ### Pressure
L218: 
L219: [【170†edit】]
L220: The pulmonary artery pressure (PA pressure) is a measure of the 【171†blood pressure】 found in the main pulmonary artery. This is measured by inserting a 【172†catheter】 into the main pulmonary artery.^{【173†[14]】} ^{: 190–191 } The mean pressure is typically 9–18 mmHg,^{【174†[15]】} and the 【175†wedge pressure】 measured in the 【176†left atrium】 may be 6–12 mmHg.
L221: The wedge pressure may be elevated in 【177†left heart failure】,^{【173†[14]】}^{: 190–191 } 【178†mitral valve stenosis】, and other conditions, such as 【179†sickle cell disease】.^{【180†[16]】}
L222: ## Clinical significance
L223: 
L224: [【181†edit】]
L225: The pulmonary artery is relevant in a number of clinical states.
L226: 【182†Pulmonary hypertension】 is used to describe an increase in the pressure of the pulmonary artery, and may be defined as a mean pulmonary artery pressure of greater than 25 mmHg.^{【173†[14]】}^{: 720 } A pulmonary artery diameter of more than 29 mm (measured on a 【123†CT scan】) is often used as an indicator for pulmonary hypertension.^{【183†[17]】} In chest X-rays, a diameter of more than 16 mm for the right descending pulmonary artery is also an indicator for pulmonary hypertension.^{【184†[18]】} This may occur as a result of heart problems such as 【185†heart failure】, lung or airway disease such as 【186†COPD】 or 【187†scleroderma】, or thromboembolic disease such as 【188†pulmonary embolism】 or emboli seen in sickle cell anaemia.^{【173†[14]】}^{: 720–721 } Most recently, computational fluid based tools (non-invasive) have been proposed to be at par with the current clinical tests (invasive) of pulmonary hypertension.^{【189†[19]】}
L227: Pulmonary embolism refers to an embolus that lodges in the pulmonary circulation. This may arise from a 【190†deep venous thrombosis】, especially after a period of immobility. A pulmonary embolus is a common cause of death in patients with cancer and stroke.^{【173†[14]】}^{: 720–721 } A large pulmonary embolus that becomes lodged in the bifurcation of the pulmonary trunk with extensions into both the left and right main pulmonary arteries is called a saddle embolus.^{【191†[20]】}
L228: (made in (1883))
L229: 【192†Anatomy】 of the 【193†horse】, with other arteries: 【194†spermatic artery】 (21), next to (posterior) 【195†vena cava】, 【196†venae portae】, 【197†External iliac artery】, and the 【198†mesenteric vessels】, 【199†Internal iliac】 and 【200†renal arteries】 labeled. The pulmonary artery and 【201†pulmonary veins】 are labelled (4) and (5), respectively.
L230: Several animal models have been utilized for investigating pulmonary artery related pathologies. Porcine model of pulmonary artery is the most frequently used and it was recently found that their mechanical properties vary with every subsequent branching.^{【202†[21]】}

L139: 【70†Anatomical terminology】
L140: The common hepatic artery is a short 【71†blood vessel】 that supplies oxygenated 【72†blood】 to the 【73†liver】, 【74†pylorus of the stomach】, 【75†duodenum】, 【76†pancreas】, and 【77†gallbladder】.^{【78†[1]】}
L141: 
L142: It arises from the 【57†celiac artery】^{【78†[1]】} and has the following branches:^{【79†[2]】}
L143: Branch  | Details
L144: --- | ---
L145: 【60†hepatic artery proper】  | supplies the 【77†gallbladder】 via the 【80†cystic artery】 and the 【73†liver】 via the left and right hepatic arteries
L146: 【61†gastroduodenal artery】  | branches into the 【81†right gastroepiploic artery】 and 【82†superior pancreaticoduodenal artery】
L147: 【83†right gastric artery】  | branches to supply the lesser curvature of the stomach inferiorly
