L121: Hepatic artery proper
L122: ---
L123: The hepatic artery proper branches from the 【55†common hepatic artery】.
L124: Inferior surface of the liver. (Entrance for hepatic artery labeled at bottom center.)
L125: Details
L126: ---
L127: Source  | 【55†Common hepatic artery】
L128: Identifiers
L129: ---
L130: 【56†Latin】  | arteria hepatica propria
L131: 【57†TA98】  | 【58†A12.2.12.029†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L132: 【57†TA2】  | 【59†4227†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】
L133: 【60†FMA】  | 【61†14772†bioportal.bioontology.org】
L134: 【62†Anatomical terminology】
L135: The hepatic artery proper (also proper hepatic artery) is the artery that supplies the 【63†liver】 and 【64†gallbladder】. It raises from the 【55†common hepatic artery】, a branch of the 【65†celiac artery】.
L136: 
L137: The HAP accounts for 10% of hepatic blood flow and 30% of its oxygen supply, with the rest provided by the 【66†portal vein】; this double blood supply makes the liver far more resilient to vascular disease than other major organs.^{【67†[1]】}
L138: ## Structure
L139: 
L140: [【68†edit】]
L141: The hepatic artery proper arises from the common hepatic artery and runs alongside the 【66†portal vein】 and the 【69†common bile duct】 to form the 【70†portal triad】. A branch of the common hepatic artery – the 【71†gastroduodenal artery】 – gives off the small 【72†supraduodenal artery】 to the 【73†duodenal bulb】. Then the 【74†right gastric artery】 comes off and runs to the left along the lesser curvature of the stomach to meet the 【75†left gastric artery】, which is a branch of the 【76†celiac trunk】.
L142: It subsequently bifurcates into the right and left hepatic arteries.
L143: ### Variant anatomy
L144: 
L145: [【77†edit】]
L146: 
L147: Of note, the right and left hepatic arteries may demonstrate 【78†variant anatomy】. A misplaced right hepatic artery may arise from the 【79†superior mesenteric artery】 (SMA) and a misplaced left hepatic artery may arise from the 【75†left gastric artery】. The 【80†cystic artery】 generally comes from the right hepatic artery.^{【81†[2]】}
L148: Other variants of right hepatic artery includes: arising directly from the proximal or middle part of common hepatic artery, gastroduodenal artery, superior mesenteric artery, celiac axis, aorta, splenic artery, or left gastric artery instead of arising from proper hepatic artery.^{【82†[3]】}

L138: 【68†Anatomical terminology】
L139: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery (the IPDA) is a branch of the 【59†superior mesenteric artery】. It supplies the head of the 【69†pancreas】, and the ascending and inferior parts of the 【70†duodenum】. Rarely, it may have an 【71†aneurysm】.
L140: ## Structure
L141: 
L142: [【72†edit】]
L143: 
L144: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery is a branch of the 【59†superior mesenteric artery】. This occurs opposite the upper border of the inferior part of the 【70†duodenum】. As soon as it branches, it divides into 【73†anterior and posterior】 branches. These run between the head of the 【69†pancreas】 and the lesser curvature of the duodenum. They then join (【74†anastomose】) with the anterior and posterior branches of the 【75†superior pancreaticoduodenal artery】.^{【76†[1]】}
L145: ### Variation
L146: 
L147: [【77†edit】]
L148: 
L149: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery may branch from the first intestinal branch of the 【59†superior mesenteric artery】 rather than directly from it.
L150: 
L151: ## Function
L152: 
L153: [【78†edit】]
L154: 
L155: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery distributes branches to the head of the 【69†pancreas】 and to the ascending and inferior parts of the 【70†duodenum】.^{【76†[1]】}^{【79†[2]】}
L156: 
L157: ## Clinical significance
L158: 
L159: [【80†edit】]
L160: ### Aneurysm
L161: 
L162: [【81†edit】]
L163: Very rarely, the inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery may have an 【71†aneurysm】.^{【82†[3]】} It may be caused by certain 【83†medical interventions】, 【84†major trauma】, 【85†pancreatitis】, 【86†cholecystitis】, and 【87†vasculitis】 and other 【88†infections】.^{【82†[3]】} A ruptured aneurysm causes 【89†abdominal pain】, and 【90†haemorrhage】 leads to 【91†hypotension】.^{【82†[3]】} It may be treated with 【92†open abdominal surgery】.^{【82†[3]】} It may also be treated with 【93†endovascular surgery】, such as a coil.^{【82†[3]】}^{【94†[4]】} These aneurysms represent around 2% of aneurysms in visceral arteries of the 【95†abdomen】.^{【94†[4]】}^{【96†[5]】} 【97†Pseudoaneurysm】 may also occur.^{【98†[6]】}
L164: ## History
L165: 
L166: [【99†edit】]
L167: 
L168: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery may be more simply known by the 【100†acronym】 IPDA.^{【82†[3]】}

L131: 【58†Anatomical terminology】
L132: The superior pancreaticoduodenal artery is an 【59†artery】 that supplies 【60†blood】 to the 【53†duodenum】 and 【54†pancreas】.
L133: ## Structure
L134: 
L135: [【61†edit】]
L136: 
L137: It is a branch of the 【50†gastroduodenal artery】, which most commonly arises from the 【62†common hepatic artery】 of the 【63†celiac trunk】, although there are numerous variations of the origin of the gastroduodenal artery.^{【64†[1]】}
L138: The pancreaticoduodenal artery divides into two branches as it descends, an 【65†anterior and posterior】 branch. These branches then travel around the head of the pancreas and duodenum, eventually joining with the anterior and posterior branches of the 【66†inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery】.
L139: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery is a branch of the 【67†superior mesenteric artery】.^{【68†[2]】} These arteries, together with the 【69†pancreatic branches】 of the 【70†splenic artery】, form connections or 【71†anastomoses】 with one another, allowing blood to perfuse the pancreas and duodenum through multiple channels.
L140: ### Distribution
L141: 
L142: [【72†edit】]
L143: 
L144: The artery supplies the anterior and posterior sides of the duodenum and head of 【54†pancreas】, with the anterior branch supply the anterior surface and similarly for the posterior.
L145: 
L146: The artery supplies the part of the duodenum proximal to the level of the 【73†major duodenal papilla】 of the descending part of the duodenum.^{【74†[3]】}

L127: The appendicular artery, also known as the appendiceal artery, commonly arises from the terminal branch of the 【46†ileocolic artery】, or less commonly from the 【56†posterior cecal artery】 or an 【57†ileal artery】.^{【58†[1]】}^{【59†[2]】} It descends behind the termination of the 【60†ileum】 and enters the 【61†mesoappendix】 of the 【45†vermiform appendix】. It runs near the free margin of the mesoappendix and ends in branches which supply the 【62†appendix】.

L147: Aortic arch
L148: ---
L149: The aortic arch has three branches, the 【79†brachiocephalic trunk】, left 【80†common carotid artery】, and left 【81†subclavian artery】.
L150: The aortic arch and its branches shown 【82†in situ】.
L151: Details
L152: ---
L153: 【83†Precursor】  | 【78†Fourth left pharyngeal arch artery】
L154: Source  | 【84†Ascending aorta】
L155: Branches  |
L156:   * 【85†Brachiocephalic trunk】
L157:   * 【80†Left common carotid artery】
L158:   * 【81†Left subclavian artery】
L159: Continues as 【86†descending aorta】, 【87†thoracic part】
L160: 【88†Vein】  | Combination of 【89†superior】 and 【90†inferior】 vena cava
L161: Supplies  | From its branches, the upper body, 【91†arms】, 【92†head】 and 【93†neck】. As a part of the 【94†aorta】, the entire body, with exception of the respiratory zone of the 【95†lung】 and the 【96†heart】.
L162: Identifiers
L163: ---

L168: 【103†Anatomical terminology】
L169: The aortic arch, arch of the aorta, or transverse aortic arch (English: 【104†/eɪˈɔːrtɪk/】^{【105†[1]】}^{【106†[2]】}) is the part of the 【94†aorta】 between the 【84†ascending】 and 【86†descending aorta】. The arch travels backward, so that it ultimately runs to the left of the 【107†trachea】.
L170: ## Structure
L171: 
L172: [【108†edit】]
L173: The aorta begins at the level of the upper border of the second/third 【109†sternocostal articulation】 of the right side, behind the 【110†ventricular outflow tract】 and 【111†pulmonary trunk】. The right 【112†atrial appendage】 overlaps it.
L174: The first few centimeters of the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk lies in the same 【113†pericardial sheath】 and runs at first upward, arches over the 【111†pulmonary trunk】, 【114†right pulmonary artery】, and 【115†right main bronchus】 to lie behind the right second 【116†costal cartilage】. The right lung and sternum lies anterior to the aorta at this point.
L175: The aorta then passes posteriorly and to the left, anterior to the trachea, and arches over 【117†left main bronchus】 and 【118†left pulmonary artery】, and reaches to the left side of the T4 vertebral body.^{【119†[3]】}^{【120†[4]】} Apart from T4 vertebral body, other structures such as trachea, oesophagus, and 【121†thoracic duct】 (from front to back) also lies to the left of the aorta.^{【119†[3]】} Inferiorly, the arch of aorta is connected to 【122†ligamentum arteriosum】 while superiorly, it gives rise to three main branches.^{【119†[3]】} The arch of aorta continues as the 【86†descending aorta】 after T4 vertebral body.^{【123†[5]】}^{: 214 }^{【124†[6]】}
L176: The aortic arch has three main branches on its superior aspect. The first, and largest, branch of the arch of the aorta is the 【79†brachiocephalic trunk】, which is to the right and slightly anterior to the other two branches and originates behind the manubrium of the sternum. Next, the 【125†left common carotid artery】 originates from the aortic arch to the left of the brachiocephalic trunk, then ascends along the left side of the trachea and through the superior mediastinum.

L157: 【102†Anatomical terminology】
L158: The ascending aorta (AAo)^{【103†[1]】} is a portion of the 【104†aorta】 commencing at the upper part of the base of the 【87†left ventricle】, on a level with the lower border of the third costal cartilage behind the left half of the 【105†sternum】.
L159: ## Structure
L160: 
L161: [【106†edit】]
L162: 
L163: It passes obliquely upward, forward, and to the right, in the direction of the heart's axis, as high as the upper border of the second right 【107†costal cartilage】, describing a slight curve in its course, and being situated, about 6 centimetres (2.4 in) behind the posterior surface of the 【105†sternum】. The total length is about 5 centimetres (2.0 in).
L164: ### Components
L165: 
L166: [【108†edit】]
L167: 
L168: The aortic root is the portion of the aorta beginning at the aortic annulus and extending to the sinotubular junction. It is sometimes regarded as a part of the ascending aorta,^{【109†[2]】} and sometimes regarded as a separate entity from the rest of the ascending aorta.^{【110†[3]】}
L169: 
L170: Between each commissure of the 【111†aortic valve】 and opposite the cusps of the aortic valve, three small dilations called the 【112†sinuses of Valsalva】.
L171: The sinotubular junction is the point in the ascending aorta where the sinuses of Valsalva end and the aorta becomes a tubular structure.
L172: ### Size
L173: 
L174: [【113†edit】]
L175: 
L176: A 【114†thoracic aorta】 diameter greater than 3.5 cm is generally considered dilated, whereas a diameter greater than 4.5 cm is generally considered to be a 【115†thoracic aortic aneurysm】.^{【116†[4]】} Still, the average diameter in the population varies by for example age and sex. The upper limit of 【117†standard reference range】 of the ascending aorta may be up to 4.3 cm among large, elderly individuals.^{【118†[5]】}
L177: ## Relations
L178: 
L179: [【119†edit】]
L180: 
L181: At the union of the ascending aorta with the 【82†aortic arch】 the caliber of the vessel is increased, owing to a bulging of its right wall.

L147: 【79†Anatomical terminology】
L148: The azygos vein (from 【80†Ancient Greek】 ἄζυγος (ázugos), meaning 'unwedded' or 'unpaired') is a vein running up the right side of the thoracic 【81†vertebral column】 draining itself towards the 【65†superior vena cava】. It connects the systems of superior 【82†vena cava】 and inferior vena cava and can provide an alternative path for blood to the 【83†right atrium】 when either of the venae cavae is blocked.^{【84†[2]】}^{【85†[3]】}
L149: ## Structure
L150: 
L151: [【86†edit】]
L152: 
L153: The azygos vein transports deoxygenated blood from the posterior walls of the 【87†thorax】 and 【88†abdomen】 into the 【65†superior vena cava】.
L154: It is formed by the union of the 【89†ascending lumbar veins】 with the right 【90†subcostal veins】 at the level of the 12th thoracic vertebra, ascending to the right of the 【91†descending aorta】 and 【92†thoracic duct】, passing behind the right crus of diaphragm, anterior to the vertebral bodies of T12 to T5 and right posterior 【93†intercostal arteries】. At the level of T4 vertebrae, it arches over the root of the right 【94†lung】 from behind to the front to join the superior vena cava.
L155: The trachea and oesophagus is located medially to the arch of the azygous vein.^{【95†[4]】}^{【96†[5]】}
L156: The "arch of the azygos vein" (arcus vena azygos) is an important anatomic landmark. As an anatomical variation in 1–2% of the population, the arch can be displaced laterally, thereby creating a 【97†pleural】 septum separating an 【98†azygos lobe】 from the upper lobe of the right lung.
L157: The origin and anatomical course of the azygos vein are quite variable. Usually, there is a singular azygos vein on the right side of the body. However, the azygos vein is occasionally located in the midline or two independent veins may be present like in early embryonic development. In some rare variations, for example, it also drains thoracic veins, bronchial veins, and even gonadal veins. The vein is so named because it has no symmetrically equivalent 【99†vein】 on the left side of the body.
L158: Structure and location of azygos vein
L159: ### Development
L160: 
L161: [【100†edit】]
L162: 
L163: It has been proposed that the azygos vein develops by originally draining to the posterior cardinal vein and then to the longitudinal venous channel. Following retrogression of the left common cardinal vein, the left azygos vein loses contact with the posterior cardinal vein. Thus, the blood drains into the right azygos line.^{【101†[6]】}
L164: ### Tributaries
L165: 
L166: [【102†edit】]
L167: Major tributaries are the 【103†hemiazygos vein】 and 【104†accessory hemiazygos vein】, draining into the azygous vein at the midthoracic level. These two veins are located at the opposite side of the vertebral column. The azygous vein also receives drainage from all the 【105†intercostal veins】 on the right, except for 【106†supreme intercostal vein】 (first intercostal vein).

L162: 【96†Anatomical terminology】
L163: The brachiocephalic artery, brachiocephalic trunk, or innominate artery is an 【97†artery】 of the 【98†mediastinum】 that supplies blood to the right 【99†arm】, 【100†head】, and 【101†neck】.^{【102†[1]】}^{【103†[2]】}
L164: 
L165: It is the first branch of the 【82†aortic arch】.^{【104†[3]】} Soon after it emerges, the brachiocephalic artery divides into the right 【83†common carotid artery】 and the right 【84†subclavian artery】.^{【105†[4]】}
L166: There is no brachiocephalic artery for the left side of the body. The left common carotid artery and the left subclavian artery come directly off the aortic arch. Despite this, there are two 【87†brachiocephalic veins】.^{【106†[5]】}
L167: ## Structure
L168: 
L169: [【107†edit】]
L170: The brachiocephalic artery arises on a level with the upper border of the second right 【108†costal cartilage】 from the start of the 【82†aortic arch】^{【104†[3]】} on a plane anterior to the origin of the left 【109†carotid artery】. It ascends obliquely upward, backward, and to the right to the level of the upper border of the right sternoclavicular articulation, where it divides into the right 【83†common carotid artery】 and right 【84†subclavian arteries】.
L171: The artery then crosses the 【110†trachea】 in front of it obliquely from the left to the right, roughly at the middle of the trachea or the level of the ninth 【111†tracheal cartilage】.
L172: ### Relations
L173: 
L174: [【112†edit】]
L175: 
L176: The brachiocephalic artery has relation with:^{【113†[6]】}
L177: 
L178:   * anterior - left 【87†brachiocephalic vein】 and thymus
L179:   * posterior - trachea
L180:   * right - 【114†superior vena cava】, right brachiocephalic vein, and 【115†pleura】
L181:   * left - left common carotid artery and thymus
L182: 
L183: The 【116†thymus】 typically sits atop the brachiocephalic artery, and it separates the artery from the posterior surface of the 【117†manubrium】 of 【118†sternum】.^{【105†[4]】}
L184: ### Branches
L185: 
L186: [【119†edit】]
L187: 
L188: The 【85†thyroid ima artery】 ascends in front of the trachea to the lower part of the 【120†thyroid】, which it supplies.
L189: ### Variation
L190: 
L191: [【121†edit】]
L192: 
L193: The innominate artery usually gives off no branches, but occasionally a small branch, the thyroid ima artery, arises from it. Other times, it gives off a thymic or bronchial branch.
L194: 
L195: Thyroid ima artery varies greatly in size, and appears to compensate for deficiency or absence of one of the other thyroid vessels. It occasionally arises from the 【122†aorta】, the 【123†right common carotid】, the 【84†subclavian】 or the 【124†internal mammary】.
L196: ## Development
L197: 
L198: [【125†edit】]
L199: The 【81†aortic sac】 is the embryological precursor of the proximal portion of the aortic arch. It is chronologically the first portion of the aorta to form, and appears as a dilation superior to the 【126†truncus arteriosus】. Between the two horns of aortic sac, right horn gives rise to the brachiocephalic artery.
L200: Then the right horn fuses with the right-sided third and fourth 【127†aortic arches】, which give rise to the right common carotid artery and the proximal right subclavian artery respectively.^{【105†[4]】} Eventually, brachiocephalic artery is derived from 【128†ventral aorta】, same as 【129†ascending aorta】. Left horn forms proximal ascending portion of aorta.^{【130†[7]】}

L156: 【90†Anatomical terminology】
L157: The celiac (【91†/ˈsiːli.æk/】) artery (also spelled coeliac in 【92†British English】), also known as the celiac trunk, Haller's tripod or truncus coeliacus, is the first major branch of the 【78†abdominal aorta】. It is about 1.27 cm (half an inch) in length. Branching from the aorta at the level of the T12-L1 【93†intervertebral disc】 in typical anatomy, it is one of three anterior/midline branches of the abdominal aorta (the others are the 【94†superior】 and 【95†inferior mesenteric arteries】).
L158: ## Structure
L159: 
L160: [【96†edit】]
L161: 
L162: The celiac artery is the first major branch of the descending 【78†abdominal aorta】, branching at a 90° 【97†angle】.^{【98†[1]】}^{【99†[2]】} This occurs just below the 【100†crus of the diaphragm】.^{【99†[2]】} In typical anatomy, this is at the T12-L1 vertebral level.^{【101†[3]】}
L163: 
L164: There are three main divisions of the celiac artery, and each in turn has its own named branches:
L165: Artery  | Branches
L166: --- | ---
L167: 【79†left gastric artery】^{【99†[2]】}  | esophageal branch, stomach branch
L168: 【80†common hepatic artery】^{【99†[2]】}  | 【102†proper hepatic artery】, 【103†right gastric artery】, 【104†gastroduodenal artery】
L169: 【81†splenic artery】^{【99†[2]】}  | 【105†dorsal pancreatic artery】, 【106†short gastric arteries】, 【107†left gastro-omental artery】, 【108†greater pancreatic artery】
L170: 
L171: The celiac artery may also give rise to the 【109†inferior phrenic arteries】.
L172: ## Function
L173: 
L174: [【110†edit】]
L175: The celiac artery supplies oxygenated 【111†blood】 to the 【112†liver】, 【113†stomach】, abdominal 【114†esophagus】, 【115†spleen】, and the superior half of both the 【116†duodenum】 and the 【117†pancreas】.^{【99†[2]】} These structures correspond to the embryonic 【118†foregut】. (Similarly, the 【94†superior mesenteric artery】 and 【95†inferior mesenteric artery】 feed structures arising from the embryonic 【119†midgut】 and 【120†hindgut】 respectively.
L176: Note that these three anterior branches of the abdominal aorta are distinct and cannot substitute for one another, although there are limited connections between their terminal branches.)
L177: The celiac artery is an essential source of blood, since the interconnections with the other major arteries of the gut are not sufficient to sustain adequate 【121†perfusion】. Thus it cannot be safely ligated in a living person, and obstruction of the celiac artery will lead to 【122†necrosis】 of the structures it supplies.
L178: ### Drainage
L179: 
L180: [【123†edit】]
L181: 
L182: The celiac artery is the only major 【124†artery】 that nourishes the abdominal 【125†digestive organs】 that does not have a similarly named vein.
L183: 
L184: Most blood returning from the digestive organs (including from the area of distribution of the celiac artery) is diverted to the liver via the 【126†portal venous system】 for further processing and detoxification in the liver before returning to the 【127†systemic circulation】 via the 【128†hepatic veins】.
L185: In contrast to the drainage of midgut and hindgut structures by the 【129†superior mesenteric vein】 and 【130†inferior mesenteric vein】 respectively, venous return from the celiac artery is through either the 【131†splenic vein】 emptying into the 【132†hepatic portal vein】 or via smaller tributaries of the portal venous system.
L186: ## Clinical significance
L187: 
L188: [【133†edit】]
L189: 
L190: 【134†Aneurysms】 in the celiac artery account for around 4% of visceral artery aneurysms.^{【135†[4]】}^{【136†[5]】} This may cause 【137†abdominal pain】.^{【136†[5]】}

L124: In 【57†human anatomy】, the descending aorta is part of the 【58†aorta】, the largest artery, situated in the chest. It is the continued portion of the aorta immediately following the aortic arch.

L126: ---

L129: Details

L142: 【70†Anatomical terminology】
L143: The descending aorta begins at the 【71†aortic arch】 and runs down through the 【72†chest】 and 【73†abdomen】. The descending aorta anatomically consists of two portions or segments, the 【59†thoracic】 and the 【63†abdominal】 aorta, in correspondence with the two great cavities of the trunk in which it is situated. Within the abdomen, the descending aorta branches into the two 【74†common iliac arteries】 which serve the 【75†pelvis】 and, eventually, the legs.
L144: The 【76†ductus arteriosus】 connects to the junction between the 【77†pulmonary artery】 and the descending aorta in 【78†foetal life】. This artery later regresses as the 【79†ligamentum arteriosum】.^{【80†[1]】}^{【81†[2]】}
L145: ## Structure
L146: 
L147: [【82†edit】]
L148: 
L149: Main article: 【58†Aorta】
L150: 
L151: The descending aorta is made up of multiple parts that extend from the chest to the abdomen. The specific name changes depending on location. The descending thoracic aorta becomes the descending abdominal aorta once it reaches the diaphragm. It is preceded by the 【62†ascending aorta】.
L152: The descending aorta is composed of three layers. The inner layers is the 【83†tunica intima】 which regulates blood pressure. The middle layers is the media, which moves blood in one direction. The outer layer is the 【84†adventitia】 which provides structure and support.^{【85†[3]】}
L153: 
L154: The diameter of the descending aorta varies largely based on sex and age.
L155: ## Function
L156: 
L157: [【86†edit】]
L158: 
L159: The anatomical segments of the aorta.
L160: 
L161: The 【58†aorta】 transports oxygenated 【87†blood】 from the 【88†heart】 to the entire body.^{【89†[4]】} As the aorta descends down the body, it branches into smaller arteries. The descending thoracic aorta branches into the following (descending order)
L162: 
L163:   * 【90†Bronchial arteries】
L164:   * 【91†Esophageal arteries】
L165:   * Mediastinal arteries
L166:   * 【92†Pericardial arteries】
L167:   * 【93†Superior phrenic arteries】
L168: The branches of the descending abdominal aorta include (descending order)
L169: 
L170:   * 【94†Inferior phrenic arteries】
L171:   * Celiac trunk arteries
L172:   * 【95†Superior mesenteric arteries】
L173:   * 【96†Middle suprarenal arteries】
L174:   * 【97†Renal arteries】
L175:   * 【98†Gonadal arteries】
L176:   * 【99†Lumbar arteries】
L177:   * 【100†Inferior mesenteric arteries】
L178:   * 【101†Median sacral arteries】
L179:   * 【74†Common iliac arteries】
L180: ## Clinical significance
L181: 
L182: [【102†edit】]
L183: Aortic aneurysms are the most common condition of the descending aorta. Aortic aneurysms are a bulge or swelling of the aorta due to a weak spot. A 【103†thoracic aortic aneurysm】 (TAA) is an aortic aneurysm occurring in the upper part of the descending aorta. An 【104†abdominal aortic aneurysm】 (AAA) is the most common kind of aortic aneurysm, occurring in the descending abdominal aorta.
L184: A 【105†thoracoabdominal aneurysm】 (TAAA) is an aneurysm that extends from the descending thoracic aorta to the descending abdominal aorta.^{【85†[3]】}
L185: Another serious condition that can occur in the descending aorta is an 【106†aortic dissection】, specifically type B aortic dissection.^{【107†[5]】} A type B dissection involves a tear in the 【83†tunica intima】 along the descending aorta either in the chest or the abdominal region.
L186: A pre-existing aneurysm, such as one described above, can contribute to the risk of developing type B aortic dissection.^{【107†[5]】} Among patients who develop uncomplicated type B aortic dissection, the maximum initial total descending aorta diameter can predict the likelihood of patients experiencing adverse events later in life or even mortality.^{【108†[6]】}^{【109†[7]】} Patients with total diameter of ≥40 mm would have higher risk than those with lower diameter.^{【109†[7]】}

L126: The dorsal pancreatic artery is a branch of the 【44†splenic artery】. It anastomoses with the 【53†superior pancreaticoduodenal artery】 and continues as the inferior pancreatic artery on its lower border.^{【54†[1]】}
L127: ## Anatomy
L128: 
L129: [【55†edit】]
L130: 
L131: The dorsal pancreatic artery is a short artery that issues numerous branches. Its course and length depends upon its (variable) origin.^{【56†[2]】}
L132: 
L133: ### Origin
L134: 
L135: [【57†edit】]
L136: 
L137: The dorsal pancreatic artery usually arises from the proximal 2 cm (0.79 in) of the 【44†splenic artery】. It may also arise from the 【58†common hepatic artery】, 【59†superior mesenteric artery】, or 【60†coeliac trunck】.^{【56†[2]】}
L138: ### Fate
L139: 
L140: [【61†edit】]
L141: 
L142: It consistently terminates near the inferior border of the pancreas, near to the origin of the 【62†portal vein】.^{【56†[2]】}

L126: 【53†Anatomical terminology】
L127: In 【54†human anatomy】, the greater pancreatic artery (great pancreatic artery or arteria pancreatica magna), is the largest 【55†artery】 that supplies the 【56†pancreas】. It arises from the 【46†splenic artery】.
L128: ## Clinical relevance
L129: 
L130: [【57†edit】]
L131: 
L132: Rarely, the greater pancreatic artery can rupture as a complication of 【58†chronic pancreatitis】;^{【59†[1]】} this is often fatal.^{【60†[2]】}

L136: 【69†Anatomical terminology】
L137: The hemiazygos vein (vena azygos minor inferior) is a vein running superiorly in the lower thoracic region, just to the left side of the 【70†vertebral column】.
L138: ## Structure
L139: 
L140: [【71†edit】]
L141: The hemiazygos vein and the 【72†accessory hemiazygos vein】, when taken together, essentially serve as the left-sided equivalent of the 【62†azygos vein】.^{【73†[2]】} That is, the azygos vein serves to drain most of the 【74†posterior intercostal veins】 on the right side of the body, and the hemiazygos vein and the accessory hemiazygos vein drain most of the posterior intercostal veins on the left side of the body.^{【73†[2]】} Specifically, the hemiazygos vein mirrors the bottom part of the azygos vein.
L142: The structure of the hemiazygos vein is often variable. It usually begins in the left 【75†ascending lumbar vein】 or 【76†renal vein】, and passes upward through the left 【77†crus of the diaphragm】 to enter the 【78†thorax】. It continues ascending on the left side of the 【70†vertebral column】, and around the level of the ninth 【79†thoracic vertebra】, it passes rightward across the column, behind the 【80†aorta】, 【81†esophagus】, and 【82†thoracic duct】, to end in the 【62†azygos vein】.^{【73†[2]】}^{【83†[3]】}
L143: It receives the 9th, 10th, and 11th 【74†posterior intercostal veins】 and the 【84†subcostal vein】 of the left side, and some esophageal and mediastinal veins.
L144: ### Variations
L145: 
L146: [【85†edit】]
L147: 
L148: The hemiazygos may or may not be continuous superiorly with the 【72†accessory hemiazygos vein】.^{【86†[4]】}
L149: ## Clinical significance
L150: 
L151: [【87†edit】]
L152: The dilated hemiazygos system displayed by chest or abdominal X-ray films can be misdiagnosed as a mediastinal or retroperitoneal neoplasm, lymphadenopathy or aortic dissection (2, 5–7, 10). Venostasis which is the consequence of pathological conditions such as acquired obstruction of the IVC or SVC, the right heart failure, portal hypertension or due to pregnancy can have the same clinical presentation as hemiazygos continuation of the IVC (5, 6, 10, 13).
L153: In the case of hemiazygos continuation of the IVC, the hepatic veins can drain directly into the right atrium (3, 10). An incidental finding of this condition during venous cannulation for cardiopulmonary bypass complicates the procedure, since no solid IVC trunk for placing the cannula is present. Separate cannulation of the SVC and the right atrium should be used in this case.^{【88†[5]】}
L154: ## History
L155: 
L156: [【89†edit】]
L157: 
L158: The name for this vein is derived from that of the 【62†azygos vein】. Azygos means 'unpaired', and hemi means half. This vein mirrors the bottom half of the azygos vein.

L132: 【60†Anatomical terminology】
L133: The ileocolic artery is the lowest branch arising from the concavity of the 【50†superior mesenteric artery】. It supplies the cecum, ileum, and appendix.
L134: 
L135: It passes downward and to the right behind the 【61†peritoneum】 toward the right 【62†iliac fossa】, where it divides into a superior and an inferior branch: the inferior gives rise to the 【51†appendicular artery】 and anastomoses with the end of the 【50†superior mesenteric artery】; the superior branch anastomoses with the 【63†right colic artery】.
L136: ## Anatomy
L137: 
L138: [【64†edit】]
L139: ### Branches
L140: 
L141: [【65†edit】]
L142: 
L143: The inferior branch of the ileocolic runs toward the upper border of the 【66†ileocolic junction】 and produces the following branches:
L144:   * 【67†colic branch of ileocolic artery】, which passes upward on the 【68†ascending colon】 - from the posterior branch of the inferior branch of the ileocolic artery
L145:   * ileocecal (some sources acknowledge this division^{【69†[1]】} while others do not)
L146:     * 【70†anterior cecal artery】 and 【71†posterior cecal artery】, which are distributed to the front and back of the 【48†cecum】
L147:     * 【72†ileal branch of ileocolic artery】, which runs upward and to the left on the lower part of the ileum and anastomoses with the termination of the superior mesenteric artery
L148:     * an 【51†appendicular artery】

L173: 【103†Anatomical terminology】
L174: The inferior vena cava is a large vein that carries the deoxygenated 【104†blood】 from the lower and middle body into the 【92†right atrium】 of the 【105†heart】. It is formed by the joining of the right and the left 【86†common iliac veins】, usually at the level of the fifth 【106†lumbar vertebra】.^{【107†[1]】}^{【108†[2]】}
L175: The inferior vena cava is the lower ("【109†inferior】") of the two 【110†venae cavae】, the two large 【111†veins】 that carry deoxygenated 【104†blood】 from the body to the right atrium of the heart: the inferior vena cava carries blood from the lower half of the body whilst the 【112†superior vena cava】 carries blood from the upper half of the body.
L176: Together, the venae cavae (in addition to the 【113†coronary sinus】, which carries blood from the muscle of the heart itself) form the venous counterparts of the 【114†aorta】.
L177: It is a large 【115†retroperitoneal】 vein that lies 【116†posterior】 to the 【117†abdominal cavity】 and runs along the right side of the 【118†vertebral column】.^{【107†[1]】} It enters the right auricle at the lower right, back side of the heart. The name derives from 【119†Latin】: vena, "vein", cavus, "hollow".
L178: ## Structure
L179: 
L180: [【120†edit】]
L181: 
L182: The IVC is formed by the joining of the left and right 【86†common iliac veins】 and brings collected blood into the 【92†right atrium】 of the heart.^{【107†[1]】} It also 【121†joins】 with the 【122†azygos vein】 (which runs on the right side of the vertebral column) and venous 【123†plexuses】 next to the 【124†spinal cord】.
L183: The inferior vena cava begins as the left and right common iliac veins behind the 【125†abdomen】 unite, at about the level of 【126†L5】.^{【107†[1]】}^{【108†[2]】} It passes through the 【127†thoracic diaphragm】 at the 【128†caval opening】 at the level of 【129†T8】.^{【107†[1]】}^{【130†[3]】} It passes to the right of the 【131†descending aorta】.^{【130†[3]】}

L146: 【82†Anatomical terminology】
L147: In 【83†human anatomy】, the inferior mesenteric artery (IMA) is the third main branch of the 【67†abdominal aorta】 and arises at the level of 【84†L3】, supplying the 【85†large intestine】 from the distal 【86†transverse colon】 to the upper part of the 【87†anal canal】. The regions supplied by the IMA are the 【88†descending colon】, the 【62†sigmoid colon】, and part of the 【63†rectum】.^{【89†[1]】}
L148: ## Structure
L149: 
L150: [【90†edit】]
L151: ### Origin
L152: 
L153: [【91†edit】]
L154: 
L155: The IMA arises from the anterior aspect of the 【67†abdominal aorta】.^{【92†[2]】}^{【93†[3]】}
L156: The vertebral level of its origin is situated at L3 (【94†subcostal plane】),^{【92†[2]】}^{【93†[3]】} below the origins of the two 【95†renal arteries】,^{【93†[3]】} 3.8 cm (1 and a half inches) above the 【96†aortic bifurcation】,^{【93†[3]】}^{【92†[2]】} at the level of the 【97†umbilicus】 (【98†transumbilical plane】), and posterior to the inferior border of the horizontal (III) part of the 【99†duodenum】.^{【92†[2]】}
L157: ### Branches
L158: 
L159: [【100†edit】]
L160: 
L161: Along its course, the IMA has the following branches:^{【89†[1]】}^{【101†[4]】}^{【93†[3]】}
L162: 
L163: Branch  | notes
L164: --- | ---
L165: 【68†left colic artery】  | supplies 【88†descending colon】
L166: 【69†sigmoid branches】  | the most superior being described as 'the superior sigmoid artery'
L167: 【70†superior rectal artery】  | effectively the terminal branch of the IMA (the continuation of the IMA after all other branches)
L168: All these arterial branches further divide into 【102†arcades】 which then supply the 【103†colon】 at regular intervals.
L169: ### Relations
L170: 
L171: [【104†edit】]
L172: 
L173: The IMA is accompanied along its course by a similarly named 【71†vein】, the 【72†inferior mesenteric vein】, which drains into the 【105†splenic vein】.^{【89†[1]】} The IMV drains to the 【106†portal vein】 and does therefore not fully mirror the course of the IMA.^{【89†[1]】}^{【101†[4]】}^{【93†[3]】}
L174: ### Distribution
L175: 
L176: [【107†edit】]
L177: Proximally, its territory of distribution overlaps (forms a 【108†watershed】) with the 【109†middle colic artery】, and therefore the 【110†superior mesenteric artery】. The SMA and IMA anastomose via the 【111†marginal artery of the colon】 (artery of Drummond) and via 【112†Riolan's arcade】 (also called the "meandering artery", an arterial connection between the left colic artery and the middle colic artery).

L134: 【67†Anatomical terminology】
L135: In 【68†human anatomy】, the inferior mesenteric vein (IMV) is a 【69†blood vessel】 that drains 【70†blood】 from the 【71†large intestine】. It usually terminates when reaching the 【52†splenic vein】, which goes on to form the 【50†portal vein】 with the 【51†superior mesenteric vein】 (SMV).
L136: ## Structure
L137: 
L138: [【72†edit】]
L139: 
L140: The inferior mesenteric vein merges with the 【52†splenic vein】, posterior to the middle of the body of the 【73†pancreas】.^{【74†[1]】} The splenic vein then merges with the 【51†superior mesenteric vein】 to form the 【50†portal vein】.^{【74†[1]】}
L141: ### Tributaries
L142: 
L143: [【75†edit】]
L144: 
L145: Tributaries of the inferior mesenteric vein drain the 【71†large intestine】, 【76†sigmoid colon】 and 【77†rectum】. These include:
L146: 
L147:   * 【56†left colic vein】
L148:   * 【78†sigmoid veins】
L149:   * 【58†superior rectal vein】
L150:   * rectosigmoid veins
L151: 
L152: ### Variation
L153: 
L154: [【79†edit】]
L155: 
L156: Anatomical variations include the inferior mesenteric vein draining into the confluence of the superior mesenteric vein and splenic vein and the inferior mesenteric vein draining in the superior mesenteric vein.
L157: ## Clinical significance
L158: 
L159: [【80†edit】]
L160: 
L161: The inferior mesenteric vein may be damaged during 【81†surgery】 on the body and tail of the 【73†pancreas】.^{【82†[2]】} If a serious 【83†laceration】 occurs, the inferior mesenteric vein may be 【84†ligated】, as other veins can drain the 【71†large intestine】.^{【82†[2]】}

L139: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery (the IPDA) is a branch of the 【59†superior mesenteric artery】. It supplies the head of the 【69†pancreas】, and the ascending and inferior parts of the 【70†duodenum】. Rarely, it may have an 【71†aneurysm】.
L140: ## Structure
L141: 
L142: [【72†edit】]
L143: 
L144: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery is a branch of the 【59†superior mesenteric artery】. This occurs opposite the upper border of the inferior part of the 【70†duodenum】. As soon as it branches, it divides into 【73†anterior and posterior】 branches. These run between the head of the 【69†pancreas】 and the lesser curvature of the duodenum. They then join (【74†anastomose】) with the anterior and posterior branches of the 【75†superior pancreaticoduodenal artery】.^{【76†[1]】}
L145: ### Variation
L146: 
L147: [【77†edit】]
L148: 
L149: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery may branch from the first intestinal branch of the 【59†superior mesenteric artery】 rather than directly from it.
L150: 
L151: ## Function
L152: 
L153: [【78†edit】]
L154: 
L155: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery distributes branches to the head of the 【69†pancreas】 and to the ascending and inferior parts of the 【70†duodenum】.^{【76†[1]】}^{【79†[2]】}
L156: 
L157: ## Clinical significance
L158: 
L159: [【80†edit】]
L160: ### Aneurysm
L161: 
L162: [【81†edit】]
L163: Very rarely, the inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery may have an 【71†aneurysm】.^{【82†[3]】} It may be caused by certain 【83†medical interventions】, 【84†major trauma】, 【85†pancreatitis】, 【86†cholecystitis】, and 【87†vasculitis】 and other 【88†infections】.^{【82†[3]】} A ruptured aneurysm causes 【89†abdominal pain】, and 【90†haemorrhage】 leads to 【91†hypotension】.^{【82†[3]】} It may be treated with 【92†open abdominal surgery】.^{【82†[3]】} It may also be treated with 【93†endovascular surgery】, such as a coil.^{【82†[3]】}^{【94†[4]】} These aneurysms represent around 2% of aneurysms in visceral arteries of the 【95†abdomen】.^{【94†[4]】}^{【96†[5]】} 【97†Pseudoaneurysm】 may also occur.^{【98†[6]】}
L164: ## History
L165: 
L166: [【99†edit】]
L167: 
L168: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery may be more simply known by the 【100†acronym】 IPDA.^{【82†[3]】}

L150: 【81†Anatomical terminology】
L151: The common iliac artery is a large 【82†artery】 of the abdomen paired on each side. It originates from the 【83†aortic bifurcation】 at the level of the 4th 【84†lumbar vertebra】. It ends in front of the 【85†sacroiliac joint】, one on either side, and each bifurcates into the 【71†external】 and 【86†internal iliac arteries】.
L152: ## Structure
L153: 
L154: [【87†edit】]
L155: 
L156: The common iliac artery are about 4 cm long in adults and more than a centimeter in diameter. It begins as a branch of the 【88†aorta】.^{【89†[1]】} This is at the level of the fourth 【90†lumbar vertebra】.^{【89†[1]】} It runs inferolaterally, along the medial border of the 【91†psoas muscles】. It bifurcates into the 【71†external iliac artery】 and the 【72†internal iliac artery】 at the 【92†pelvic brim】, in front of the 【85†sacroiliac joints】.^{【89†[1]】}
L157: The common iliac artery, and all of its branches, exist as paired structures (that is to say, there is one on the left side and one on the right).
L158: 
L159: The distribution of the common iliac artery is basically the 【93†pelvis】 and 【94†lower limb】 (as the 【95†femoral artery】) on the corresponding side.
L160: ### Relations
L161: 
L162: [【96†edit】]
L163: 
L164: Both common iliac arteries are accompanied along their course by the two 【74†common iliac veins】, which lie posteriorly and to the right. Their terminal bifurcation is crossed anteriorly by the 【97†ureters】.^{【89†[1]】} This is significant, as the bifurcation of the common iliac artery is the second point of ureteric constriction.^{【89†[1]】}
L165: 
L166: ## Function
L167: 
L168: [【98†edit】]
L169: 
L170: The common iliac artery supplies the leg and the pelvic region.
L171: 
L172: ## Clinical significance
L173: 
L174: [【99†edit】]
L175: ### Constriction
L176: 
L177: [【100†edit】]
L178: 
L179: The common iliac artery may become narrowed.^{【101†[2]】} This is most common at the 【83†aortic bifurcation】.^{【101†[2]】}
L180: 
L181: ### Dilatation
L182: 
L183: [【102†edit】]
L184: 
L185: Dilatation of the common iliac artery can be graded into the following categories:^{【103†[3]】}
L186: 
L187: Normal  | Diameter ≤ 12 mm
L188: 【104†Ectasia】  | Diameter 12 to 18 mm
L189: 【105†Aneurysm】  | Diameter ≥ 18 mm

L133: 【69†Anatomical terminology】
L134: In 【70†human anatomy】, the common iliac veins are formed by the 【53†external iliac veins】 and 【54†internal iliac veins】. The left and right common iliac veins come together in the 【50†abdomen】 at the level of the 【71†fifth lumbar vertebra】,^{【72†[1]】} forming the 【52†inferior vena cava】. They drain 【73†blood】 from the 【58†pelvis】 and lower limbs.
L135: 
L136: Both common iliac veins are accompanied along their course by 【60†common iliac arteries】.
L137: ## Structure
L138: 
L139: [【74†edit】]
L140: 
L141: The 【53†external iliac vein】 and 【54†internal iliac vein】 unite in front of the sacroiliac joint to form the common iliac veins.^{【75†[2]】} Both common iliac veins ascend to form the inferior vena cava behind the right common iliac artery at the level of the fifth lumbar vertebra.^{【76†[3]】}
L142: The vena cava is to the right of the midline and therefore the left common iliac vein is longer than the right.^{【75†[2]】} The left common iliac vein occasionally travels upwards to the left of the 【56†aorta】 to the level of the 【77†kidney】, where it receives the left 【78†renal vein】 and crosses in front of the aorta to join the inferior vena cava.^{【79†[4]】} The right common iliac vein is virtually vertical and lies behind and then lateral to its artery.
L143: Each common iliac vein receives 【80†iliolumbar veins】, while the left also receives the 【81†median sacral vein】 which lies on the right of the corresponding artery.^{【75†[2]】}
L144: ## Clinical significance
L145: 
L146: [【82†edit】]
L147: 
L148: Overlying arterial structures may cause compression of the upper part of the left common iliac vein.^{【76†[3]】}
L149: 
L150: Compression of the left common iliac vein against the fifth lumbar vertebral body by the right common iliac artery as the artery crosses in front of it traditionally happens in 【83†May–Thurner syndrome】.^{【84†[5]】}
L151: Continuous 【85†pulsation】 of the common iliac artery may trigger an 【86†inflammatory response】 within the common iliac vein. The resulting intraluminal 【87†elastin】 and 【88†collagen】 deposition can cause intimal 【89†fibrosis】 and the formation of venous spurs and webs. This can lead to narrowing of the vein and cause persistent unilateral leg swelling, contributing to 【90†venous thromboembolism】.^{【84†[5]】}

L141: 【73†Anatomical terminology】
L142: The external iliac arteries are two major 【74†arteries】 which bifurcate off the 【75†common iliac arteries】 anterior to the 【76†sacroiliac joint】 of the 【77†pelvis】.
L143: ## Structure
L144: 
L145: [【78†edit】]
L146: The external iliac artery arises from the bifurcation of the 【60†common iliac artery】. They proceed anterior and inferior along the medial border of the 【79†psoas major muscles】. They exit the 【77†pelvic girdle】 posterior and inferior to the 【80†inguinal ligament】.^{【81†[1]】}^{【82†[2]】} This occurs about one third laterally from the insertion point of the inguinal ligament on the 【83†pubic tubercle】.^{【81†[1]】} At this point they are referred to as the 【84†femoral arteries】.^{【81†[1]】}^{【85†[3]】}

L156: ## Function
L157: 
L158: [【91†edit】]
L159: 
L160: The external iliac artery provides the main blood supply to the legs. It passes down along the brim of the pelvis and gives off two large branches - the "inferior epigastric artery" and a "deep circumflex artery." These vessels supply blood to the muscles and skin in the lower abdominal wall. The external iliac artery passes beneath the inguinal ligament in the lower part of the abdomen and becomes the femoral artery.
L161: ## Clinical significance
L162: 
L163: [【92†edit】]
L164: 
L165: The external iliac artery is usually the artery used to attach the renal artery to the recipient of a kidney transplant.

L130: 【62†Anatomical terminology】
L131: The inferior suprarenal artery is a paired artery that supplies the 【55†adrenal gland】. It usually originates at the trunk of the 【52†renal artery】 before its terminal division, but with many common variations. It supplies the 【55†adrenal gland】 【63†parenchyma】, the 【64†ureter】, and the surrounding cellular tissue and muscles.
L132: ## Structure
L133: 
L134: [【65†edit】]
L135: 
L136: The inferior suprarenal artery usually originates at the trunk of the 【52†renal artery】.^{【66†[1]】}^{【67†[2]】} This is usually on its superior surface before its terminal division.^{【66†[1]】} It enters the 【63†parenchyma】 of the 【55†adrenal gland】.^{【66†[1]】}
L137: ### Variations
L138: 
L139: [【68†edit】]
L140: 
L141: Variations in the inferior suprarenal artery are common.^{【66†[1]】}^{【69†[3]】} It usually originates from the 【52†renal artery】 before its final divisions, but may also originate as a final division or after the final divisions.^{【66†[1]】} More rarely, it may originate directly from the 【70†aorta】.^{【66†[1]】} It may give off a small branch to the 【51†kidney】.^{【66†[1]】}
L142: There may be two or three inferior suprarenal arteries in some people.^{【66†[1]】} Its diameter changes significantly with age.^{【71†[4]】}
L143: ## Function
L144: 
L145: [【72†edit】]
L146: 
L147: The inferior suprarenal artery supplies the 【55†adrenal gland】 (suprarenal gland).^{【66†[1]】} They also supply the 【64†ureter】 and some surrounding tissue and 【73†skeletal muscle】.
L148: 
L149: ## Clinical significance
L150: 
L151: [【74†edit】]
L152: 
L153: The inferior suprarenal artery may be affected by an 【75†aneurysm】.^{【76†[5]】} It may be assessed using 【77†Doppler ultrasound】.^{【78†[6]】}
L154: 
L155: ## History
L156: 
L157: [【79†edit】]
L158: 
L159: The inferior suprarenal artery may also be known as the inferior adrenal artery.^{【78†[6]】}

L147: 【89†Anatomical terminology】
L148: The internal iliac artery (formerly known as the hypogastric artery) is the main 【90†artery】 of the 【91†pelvis】.
L149: ## Structure
L150: 
L151: [【92†edit】]
L152: 
L153: The internal iliac artery supplies the walls and 【93†viscera】 of the 【91†pelvis】, the 【94†buttock】, the 【95†reproductive organs】, and the 【96†medial compartment of the thigh】. The vesicular branches of the internal iliac arteries supply the bladder.^{【97†[1]】}
L154: 
L155: It is a short, thick vessel, smaller than the 【98†external iliac artery】, and about 3 to 4 cm in length.
L156: ### Course
L157: 
L158: [【99†edit】]
L159: 
L160: The internal iliac artery arises at the bifurcation of the 【66†common iliac artery】, opposite the lumbosacral articulation, and, passing downward to the upper margin of the 【100†greater sciatic foramen】, divides into two large trunks, an anterior and a posterior.
L161: It is posterior to the 【101†ureter】,^{【102†[2]】} anterior to the 【80†internal iliac vein】,^{【102†[2]】} anterior to the 【103†lumbosacral trunk】, and anterior to the 【104†piriformis muscle】. Near its origin, it is medial to the 【105†external iliac vein】, which lies between it and the 【106†psoas major muscle】. It is above the 【107†obturator nerve】.
L162: ### Branches
L163: 
L164: [【108†edit】]
L165: 
L166: The arrangement of branches of the internal iliac artery is extremely variable.^{【109†[3]】} Typically, the artery divides into an anterior division and a posterior division, with the posterior division giving rise to the superior gluteal, iliolumbar, and lateral sacral arteries. The rest usually arise from the anterior division. Because it is variable, an artery may not be a direct branch, but instead might arise off a direct branch.
L167: In recent years the development of techniques like prostate artery embolisation and angiografy led to an increased understanding of the prostate vascularisation. Regarding the arterial supply M. de Assis et al. has suggested an anatomic classification for the origin of the inferior vesical artery.^{【110†[4]】}
L168: 
L169: The following are the branches of internal iliac artery:

L138: 【64†Anatomical terminology】
L139: The internal iliac vein (hypogastric vein) begins near the upper part of the 【65†greater sciatic foramen】, passes upward behind and slightly medial to the 【57†internal iliac artery】 and, at the 【66†brim of the pelvis】, joins with the 【67†external iliac vein】 to form the 【55†common iliac vein】.
L140: ## Structure
L141: 
L142: [【68†edit】]
L143: Several veins unite above the 【65†greater sciatic foramen】 to form the internal iliac vein. It does not have the predictable branches of the 【57†internal iliac artery】 but its tributaries drain the same regions.^{【69†[1]】} The internal iliac vein emerges from above the level of the greater sciatic notch It runs backwards, upwards and towards the midline to join the external iliac vein in forming the common iliac vein in front of the 【70†sacroiliac joint】.
L144: It usually lies lateral to the internal iliac artery.^{【71†[2]】} It is wide and 3 cm long.^{【72†[3]】}
L145: ### Tributaries
L146: 
L147: [【73†edit】]
L148: 
L149: Originating outside the pelvis, its tributaries are the gluteal, internal pudendal and obturator veins. Running from the anterior surface of the sacrum are the lateral sacral veins. Coming from the pelvic plexuses and appropriate to gender are the middle rectal, vesical, prostatic, uterine and vaginal veins.^{【69†[1]】}^{【72†[3]】}

L161: ### Variation
L162: 
L163: [【88†edit】]
L164: 
L165: On the left, the internal iliac vein lies lateral to the internal iliac artery 73% of the time.^{【89†[4]】} On the right, this is 93% of the time.^{【89†[4]】}
L166: 
L167: ## Function
L168: 
L169: [【90†edit】]
L170: 
L171: The internal iliac veins drain the pelvic organs, 【80†sacrum】, and 【91†coccyx】.^{【71†[2]】}
L172: ## Clinical significance
L173: 
L174: [【92†edit】]
L175: 
L176: If 【93†thrombosis】 disrupts blood flow in the external iliac systems, the internal iliac tributaries offer a major route of venous return from the femoral system. Damage to internal iliac vein tributaries during surgery can seriously compromise venous drainage and cause swelling of one or both legs.^{【69†[1]】}

L139: 【71†Anatomical terminology】
L140: The middle suprarenal artery (middle capsular artery) is a paired artery in the abdomen. It is a branch of the 【72†aorta】. It supplies the 【64†adrenal gland】.
L141: ## Structure
L142: 
L143: [【73†edit】]
L144: 
L145: ### Origin
L146: 
L147: [【74†edit】]
L148: 
L149: The middle suprarenal artery (usually) arises from lateral aspect of the 【61†abdominal aorta】. Its origin occurs at roughly the same level as that of the 【75†superior mesenteric artery】.^{【76†[1]】}^{: 1240 }
L150: ### Course
L151: 
L152: [【77†edit】]
L153: 
L154: The vessel passes laterally and slightly superior-ward, passing over the 【78†crura】 of the 【79†diaphragm】 to reach the surface of the ipsilateral 【80†suprarenal gland】, whereupon it forms anastomoses with the other suprarenal arteries.^{【76†[1]】}^{: 1240 }
L155: ### Relations
L156: 
L157: [【81†edit】]
L158: 
L159: The anatomical relations of the left and right middle superior artery differ. The right vessel crosses the 【82†inferior vena cava】 posteriorly near the 【83†right celiac ganglion】. The left vessel passes near the 【83†right celiac ganglion】, superior margin of the spleen, and 【84†splenic artery】.^{【76†[1]】}^{: 1240 }
L160: ### Variation
L161: 
L162: [【85†edit】]
L163: 
L164: There is usually a single middle suprarenal artery (on either side of the body), but in some individuals, there may be multiple, or the vessel may be absent.^{【76†[1]】}^{: 1240 }
L165: 
L166: The vessel may sometimes arise from the (ipsilateral) 【86†renal artery】, or (ipsilateral) 【87†inferior phrenic artery】.^{【76†[1]】}^{: 1240 }
L167: 
L168: ## Function
L169: 
L170: [【88†edit】]
L171: 
L172: The middle suprarenal artery supplies the 【64†adrenal gland】.^{【89†[2]】}
L173: ## Clinical significance
L174: 
L175: [【90†edit】]
L176: 
L177: The middle suprarenal artery may be assessed using 【91†Doppler ultrasound】.^{【92†[3]】}
L178: 
L179: ## History
L180: 
L181: [【93†edit】]
L182: 
L183: The middle suprarenal artery may also be known as the middle adrenal artery^{【92†[3]】} or the middle capsular artery.

L163: 【92†Anatomical terminology】
L164: The renal veins in the 【93†renal circulation】, are large-calibre^{【94†[1]】} 【95†veins】 that drain blood filtered by the 【80†kidneys】 into the 【83†inferior vena cava】. There is one renal vein draining each kidney. Each renal vein is formed by the convergence of the 【81†interlobar veins】 of one kidney.^{【96†[2]】}
L165: 
L166: Because the inferior vena cava is on the right half of the body, the left renal vein is longer than the right one.
L167: ## Structure
L168: 
L169: [【97†edit】]
L170: 
L171: One renal vein drains each 【80†kidney】. A renal vein is situated anterior to its corresponding accompanying 【66†renal artery】. The renal veins empty into the 【83†inferior vena cava】, entering it at nearly a 90° angle.^{【94†[1]】}
L172: 
L173: Due to the right-ward displacement of the inferior vena cava from the midline, the left renal vein is some 3 times longer than the right one (~7.5 cm and ~2.5 cm, respectively).^{【94†[1]】}
L174: The renal vein divides into 4 divisions upon entering the kidney:
L175: 
L176:   * the anterior branch which receives blood from the anterior portion of the kidney and,
L177:   * the posterior branch which receives blood from the posterior portion.
L178: ### Tributaries
L179: 
L180: [【98†edit】]
L181: 
L182: Because the tributaries of the 【83†inferior vena cava】 are not bilaterally symmetrical, the left renal vein often receives the ipsilateral 【99†inferior phrenic vein】, 【100†suprarenal vein】, 【101†gonadal vein】 (【102†left testicular vein】 in males, 【103†left ovarian vein】 in females), and 2nd 【104†lumbar vein】.^{【105†[3]】} This is in contrast to the right side of the body, where these veins drain directly into the IVC.^{【105†[3]】}
L183: ### Relations
L184: 
L185: [【106†edit】]
L186: 
L187: The anatomical relations of the two renal veins are bilaterally asymmetrical.
L188: 
L189: Left renal vein
L190: The left renal vein is situated posterior to the 【107†splenic vein】, and the 【108†body of the pancreas】.^{【94†[1]】} It passes through the angle formed by the abdominal aorta (situated posteriorly), and 【109†superior mesenteric artery】 (situated anteriorly) (increased acuteness of this angle may lead to the left renal vein being "pinched" between the two arteries, with the resulting compression impairing blood flow through the vein, a condition known as 【110†nutcracker syndrome】).
L191: Occasionally, the left renal vein (or accessory left renal vein) passes posterior to the aorta.^{【94†[1]】}
L192: Right renal vein
L193: 
L194: The right renal vein is situated posterior to the descending part of the 【111†duodenum】.^{【94†[1]】}
L195: ### Variation
L196: 
L197: [【112†edit】]
L198: 
L199: There is typically a single renal vein draining each kidney, but accessory renal veins are commonly encountered; renal vasculature anomalies are more frequent with 【113†ectopic kidneys】, and almost always present with 【114†horseshoe kidney】).^{【115†[4]】}
L200: In some individuals, the left renal vein passes posterior to the abdominal aorta instead of in anterior to it;^{【94†[1]】} this is termed a retro-aortic left renal vein (also known as "The Vein of Schnitker"). If there is both a vein passing in front of and one behind the aorta this is called a circumaortic renal vein.
L201: In the case of a left sided IVC and the right renal vein passes behind the abdominal aorta, this is termed a retroaortic right renal vein, which is also known as “The Reverse Vein of Schnitker”.
L202: ## Clinical significance
L203: 
L204: [【116†edit】]
L205: 
L206: Diseases associated with the renal vein include 【117†renal vein thrombosis】 (RVT) and 【110†nutcracker syndrome】 (renal vein entrapment syndrome).

L151: Subclavian artery

L153: Schematic of the proximal aorta and its branches. The left subclavian artery is the fifth branch of the aorta and the third branch from the arch of the aorta. The right subclavian artery arises from the 【96†brachiocephalic artery】 and its branches. (Right subclavian is at upper left, and left subclavian is at upper right.)

L171: 【113†Anatomical terminology】
L172: In 【114†human anatomy】, the subclavian arteries are paired major 【115†arteries】 of the upper 【116†thorax】, below the 【117†clavicle】. They receive blood from the 【97†aortic arch】. The left subclavian artery supplies blood to the left arm and the right subclavian artery supplies blood to the right arm, with some branches supplying the head and thorax.
L173: On the left side of the body, the subclavian comes directly off the 【97†aortic arch】, while on the right side it arises from the relatively short 【96†brachiocephalic artery】 when it bifurcates into the subclavian and the right 【118†common carotid artery】.
L174: The usual branches of the subclavian on both sides of the body are the 【98†vertebral artery】, the 【99†internal thoracic artery】, the 【100†thyrocervical trunk】, the 【101†costocervical trunk】 and the 【102†dorsal scapular artery】, which may branch off the transverse cervical artery, which is a branch of the thyrocervical trunk. The subclavian becomes the 【119†axillary artery】 at the lateral border of the first 【120†rib】.
L175: ## Structure
L176: 
L177: [【121†edit】]
L178: 
L179: From its origin, the subclavian artery travels laterally, passing between anterior and middle 【122†scalene muscles】, with the 【123†anterior scalene】 on its anterior side and the 【124†middle scalene】 on its posterior. This is in contrast to the 【104†subclavian vein】, which travels anterior to the anterior scalene. As the subclavian artery crosses the lateral border of the 【125†first rib】, it becomes the 【119†axillary artery】.^{【126†[1]】}^{【127†[2]】}
L180: On the right side, the subclavian artery arises from the brachiocephalic (innominate) artery behind the right sternoclavicular articulation; on the left side it springs from the arch of the aorta.^{【126†[1]】}^{【128†[3]】} The two vessels, therefore, in the first part of their course, differ in length, direction, and relation with neighboring structures.^{【129†[4]】} The left subclavian artery is around 9 【130†cm】 long in 【131†adults】, while the right subclavian artery is around 6 cm long.^{【129†[4]】} Both have a width of 9-12 【132†mm】.^{【129†[4]】}
L181: ### Parts
L182: 
L183: [【133†edit】]
L184: 
L185: In order to facilitate the description, each subclavian artery is divided into three parts:
L186:   * The first part, also known as the prescalene part,^{【129†[4]】} extends from the origin of the vessel to the medial border of the scalenus anterior muscle.^{【126†[1]】}
L187:   * The second part, also known as the scalene part,^{【129†[4]】} lies behind the anterior scalene muscle.^{【126†[1]】}
L188:   * The third part, also known as the postscalene part,^{【129†[4]】} extends from the lateral margin of the muscle to the outer border of the first rib, where it becomes the axillary artery.^{【126†[1]】}^{【127†[2]】}
L189: The first portions of the two vessels require separate descriptions; the second and third parts of the two arteries are practically alike.

L146: 【75†Anatomical terminology】
L147: The left and right brachiocephalic veins (previously called innominate veins) are major 【76†veins】 in the 【77†upper chest】, formed by the union of the 【78†ipsilateral】 【59†internal jugular vein】 and 【60†subclavian vein】 (the so-called 【79†venous angle】)^{【80†[1]】} behind the 【81†sternoclavicular joint】.^{【82†[2]】} The left brachiocephalic vein is more than twice the length of the right brachiocephalic vein.^{【83†[3]】}
L148: These veins merge to form the 【64†superior vena cava】, a 【84†great vessel】, posterior to the junction of the first 【85†costal cartilage】 with the 【86†manubrium of the sternum】.^{【83†[3]】}
L149: 
L150: The brachiocephalic veins are the major veins returning blood to the 【64†superior vena cava】.^{【83†[3]】}
L151: ## Left and right veins
L152: 
L153: [【87†edit】]
L154: 
L155: Veins of the thoracic and abdominal regions
L156: ### Left brachiocephalic vein
L157: 
L158: [【88†edit】]
L159: 
L160: The left brachiocephalic vein is about 6 cm long, more than twice the length of the right brachiocephalic vein,^{【83†[3]】} and is formed by the confluence of the left 【60†subclavian】 and left 【59†internal jugular veins】. In addition, the left vein receives drainage from the following tributaries:
L161:   * The left 【62†vertebral vein】, 【89†internal thoracic vein】, 【63†inferior thyroid veins】, 【61†superior intercostal veins】, the 【90†thymic veins】 and the 【91†pericardial veins】^{【83†[3]】}^{【92†[4]】}
L162: ### Right brachiocephalic vein
L163: 
L164: [【93†edit】]
L165: 
L166: The right brachiocephalic vein is about 2.5cm long.^{【83†[3]】} The right vein is formed by the confluence of the right subclavian vein and the right internal jugular vein. It receives the following tributaries:
L167: 
L168:   * The right vertebral vein, the internal thoracic vein, and the thyroid veins, and occasionally from the first right posterior intercostal veins.^{【83†[3]】}
L169: ## Embryological origin
L170: 
L171: [【94†edit】]
L172: 
L173: The left brachiocephalic vein develops from the anastomosis between the left and right anterior cardinal veins when the caudal segment of the left anterior cardinal vein degenerates.

L180: 【114†Anatomical terminology】
L181: In anatomy, the left and right common carotid arteries (carotids) (English: 【115†/kəˈrɒtɪd/】^{【116†[1]】}^{【117†[2]】}) are 【118†arteries】 that supply the head and neck with 【119†oxygenated blood】; they divide in the neck to form the 【103†external】 and 【102†internal carotid arteries】.^{【120†[3]】}^{【121†[4]】}
L182: ## Structure
L183: 
L184: [【122†edit】]
L185: 
L186: The common carotid arteries are present on the left and right sides of the body. These arteries originate from different arteries but follow symmetrical courses. The right common carotid originates in the neck from the 【97†brachiocephalic trunk】; the left from the 【100†aortic arch】 in the thorax. These split into the external and internal carotid arteries at the upper border of the 【123†thyroid cartilage】, at around the level of the 【124†fourth cervical vertebra】.
L187: The left common carotid artery can be thought of as having two parts: a thoracic (chest) part and a cervical (neck) part.^{【125†[5]】} The right common carotid originates in or close to the neck and contains only a small thoracic portion. There are studies in the bioengineering literature that have looked into characterizing the geometric structure of the common carotid artery from both qualitative and mathematical (quantitative) standpoints.^{【121†[4]】}
L188: The average diameters of the common carotids in adult males and females are 6.5 mm and 6.1 mm respectively.^{【126†[6]】}
L189: ### In the chest
L190: 
L191: [【127†edit】]
L192: 
L193: Only the left common carotid artery has a substantial presence in the thorax. It originates directly from the aortic arch, and travels upward through the superior 【128†mediastinum】 to the level of the left 【129†sternoclavicular joint】.
L194: During the thoracic part of its course, the left common carotid artery is related to the following structures: In front, it is separated from the 【130†manubrium】 of the 【131†sternum】 by the 【132†sternohyoid】 and 【133†sternothyroid】 muscles, the anterior portions of the left 【134†pleura】 and 【135†lung】, the left 【136†brachiocephalic vein】, and the remains of the 【137†thymus】; behind, it lies on the 【138†trachea】, 【139†esophagus】, left 【140†recurrent laryngeal nerve】, and 【141†thoracic duct】.

L120: External iliac vein
L121: ---
L122: Veins of the 【54†abdomen】 and 【55†lower limb】 - 【56†inferior vena cava】, 【57†common iliac vein】, external iliac vein, 【58†internal iliac vein】, 【59†femoral vein】 and their tributaries. The 【60†aorta】 and its bifurcation (unlabeled) appear in red.
L123: The relations of the femoral and abdominal inguinal rings, seen from within the abdomen. Right side. (External iliac vein is large vein at center.)

L136: 【69†Anatomical terminology】
L137: The external iliac veins are large 【70†veins】 that connect the 【59†femoral veins】 to the 【57†common iliac veins】. Their origin is at the inferior margin of the 【71†inguinal ligaments】 and they terminate when they join the 【58†internal iliac veins】 (to form the 【57†common iliac veins】).
L138: 
L139: Both external iliac veins are accompanied along their course by 【62†external iliac arteries】.
L140: ## Structure
L141: 
L142: [【72†edit】]
L143: 
L144: A continuation of the 【59†femoral vein】,^{【73†[1]】} the external iliac vein starts at the level of the inguinal ligament.^{【74†[2]】} It runs beside its corresponding artery and along the brim of the 【75†lesser pelvis】 to unite with the internal iliac vein anterior to the 【76†sacroiliac joint】 where it forms the common iliac vein.^{【77†[3]】}
L145: The left external iliac vein remains medial to the artery along its whole path. The right external iliac vein is medial to the artery, but as it ascends, it runs posterior to it.^{【74†[2]】}
L146: The external iliac vein is crossed by the 【78†ureter】 and internal iliac artery which both extend towards the middle. In males it is crossed by the 【79†vas deferens】 and in females the 【80†round ligament】 and 【81†ovarian vessels】 cross it. 【82†Psoas major】 lies to its side, except where the artery intervenes.^{【83†[4]】}
L147: 
L148: The external iliac vein may have one valve, but often has no valves.^{【74†[2]】}
L149: In addition to pubic veins, the main tributaries of the external iliac veins are the 【84†inferior epigastric veins】 and the 【85†deep circumflex iliac vein】.^{【83†[4]】}
L150: ## Clinical significance and history
L151: 
L152: [【86†edit】]
L153: In 1967, Cockett noted anatomical variations which predisposed to compression of the external iliac vein, amongst other veins. Although less common than 【87†May-Thurner syndrome】, it is being progressively documented due to modern imaging methods. Compression of the left external iliac vein by the right common iliac artery or left hypogastric artery can occur as it crosses over the vein into the pelvis. The right external iliac vein can similarly be compressed.
L154: Such compressions may contribute to 【88†deep vein thrombosis】.^{【89†[5]】}
L155: Failure to develop or 【90†agenesis】 of the external iliac vein has been described in association with 【91†Klippel–Trenaunay syndrome】.^{【83†[4]】}

L148: 【82†Anatomical terminology】
L149: The internal jugular vein is a paired 【83†jugular vein】 that collects blood from the 【84†brain】 and the superficial parts of the 【85†face】 and 【86†neck】. This vein runs in the 【87†carotid sheath】 with the 【75†common carotid artery】 and 【88†vagus nerve】.
L150: 
L151: It begins in the posterior compartment of the 【89†jugular foramen】, at the base of the 【90†skull】. It is somewhat dilated at its origin, which is called the superior bulb.
L152: This vein also has a common trunk into which drains the anterior branch of the 【91†retromandibular vein】, the 【92†facial vein】, and the 【93†lingual vein】.
L153: It runs down the side of the neck in a vertical direction, being at one end lateral to the 【74†internal carotid artery】, and then lateral to the 【75†common carotid artery】, and at the root of the neck, it unites with the 【94†subclavian vein】 to form the 【72†brachiocephalic vein】 (innominate vein); a little above its termination is a second dilation, the inferior bulb.
L154: Above, it lies upon the 【95†rectus capitis lateralis】, behind the 【74†internal carotid artery】 and the nerves passing through the 【89†jugular foramen】. Lower down, the vein and artery lie upon the same plane, the 【96†glossopharyngeal】 and 【97†hypoglossal】 nerves passing forward between them.
L155: The 【88†vagus nerve】 descends between and behind the 【98†vein】 and the 【73†artery】 in the same sheath (the 【87†carotid sheath】), and the 【99†accessory】 runs obliquely backward, 【100†superficial†en.wiktionary.org】 or deep to the vein.
L156: At the root of the neck, the right internal jugular vein is a little distance from the 【75†common carotid artery】, and crosses the first part of the 【101†subclavian artery】, while the left internal jugular vein usually overlaps the common carotid artery.
L157: 
L158: The left vein is generally smaller than the right, and each contains a pair of 【102†valves】, which exist about 2.5 cm above the termination of the vessel.
L159: ## Variation
L160: 
L161: [【103†edit】]
L162: 
L163: In 9–12% of the Western population, the size, shape or course of the internal jugular vein is abnormal.^{【104†[1]】} Variants identified including veins markedly smaller, or not functionally present.^{【105†[2]】} The mean diameter is 10 mm, but may range between 5 and 35 mm.^{【106†[3]】}

L156: 【98†Anatomical terminology】
L157: The subclavian vein is a paired large 【99†vein】, one on either side of the body, that is responsible for draining 【100†blood】 from the upper extremities, allowing this blood to return to the 【101†heart】. The left subclavian vein plays a key role in the absorption of 【102†lipids】, by allowing products that have been carried by 【103†lymph】 in the 【104†thoracic duct】 to enter the bloodstream. The 【105†diameter】 of the subclavian veins is approximately 1–2 cm, depending on the individual.
L158: ## Structure
L159: 
L160: [【106†edit】]
L161: 
L162: Each subclavian vein is a continuation of the 【85†axillary vein】 and runs from the outer border of the 【107†first rib】 to the 【108†medial】 border of 【109†anterior scalene muscle】.^{【110†[1]】} From here it joins with the 【111†internal jugular vein】 to form the 【87†brachiocephalic vein】 (also known as "innominate vein"). The angle of union is termed the 【112†venous angle】.
L163: The subclavian vein follows the 【89†subclavian artery】 and is separated from the subclavian artery by the insertion of 【113†anterior scalene】.^{【110†[1]】} Thus, the subclavian vein lies anterior to the anterior scalene while the subclavian artery lies posterior to the anterior scalene (and anterior to the middle scalene).^{【114†[2]】}
L164: ## Function
L165: 
L166: [【115†edit】]
L167: The 【104†thoracic duct】 drains into the left subclavian vein,^{【116†[3]】} near its junction with the left 【111†internal jugular vein】. It carries 【103†lymph】 (water and solutes) from the 【117†lymphatic system】, as well as 【118†chylomicrons】 or 【119†chyle】, formed in the 【120†intestines】 from dietary fat and 【121†lipids】, allowing these to enter the bloodstream; the products of 【122†fats】 and 【102†lipids】 can then be carried by the bloodstream to the 【123†hepatic portal vein】, and then finally to the liver.
L168: Consequently, the left subclavian vein plays a key role in the absorption of these fats and lipids.
L169: The 【124†right lymphatic duct】 drains its lymph into the junction of the right internal jugular vein, and the right subclavian vein.

L119: 【46†FMA】  | 【47†12858†bioportal.bioontology.org】
L120: 【48†Anatomical terminology】
L121: 
L122: The ascending lumbar vein is a vein that runs up through the lumbar region on the side of the 【49†vertebral column】.
L123: ## Structure
L124: 
L125: [【50†edit】]
L126: 
L127: The ascending lumbar vein is a paired structure (i.e. one each for the right and left sides of the body). It starts at the 【51†common iliac veins】. It runs superiorly, intersecting with the 【52†lumbar veins】 as it crosses them. It passes behind the 【53†psoas major muscle】, but in front of the 【54†lumbar vertebrae】.^{【55†[1]】}
L128: 
L129: When the ascending lumbar vein crosses the 【56†subcostal vein】, it becomes one of the following:
L130:   * the 【42†azygos vein】 (in the case of the right ascending lumbar vein).^{【55†[1]】}^{【57†[2]】}
L131:   * the 【44†hemiazygos vein】 (in the case of the left ascending lumbar vein).^{【55†[1]】}
L132: 
L133: The first and second lumbar veins ends in the ascending lumbar vein (the third and fourth lumbar veins open into the posterior aspect of the inferior vena cava)
L134: ## Clinical significance
L135: 
L136: [【58†edit】]
L137: 
L138: Contrast medium may be injected into the ascending lumbar vein via the 【59†femoral vein】 in order to visualise the 【60†spinal canal】.^{【61†[3]】}
L139: 
L140: The ascending lumbar vein may be punctured during 【62†catheterisation】.^{【63†[4]】} This can cause 【64†bleeding】 into the 【65†dural space】.^{【63†[4]】}

L121: Dorsal artery of the penis
L122: ---
L123: Transverse section of the 【52†penis】. (Dorsal artery visible at top.)
L124: The deeper branches of the 【53†internal pudendal artery】. (Dorsal artery of penis labeled at upper right.)
L125: Details
L126: ---
L127: Source  | 【53†Internal pudendal artery】
L128: 【54†Vein】  | 【55†Deep dorsal vein of the penis】
L129: Supplies  | 【52†Penis】
L130: Identifiers
L131: ---
L132: 【56†Latin】  | arteria dorsalis penis
L133: 【57†TA98】  | 【58†A12.2.15.044M†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L134: 【57†TA2】  | 【59†4354†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】
L135: 【60†FMA】  | 【61†19795†bioportal.bioontology.org】
L136: 【62†Anatomical terminology】
L137: The dorsal artery of the penis is a bilaterally paired terminal branch of the 【53†internal pudendal artery】 which passes upon the dorsum of the penis to the base of the 【63†glans penis】, where it unites with its contralateral partner and supply the glans and foreskin.
L138: 
L139: The dorsal artery of the penis provides blood supply to the skin and fascia of the penis (including the foreskin), and the erectile tissues of the penis (especially the glans penis).
L140: The dorsal artery of the penis may be damaged in traumatic amputation of the penis and repairing the dorsal artery surgically prevents skin loss, but it is not essential for sexual and urinary function. Its 【64†hemodynamics】 and 【65†blood pressure】 can be assessed to test for sexual impairment.
L141: ## Origin
L142: 
L143: [【66†edit】]
L144: 
L145: The dorsal artery of the penis is a terminal branch of the 【53†internal pudendal artery】, arising at the inferior border of the symphysis pubis.^{【67†[1]】}
L146: ## Course and relations
L147: 
L148: [【68†edit】]
L149: 
L150: It passes between the 【69†crus penis】^{【70†[2]】} and the 【71†pubic symphysis】 of the pelvis to reach the dorsal surface of the corpus cavernosus penis.^{【70†[2]】}
L151: 
L152: As it pierces the 【72†perineal membrane】, it (depending upon the source) passes between the two layers of the 【73†suspensory ligament of the penis】, or pierces the lateral lamina of the 【74†suspensory ligament of penis】.^{【67†[1]】}
L153: It passes distally along the dorsum of the penis to reach the base of the 【63†glans penis】.^{【67†[1]】} In the dorsum of the penis, it passes in between the 【55†deep dorsal vein of penis】 (situated medially to the artery) and 【75†dorsal nerve of penis】 (situated laterally to the artery);^{【70†[2]】} it is situated superficial to the 【76†deep dorsal vein of penis】.^{【67†[1]】}
L154: ## Fate
L155: 
L156: [【77†edit】]
L157: 
L158: At the base of the glans penis, it anastomoses with its contralateral counterpart to form an arterial circle which supplies 【78†glans penis】 and 【79†foreskin】 (prepuce).^{【67†[1]】}
L159: 
L160: ## Anastomoses
L161: 
L162: [【80†edit】]
L163: 
L164: It sends branches through the fibrous sheath of the corpus cavernosum penis to 【81†anastomose】 with the 【82†deep artery of the penis】. It anastomoses with the 【83†artery of bulb of penis】.^{【84†[3]】} It terminates by anastomosing with its contralateral partner.^{【67†[1]】}
L165: ## Branches and territory
L166: 
L167: [【85†edit】]
L168: 
L169: The dorsal artery of the penis supplies the skin and fascia of the penis^{【67†[1]】}^{【84†[3]】} including the 【79†foreskin】 (prepuce),^{【67†[1]】}^{【84†[3]】} the 【86†corpus cavernosum penis】,^{【67†[1]】} and the (especially^{【70†[2]】}) the 【78†glans penis】.^{【67†[1]】}^{【84†[3]】}^{【70†[2]】}
L170: Its superficial collateral branches are distributed to the 【87†integuments】 of the penis.^{【67†[1]】} It gives deep/perforating collateral branches to the 【86†corpus cavernosum penis】^{【67†[1]】} (despite this, its contribution to erectile function is inconsistent). Through retrograde flow it helps supply the 【88†skin】 of the 【52†distal shaft】. It also gives branches to the circumflex arteries that supply the 【89†corpus spongiosum】.

L121: The iliolumbar vein is the 【47†vena comitans】 of the 【39†iliolumbar artery】.

L123: 
L124: A single vein is found more commonly than a double vein.^{【50†[2]】}
L125: 
L126: It drains vertebral segments four and five.^{【51†[3]】}
L127: 
L128: It is closely related to the 【52†ascending lumbar vein】.^{【51†[3]】}

L128: Details
L129: ---
L130: Source  | 【57†External iliac artery】
L131: Branches  | 【58†Cremasteric artery】, pubic branch of inferior epigastric artery, 【59†artery of round ligament of uterus】 ♀

L135: 【62†Latin】  | arteria epigastrica inferior
L136: 【63†TA98】  | 【64†A12.2.16.003†ifaa.unifr.ch】
