L139: 【68†Anatomical terminology】
L140: In 【69†human anatomy】, the inferior epigastric artery is an 【70†artery】 that arises from the 【57†external iliac artery】.^{【71†[1]】}^{: 225 } It is accompanied by the 【61†inferior epigastric vein】; inferiorly, these two inferior epigastric vessels together travel within the 【72†lateral umbilical fold】 (which represents the lateral border of 【73†Hesselbach's triangle】, the area through which 【74†direct inguinal hernias】 protrude.^{【75†[2]】}) The inferior epigastric artery then traverses the 【76†arcuate line of rectus sheath】 to enter the 【77†rectus sheath】,^{【71†[1]】}^{: 234 } then 【78†anastomoses】 with the 【79†superior epigastric artery】 within the 【77†rectus sheath】.^{【71†[1]】}^{: 225 }
L141: ## Structure
L142: 
L143: [【80†edit】]
L144: 
L145: ### Origin
L146: 
L147: [【81†edit】]
L148: 
L149: The inferior epigastric artery arises from the 【57†external iliac artery】, immediately superior to the 【82†inguinal ligament】.^{【83†[3]】}
L150: ### Course and relations
L151: 
L152: [【84†edit】]
L153: 
L154: It curves forward in the subperitoneal tissue, and then ascends obliquely along the medial margin of the abdominal inguinal ring; continuing its course upward, it pierces the 【85†transversalis fascia】, and, passing in front of the 【86†linea semicircularis】, ascends between the 【87†rectus abdominis muscle】 and the posterior lamella of its sheath.
L155: It finally divides into numerous branches, which anastomose, above the 【88†umbilicus】, with the superior epigastric branch of the 【89†internal thoracic artery】 and with the 【90†lower intercostal arteries】.
L156: 
L157: As the inferior epigastric artery passes obliquely upward from its origin it lies along the lower and medial margins of the abdominal inguinal ring, and behind the commencement of the 【91†spermatic cord】.
L158: The 【92†vas deferens】, as it leaves the 【91†spermatic cord】 in the male, and the round ligament of the 【93†uterus】 in the female, winds around the lateral and posterior aspects of the artery.
L159: ### Anastomoses
L160: 
L161: [【94†edit】]
L162: 
L163: It 【95†anastomoses】 with the 【79†superior epigastric artery】.^{【83†[3]】}
L164: 
L165: ## Clinical significance
L166: 
L167: [【96†edit】]
L168: 
L169: ### Hernia
L170: 
L171: [【97†edit】]
L172: 
L173: The inferior epigastric artery may lie close to an 【98†inguinal hernia】, so acts as a useful 【68†landmark】.^{【99†[4]】}
L174: ### Surgery
L175: 
L176: [【100†edit】]
L177: 
L178: The inferior epigastric artery may be damaged during 【101†laparoscopic surgery】.^{【99†[4]】} It may also be damaged when manually finding the 【102†peritoneum】 beneath the 【103†rectus abdominis muscle】.^{【99†[4]】}

L123: 【50†Anatomical terminology】
L124: The inferior gluteal veins are 【51†venae comitantes】 of the 【43†inferior gluteal artery】. They commence in the superior/proximal posterior 【52†thigh】. They enter the pelvis through the lower part of the 【53†greater sciatic foramen】. They converge to form a single vessel before emptying into the distal portion of the 【41†internal iliac vein】.^{【54†[1]】}
L125: ## Anatomy
L126: 
L127: [【55†edit】]
L128: 
L129: ### Anastomoses
L130: 
L131: [【56†edit】]
L132: 
L133: At their origin, the inferior gluteal veins form anastomoses with the 【57†medial femoral circumflex vein】 and the 【58†first perforating veins】. They provide a means of 【59†collateral circulation】 between the 【60†femoral vein】, and 【41†lnternal iliac vein】.^{【54†[1]】}

L141: 【73†Anatomical terminology】
L142: The inferior phrenic artery is a 【74†bilaterally paired】 artery of the abdominal cavity which represents the main source of arterial supply to the diaphragm. Each artery usually arises either from the coeliac trunk or the abdominal aorta, however, their origin is highly variable and the different sites of origin are different for the left artery and right artery. The 【63†superior suprarenal artery】 is a branch of the inferior phrenic artery.
L143: ## Structure
L144: 
L145: [【75†edit】]
L146: ### Origin
L147: 
L148: [【76†edit】]
L149: 
L150: The inferior phrenic arteries vary considerably in their site of origin.^{【77†[1]】} typically arise from either the 【78†coeliac trunk】 or (the anterior aspect of^{【77†[1]】}) 【57†abdominal part of aorta】 (just superior to the coeliac trunk^{【77†[1]】}); the two arteries arise either separately or as a common trunk.^{【79†[2]】} The inferior phrenic arteries usually arise at the level corresponding to between 【80†T12】 and 【81†L2】 【82†vertebrae】.^{【83†[3]】}
L151: The right inferior phrenic artery may less often arise from the 【84†right renal artery】, 【85†left gastric artery】, 【86†hepatic artery proper】.^{【79†[2]】}
L152: 
L153: The left inferior phrenic artery may less often arise from either 【87†renal artery】, 【85†left gastric artery】, or 【86†hepatic artery proper】.^{【79†[2]】}
L154: ### Course and relations
L155: 
L156: [【88†edit】]
L157: 
L158: The artery courses beneath the posterior portion of the 【89†parietal peritoneum】.^{【90†[4]】} Each artery passes superoanteriorly and laterally to reach^{【79†[2]】}^{【90†[4]】} and cross the 【91†crura of diaphragm】,^{【90†[4]】} passing close to the medial border of the ipsilateral suprarenal gland.^{【79†[2]】}
L159: ### Termination
L160: 
L161: [【92†edit】]
L162: 
L163: Each artery splits into a medial branch and a lateral branch near the posterior border of the 【93†central tendon of diaphragm】.^{【79†[2]】} Alternatively, it may terminate by trifurcating into an anterior, a middle, and a posterior branch.^{【90†[4]】}
L164: 
L165: Left inferior phrenic artery
L166: The left phrenic passes posterior the 【94†esophagus】,^{【79†[2]】} then anterior-ward upon the left side of the 【95†esophageal hiatus】,^{【77†[1]】} past the left side of the 【96†oesophageal hiatus】.^{【79†[2]】}
L167: 
L168: Right inferior phrenic artery
L169: 
L170: The right phrenic passes posterior to the 【97†inferior vena cava】. It passes past the right side of the 【98†caval opening】.^{【79†[2]】}
L171: ### Branches
L172: 
L173: [【99†edit】]
L174:   * The medial branch curves anterior-ward, and anastomoses with its fellow of the opposite side, and with the 【100†musculophrenic】 and 【101†pericardiacophrenic】 arteries.^{【77†[1]】}
L175:   * The lateral branch passes toward the side of the thorax, and anastomoses with the 【102†lower intercostal】 arteries, and with the 【100†musculophrenic】. The lateral branch of the right phrenic gives off a few vessels to the 【97†inferior vena cava】; and the left one, some branches to the 【94†esophagus】.^{【77†[1]】}

L113: Internal pudendal veins
L114: ---
L115: The 【45†veins】 of the right half of the male 【46†pelvis】 (internal pudendal visible at bottom)
L116: The superficial branches of the internal pudendal veins.
L117: Details
L118: ---
L119: Drains to  | 【47†Internal iliac vein】
L120: 【48†Artery】  | 【49†Internal pudendal artery】
L121: Identifiers
L122: ---
L123: 【50†Latin】  | vena pudenda interna
L124: 【51†TA98】  | 【52†A12.3.10.019†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L125: 【51†TA2】  | 【53†5032†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】
L126: 【54†FMA】  | 【55†18917†bioportal.bioontology.org】
L127: 【56†Anatomical terminology】
L128: The internal pudendal veins (internal pudic veins) are a set of 【57†veins】 in the 【46†pelvis】. They are the 【58†venae comitantes】 of the 【49†internal pudendal artery】. Internal pudendal veins are enclosed by 【59†pudendal canal】, with internal pudendal artery and 【60†pudendal nerve】.
L129: They begin in the 【61†deep veins】 of the 【62†scrotum】 and of the 【63†penis】, issuing from the 【64†bulb of the vestibule】 and the 【65†bulb of the penis】, respectively. They accompany the internal pudendal artery, and unite to form a single vessel, which ends in the 【47†internal iliac vein】.
L130: 
L131: They receive the veins from the 【66†urethral bulb】, the 【67†perineal】 and 【68†inferior hemorrhoidal veins】.
L132: The 【69†deep dorsal vein of the penis】 communicates with the internal pudendal veins, but ends mainly in the 【70†pudendal plexus】.

L111: The veins of the right half of the male pelvis. (Obturator labeled at center left.)
L112: Details
L113: ---
L114: Drains to  | 【40†Internal iliac vein】

L122: 【49†Anatomical terminology】
L123: The obturator vein begins in the upper portion of the adductor region of the 【50†thigh】 and enters the 【51†pelvis】 through the upper part of the 【52†obturator foramen】, in the 【53†obturator canal】.
L124: 
L125: It runs backward and upward on the lateral wall of the pelvis below the 【42†obturator artery】, and then passes between the 【54†ureter】 and the 【55†internal iliac artery】, to end in the 【40†internal iliac vein】.
L126: It has an anterior and posterior branch (similar to obturator artery), which are larger than its corresponding arteries.
L127: 
L128: The obturator veins have valves, especially in the extrapelvic section.

L124: 【52†Anatomical terminology】
L125: The superficial epigastric artery (not to be confused with the 【53†superior epigastric artery】) arises from the front of the femoral artery about 1 cm below the 【54†inguinal ligament】, and, passing through the 【55†femoral sheath】 and the 【56†fascia cribrosa】, turns upward in front of the inguinal ligament, and ascends between the two layers of the 【57†superficial fascia】 of the 【58†abdominal wall】 nearly as far as the 【59†umbilicus】.
L126: It distributes branches to the 【60†superficial subinguinal lymph glands】, the 【57†superficial fascia】, and the 【61†integument】; it 【62†anastomoses】 with branches of the 【63†inferior epigastric】, and with its fellow of the opposite side.

L127: 【56†Anatomical terminology】
L128: In 【57†human anatomy】, the superior epigastric veins are two or more^{【58†[1]】} 【59†venae comitantes】 which accompany either 【45†superior epigastric artery】 before emptying into the 【48†internal thoracic vein】. They participate in the drainage of the superior surface of the 【60†diaphragm】.
L129: ## Structure
L130: 
L131: [【61†edit】]
L132: ### Course
L133: 
L134: [【62†edit】]
L135: 
L136: The superior epigastric vein originates from the 【63†internal thoracic vein】.^{【64†[2]】}^{: 193 } The superior epigastric veins first run between the sternal margin and the costal margin of the diaphragm, then enter the 【65†rectus sheath】.^{【66†[3]】} They run inferiorly, coursing superficially to the fibrous layer forming the posterior leaflet of the rectus sheath, and deep to the 【67†rectus abdominis muscle】.^{【68†[4]】}^{: 211 }
L137: The superior epigastric veins are 【59†venae comitantes】 of the 【45†superior epigastric artery】,^{【69†[5]】} and mirror its course.^{【66†[3]】}
L138: ### Distribution
L139: 
L140: [【70†edit】]
L141: 
L142: The superior epigastric veins participate in the drainage of the superior surface of the diaphragm.^{【66†[3]】}
L143: 
L144: ### Fate
L145: 
L146: [【71†edit】]
L147: 
L148: The superior epigastric veins drain into the 【48†internal thoracic vein】.^{【72†[6]】}^{【66†[3]】}

L122: The superior gluteal veins (gluteal veins) are 【49†venæ comitantes】 of the 【41†superior gluteal artery】. L136: 【71†Anatomical terminology】
L137: The testicular artery (the male 【72†gonadal artery】, also called the internal spermatic arteries in older texts) is a branch of the 【61†abdominal aorta】 that supplies blood to the 【73†testicle】. It is a paired 【74†artery】, with one for each of the testicles.
L138: 
L139: It is the male equivalent of the 【75†ovarian artery】. Because the testis is found in a different location than that of its female equivalent, it has a different course than the ovarian artery.
L140: They are two slender vessels of considerable length, and arise from the front of the 【76†aorta】 a little below the 【77†renal arteries】.
L141: 
L142: Each passes obliquely downward and lateralward behind the 【78†peritoneum】, resting on the 【79†psoas major】, the right lying in front of the 【80†inferior vena cava】 and behind the 【81†middle colic】 and 【82†ileocolic】 arteries and the terminal part of the 【83†ileum】, the left behind the 【84†left colic】 and 【85†sigmoid arteries】 and the 【86†iliac colon】.
L143: Each crosses obliquely over the ureter and the lower part of the external iliac artery to reach the 【87†abdominal inguinal ring】, through which it passes, and accompanies the other constituents of the 【88†spermatic cord】 along the 【89†inguinal canal】 to the 【90†scrotum】, where it becomes 【91†tortuous】, and divides into several branches.
L144: Two or three of these accompany the 【92†ductus deferens】, and supply the 【93†epididymis】, anastomosing with the artery of the ductus deferens; others pierce the back part of the 【94†tunica albuginea】, and supply the substance of the testicle.
L145: 
L146: The internal spermatic artery supplies one or two small branches to the 【95†ureter】, and in the inguinal canal gives one or two twigs to the 【96†cremaster】.
L147: ## Clinical significance
L148: 
L149: [【97†edit】]
L150: 
L151: The testicular artery may be damaged during 【98†inguinal hernia repair】, possibly resulting in insidious testicular atrophy - but not necessarily accompanied by testicular necrosis due to collateral arterial supply via the inferior epigastric, prostatic, vesical, and scrotal arteries.^{【99†[1]】}

L131: 【58†Anatomical terminology】
L132: The testicular vein (or spermatic vein), the male 【59†gonadal vein】, carries deoxygenated blood from its corresponding 【60†testis】 to the 【51†inferior vena cava】 or one of its tributaries. It is the male equivalent of the 【61†ovarian vein】, and is the venous counterpart of the 【54†testicular artery】.
L133: ## Structure
L134: 
L135: [【62†edit】]
L136: 
L137: It is a paired vein, with one supplying each testis:
L138: 
L139:   * the right testicular vein generally joins the 【51†inferior vena cava】;
L140:   * the left testicular vein, unlike the right one, joins the 【63†left renal vein】 instead of the inferior vena cava.
L141: The veins emerge from the back of the 【60†testis】, and receive tributaries from the 【64†epididymis】.^{【65†[1]】} They unite and form a convoluted plexus, called the 【50†pampiniform plexus】, which constitutes the greater mass of the 【66†spermatic cord】; the vessels composing this plexus are very numerous, and ascend along the cord, in front of the 【67†ductus deferens】.
L142: Below the 【68†subcutaneous inguinal ring】, they unite to form three or four veins, which pass along the 【69†inguinal canal】, and, entering the abdomen through the 【70†abdominal inguinal ring】, coalesce to form two veins, which ascend on the 【71†Psoas major】, behind the 【72†peritoneum】, lying one on either side of the 【73†internal spermatic artery】.
L143: These unite to form a single vein, which opens, on the right side, into the 【51†inferior vena cava】 (at an acute angle), on the left side into the 【52†left renal vein】 (at a right angle).
L144: 
L145: The left spermatic vein passes behind the 【74†iliac colon】 and is thus exposed to pressure from the contents of that part of the bowel.
L146: ### Variation
L147: 
L148: [【75†edit】]
L149: 
L150: The testicular veins usually have 【76†valves】.^{【65†[1]】} However, in 【77†post-mortem examinations】 it was found that up to 40% of left testicular veins lack valves, and up to 23% of right testicular veins lack valves.^{【65†[1]】}
L151: 
L152: ## Clinical significance
L153: 
L154: [【78†edit】]
L155: ### Varicocele
L156: 
L157: [【79†edit】]
L158: Valveless testicular veins are a major contributing factor to 【80†varicocele】.^{【65†[1]】} Since the left testicular vein goes all the way up to the left 【63†renal vein】 before it empties, this results in a higher tendency for the left testicle to develop 【80†varicocele】 because of the gravity working on the column of blood in this vein, compared to the right internal spermatic vein.
L159: One reason for this susceptibility is that the left internal testicular vein drains into the 【52†left renal vein】 with a right-angle entry unlike it is with the right testicular vein, which can create increased pressure and possibly disrupt the normal valve function, leading to poor venous return and eventually varicocele development.^{【81†[2]】}
L160: The testicular vein may be 【82†ligated】 in part (a branch) or completely to treat varicocele.^{【83†[3]】} This is typically very safe.^{【83†[3]】} There is debate about whether the 【54†testicular artery】 should also be ligated simultaneously.^{【83†[3]】} Affected testicular veins can also be removed completely to further reduce recurrence rates.
L161: ### Compression
L162: 
L163: [【84†edit】]
L164: 
L165: The left renal vein passes between the 【85†abdominal aorta】 and the 【86†superior mesenteric artery】 en route to the inferior vena cava, and is often compressed by an enlarged superior mesenteric artery—this is called the "【87†Nutcracker effect】".^{【88†[4]】}

L133: 【61†Anatomical terminology】
L134: In 【62†human anatomy】, the marginal artery of the colon, also known as the marginal artery of Drummond, the artery of Drummond, and simply as the marginal artery, is an 【63†artery】 that connects the 【52†inferior mesenteric artery】 with the 【53†superior mesenteric artery】. It is sometimes absent, as an 【64†anatomical variant】.
L135: ## Structure
L136: 
L137: [【65†edit】]
L138: 
L139: The marginal artery runs in the 【66†mesentery】 close to the 【54†large intestine】 as part of the vascular arcade that connects the 【53†superior mesenteric artery】 and the 【52†inferior mesenteric artery】.^{【67†[1]】} It provides an effective anastomosis between these two arteries for the large intestine.^{【67†[1]】}
L140: 
L141: ### Variation
L142: 
L143: [【68†edit】]
L144: 
L145: The marginal artery is almost always present, and its absence should be considered a variant.
L146: 
L147: ## Clinical significance
L148: 
L149: [【69†edit】]
L150: ### Removal of the inferior mesenteric artery
L151: 
L152: [【70†edit】]
L153: 
L154: Along with branches of the 【71†internal iliac arteries】, it is usually sufficiently large to supply the oxygenated 【72†blood】 to the 【54†large intestine】.^{【67†[1]】} This means that the 【52†inferior mesenteric artery】 does not have to be re-implanted (re-attached) into the repaired 【51†abdominal aorta】 in 【73†abdominal aortic aneurysm repair】.^{【67†[1]】}
L155: ### Arc of Riolan
L156: 
L157: [【74†edit】]
L158: The Arc of Riolan (Riolan's arcade, Arch of Riolan, Haller's anastomosis), also known as the meandering mesenteric artery, is another vascular arcade present in the colonic mesentery that connect the proximal 【75†middle colic artery】 with a branch of the 【76†left colic artery】. This artery is found low in the mesentery, near the root.
L159: In the setting of chronic 【77†ischemic colitis】, both the marginal artery and the meandering mesenteric artery may be enlarged significantly, and may provide significant blood flow to the ischemic colonic segment.
L160: ## History
L161: 
L162: [【78†edit】]
L163: 
L164: The marginal artery is also known as the marginal artery of Drummond.^{【67†[1]】} It was named after Sir 【79†David Drummond】 (1852-1932), an Anglo-Irish physician.^{【80†[2]】}

L121: The median sacral vein (or middle sacral veins) is a 【49†vein】 of the 【50†abdomen】. L137: 【65†Anatomical terminology】
L138: The middle colic artery is an 【66†artery】 of the 【67†abdomen】; a branch of the 【55†superior mesenteric artery】 distributed to parts of the 【68†ascending】 and 【58†transverse colon】. It usually divides into two terminal branches - a left one and a right one - which go on to form anastomoses with the 【69†left colic artery】, and 【70†right colic artery】 (respectively), thus participating in the formation of the 【71†marginal artery of the colon】.
L139: Parts of the artery may be removed in different types of 【72†hemicolectomy】.
L140: ## Structure
L141: 
L142: [【73†edit】]
L143: 
L144: The middle colic artery supplies the superior/distal part of the 【68†ascending colon】 and right/proximal two-thirds of the 【58†transverse colon】.^{【74†[1]】}
L145: 
L146: ### Origin
L147: 
L148: [【75†edit】]
L149: 
L150: The middle colic artery is a branch of the 【55†superior mesenteric artery】, branching off from its right aspect. Its origin is situated just inferior the neck of the 【76†pancreas】. It may share a common origin with the 【70†right colic artery】.^{【77†[2]】}
L151: ### Course
L152: 
L153: [【78†edit】]
L154: 
L155: The middle colic artery passes anterosuperiorly between the layers of the 【79†transverse mesocolon】 just right of the midline before dividing into left and right terminal branches.^{【77†[2]】}
L156: ### Branches and anastomoses
L157: 
L158: [【80†edit】]
L159: 
L160: The anastomotic arches formed by the left and right branches of the middle colic artery are about two fingers' breadth from the 【58†transverse colon】, to which they distribute branches.^{【81†[3]】}
L161: 
L162: The sequence of anastomoses of the branches of the middle colic artery constitutes part of the 【71†marginal artery of the colon】.^{【74†[1]】}
L163: #### Left branch
L164: 
L165: [【82†edit】]
L166: 
L167: The left branch anastomoses with a branch of the 【69†left colic artery】 (in turn a branch of the 【83†inferior mesenteric artery】^{【84†[4]】}) near the 【85†left colic flexure】,^{【77†[2]】} forming the arc of Riolan.^{【84†[4]】}
L168: 
L169: #### Right branch
L170: 
L171: [【86†edit】]
L172: 
L173: The right branch anastomoses with the ascending branch of the 【70†right colic artery】.^{【77†[2]】}
L174: ### Variation
L175: 
L176: [【87†edit】]
L177: 
L178: Alternate origin
L179: 
L180: The middle colic artery may rarely instead arise from the 【88†abdominal aorta】, 【83†inferior mesenteric artery】, 【89†dorsal pancreatic artery】, 【90†hepatic artery proper】, 【69†left colic artery】,^{【77†[2]】} or 【91†splenic artery】.
L181: 
L182: Accessory middle colic artery
L183: An accessory middle colic artery in encountered in 10-20% of individuals.^{【84†[4]】} The accessory artery may arise from the superior mesenteric artery proximal to the middle colic artery proper, and from the 【88†abdominal aorta】, 【83†inferior mesenteric artery】, 【89†dorsal pancreatic artery】, 【90†hepatic artery proper】, or 【69†left colic artery】.^{【77†[2]】} An accessory middle colic directly originated from the superior mesenteric artery occurred in 18% of individuals.^{【92†[5]】}
L184: Number of terminal branches
L185: 
L186: The middle colic artery may occasionally divide into 3 or more branches (in which case the two lateral-most branches are the ones forming the anastomoses).^{【77†[2]】}
L187: ## Clinical significance
L188: 
L189: [【93†edit】]
L190: 
L191: In a right 【72†hemicolectomy】 to remove the 【94†caecum】 and the 【68†ascending colon】, the right branch of the middle colic artery is ligated and removed.^{【74†[1]】}^{【95†[6]】} In a transverse hemicolectomy, the entire middle colic artery may need to be ligated and removed.^{【95†[6]】}

L121: 【49†Anatomical terminology】
L122: The middle colic vein drains the 【39†transverse colon】. It is a tributary of the 【40†superior mesenteric vein】, and follows the path of its corresponding artery, the 【42†middle colic artery】.^{【50†[1]】} As the superior mesenteric vein drains to the 【51†hepatic portal vein】, the middle colic vein is considered part of the 【52†hepatic portal system】. This vein also carries nutrients absorbed from the large intestine to the liver.
L123: This vein is sometimes used as the point of catheter insertion for treatment of acute portal and mesenteric vein thrombosis.^{【53†[2]】}

L138: 【68†Anatomical terminology】
L139: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery (the IPDA) is a branch of the 【59†superior mesenteric artery】. It supplies the head of the 【69†pancreas】, and the ascending and inferior parts of the 【70†duodenum】. Rarely, it may have an 【71†aneurysm】.
L140: ## Structure
L141: 
L142: [【72†edit】]
L143: 
L144: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery is a branch of the 【59†superior mesenteric artery】. This occurs opposite the upper border of the inferior part of the 【70†duodenum】. As soon as it branches, it divides into 【73†anterior and posterior】 branches. These run between the head of the 【69†pancreas】 and the lesser curvature of the duodenum. They then join (【74†anastomose】) with the anterior and posterior branches of the 【75†superior pancreaticoduodenal artery】.^{【76†[1]】}
L145: ### Variation
L146: 
L147: [【77†edit】]
L148: 
L149: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery may branch from the first intestinal branch of the 【59†superior mesenteric artery】 rather than directly from it.
L150: 
L151: ## Function
L152: 
L153: [【78†edit】]
L154: 
L155: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery distributes branches to the head of the 【69†pancreas】 and to the ascending and inferior parts of the 【70†duodenum】.^{【76†[1]】}^{【79†[2]】}
L156: 
L157: ## Clinical significance
L158: 
L159: [【80†edit】]
L160: ### Aneurysm
L161: 
L162: [【81†edit】]
L163: Very rarely, the inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery may have an 【71†aneurysm】.^{【82†[3]】} It may be caused by certain 【83†medical interventions】, 【84†major trauma】, 【85†pancreatitis】, 【86†cholecystitis】, and 【87†vasculitis】 and other 【88†infections】.^{【82†[3]】} A ruptured aneurysm causes 【89†abdominal pain】, and 【90†haemorrhage】 leads to 【91†hypotension】.^{【82†[3]】} It may be treated with 【92†open abdominal surgery】.^{【82†[3]】} It may also be treated with 【93†endovascular surgery】, such as a coil.^{【82†[3]】}^{【94†[4]】} These aneurysms represent around 2% of aneurysms in visceral arteries of the 【95†abdomen】.^{【94†[4]】}^{【96†[5]】} 【97†Pseudoaneurysm】 may also occur.^{【98†[6]】}
L164: ## History
L165: 
L166: [【99†edit】]
L167: 
L168: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery may be more simply known by the 【100†acronym】 IPDA.^{【82†[3]】}

L131: 【58†Anatomical terminology】
L132: The superior pancreaticoduodenal artery is an 【59†artery】 that supplies 【60†blood】 to the 【53†duodenum】 and 【54†pancreas】.
L133: ## Structure
L134: 
L135: [【61†edit】]
L136: 
L137: It is a branch of the 【50†gastroduodenal artery】, which most commonly arises from the 【62†common hepatic artery】 of the 【63†celiac trunk】, although there are numerous variations of the origin of the gastroduodenal artery.^{【64†[1]】}
L138: The pancreaticoduodenal artery divides into two branches as it descends, an 【65†anterior and posterior】 branch. These branches then travel around the head of the pancreas and duodenum, eventually joining with the anterior and posterior branches of the 【66†inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery】.
L139: The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery is a branch of the 【67†superior mesenteric artery】.^{【68†[2]】} These arteries, together with the 【69†pancreatic branches】 of the 【70†splenic artery】, form connections or 【71†anastomoses】 with one another, allowing blood to perfuse the pancreas and duodenum through multiple channels.
L140: ### Distribution
L141: 
L142: [【72†edit】]
L143: 
L144: The artery supplies the anterior and posterior sides of the duodenum and head of 【54†pancreas】, with the anterior branch supply the anterior surface and similarly for the posterior.
L145: 
L146: The artery supplies the part of the duodenum proximal to the level of the 【73†major duodenal papilla】 of the descending part of the duodenum.^{【74†[3]】}

L128: 【53†TA98】  | 【54†A12.3.07.012†ifaa.unifr.ch】

L132: 【59†Anatomical terminology】
L133: The lumbar veins are four pairs of 【60†veins】 running along the inside of the posterior 【61†abdominal wall】, and drain venous blood from parts of the abdominal wall. Each lumbar vein accompanies a single 【62†lumbar artery】. The lower two pairs of lumbar veins all drain directly into the 【49†inferior vena cava】, whereas the fate of the upper two pairs is more variable.
L134: 
L135: Lumbar veins are the lumbar equivalent of the 【63†posterior intercostal veins】 of the 【64†thorax】.
L136: ## Structure
L137: 
L138: [【65†edit】]
L139: 
L140: A lumbar vein 【66†accompanies】 each of the four 【51†lumbar arteries】 on each side of the body.^{【67†[1]】}
L141: 
L142: ### Distribution and tributaries
L143: 
L144: [【68†edit】]
L145: 
L146: Collectively, the lumbar veins drain blood from the territories supplied by the corresponding lumbar arteries (the posterior, lateral, and anterior abdominal wall).^{【67†[1]】}
L147: 
L148: The lumbar veins drain the 【69†anterior spinal veins】.^{【70†[2]】}
L149: ### Fate
L150: 
L151: [【71†edit】]
L152: 
L153: The 3rd and 4th lumbar veins drain into the 【49†inferior vena cava】.^{【72†[3]】}
L154: The fate of the two superior lumbar veins is far more variable, and may drain into either the inferior vena cava, ascending lumbar vein, azygos vein, or (on the left side) the 【73†left renal vein】; the 1st lumbar vein often passes inferiorly to join the 2nd lumbar vein, but may less commonly drain into the ascending lumbar vein, or the azygos vein; the 2nd lumbar vein may drain directly into the inferior vena cava (at or near the level of the renal veins), but may less commonly join the 3rd lumbar vein or drain into the 【74†ascending lumbar vein】.^{【67†[1]】}
L155: ### Anastomoses
L156: 
L157: [【75†edit】]
L158: 
L159: The 1st and 2nd lumbar veins are often interconnected with each other. An 【74†ascending lumbar vein】 additionally interconnects ipsilateral lumbar veins on each side.^{【67†[1]】}
L160: The lumbar veins communicate with the 【76†external】 and 【77†internal vertebral venous plexuses】, and form anastomoses with tributaries of the 【78†azygos vein】 and 【79†hemiazygos vein】 (posteriorly), and (anteriorly) with branches of the 【80†epigastric veins】, 【81†circumflex iliac veins】, and 【82†lateral thoracic veins】. The anastomoses formed by the lumbar veins provide a means of collateral veinous return.^{【67†[1]】}
L161: ### Relations
L162: 
L163: [【83†edit】]
L164: 
L165: The lumbar veins are 【66†venae comitantes】 of the 【51†lumbar arteries】.^{【67†[1]】} Each lumbar vein lies superior to its adjacent/corresponding lumbar artery (the same arrangement as in the intercostal neurovascular bundles).
L166: 
L167: All of the lumbar veins lie posterior to the ipsilateral 【84†sympathetic trunk】.
L168: 
L169: Bilateral asymmetry
L170: On the left side, the 3rd and 4th lumbar veins pass posterior to the 【85†abdominal aorta】 to reach the inferior vena cava (which is displaced to the right of the midline); thus, the left 3rd and 4th lumbar veins are longer than the corresponding contralateral two lumbar veins.^{【67†[1]】}
L171: ### Variation
L172: 
L173: [【86†edit】]
L174: 
L175: There is variation in which lumbar veins drain to the 【49†inferior vena cava】 and which drain to the 【74†ascending lumbar vein】, the 【78†azygos vein】, and the 【79†hemiazygos vein】.^{【72†[3]】} A left lumbar vein may drain into the 【73†left renal vein】.^{【72†[3]】}
L176: ## Clinical significance
L177: 
L178: [【87†edit】]
L179: 
L180: During 【88†central venous catheterisation】 of the 【49†inferior vena cava】, the 【88†catheter】 may enter a lumbar vein.^{【89†[4]】} The catheter may need to be repositioned.^{【89†[4]】}

L119: The veins of the right half of the male 【55†pelvis】 (lumbar arteries not labeled, but third lumbar vein labeled at center top)
L120: Details
L121: ---
L122: Source  | 【56†Abdominal aorta】
L123: 【57†Vein】  | 【58†Lumbar veins】
L124: Supplies  | 【59†Quadratus lumborum】

L126: ---
L127: 【60†Latin】  | arteriae lumbares
L128: 【61†TA98】  | 【62†A12.2.12.004†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L129: 【61†TA2】  | 【63†4208†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】

L131: 【66†Anatomical terminology】
L132: The lumbar arteries are 【67†arteries】 located in the lower back or 【68†lumbar region】. The lumbar arteries are in parallel with the 【69†intercostals】.
L133: 
L134: They are usually four in number on either side, and arise from the back of the 【70†aorta】, opposite the bodies of the upper four 【71†lumbar vertebrae】.
L135: 
L136: A fifth pair, small in size, is occasionally present: they arise from the 【72†middle sacral artery】.
L137: They run lateralward and backward on the bodies of the 【71†lumbar vertebrae】, behind the 【73†sympathetic trunk】, to the intervals between the adjacent 【74†transverse processes】, and are then continued into the abdominal wall.
L138: 
L139: The arteries of the right side pass behind the 【75†inferior vena cava】, and the upper two on each side run behind the corresponding 【76†crus】 of the 【77†diaphragm】.
L140: The arteries of both sides pass beneath the 【78†tendinous arches】 which give origin to the 【79†psoas major】, and are then continued behind this muscle and the 【80†lumbar plexus】.
L141: 
L142: They now cross the 【81†quadratus lumborum】, the upper three arteries running behind, the last usually in front of the muscle.
L143: 
L144: At the lateral border of the quadratus lumborum they pierce the posterior aponeurosis of the 【82†transversus abdominis】 and are carried forward between this muscle and the 【83†obliquus internus】.
L145: They anastomose with the 【84†lower intercostal】, the 【85†subcostal】, the 【86†iliolumbar】, the 【87†deep iliac circumflex】, and the 【88†inferior epigastric】 arteries.

L131: The sigmoid arteries are 2–5 branches of the 【52†inferior mesenteric artery】 that are distributed to the distal 【61†descending colon】 and the 【50†sigmoid colon】.^{【62†[1]】}
L132: ## Anatomy
L133: 
L134: [【63†edit】]
L135: 
L136: ### Course and relations
L137: 
L138: [【64†edit】]
L139: 
L140: The sigmoid arteries course obliquely inferior-ward and to the left, passing posterior to the 【65†peritoneum】 and in anterior to the 【66†psoas major】, 【67†ureter】,^{【68†[2]】} and 【69†Gonadal artery】.^{【62†[1]】}
L141: 
L142: ### Anastomoses
L143: 
L144: [【70†edit】]
L145: 
L146: The sigmoid arteries anastomose with the 【71†left colic】 superiorly, and with the 【72†superior rectal artery】 inferiorly.^{【68†[2]】}

L118: Splenic vein
L119: ---
L120: The splenic vein, here called the "lienal vein", travels from the spleen, above the pancreas, and ends in the 【51†portal vein】.
L121: Details
L122: ---
L123: 【52†System】  | 【53†Hepatic portal system】
L124: Drains from  | 【54†Trabecular vein】 of 【55†spleen】
L125: Source  | 【56†Short gastric veins】, 【57†left gastroepiploic vein】, 【58†pancreatic veins】, 【59†inferior mesenteric vein】
L126: Drains to  | 【60†Hepatic portal vein】
L127: 【61†Artery】  | 【62†Splenic artery】
L128: Identifiers
L129: ---
L130: 【63†Latin】  | vena lienalis
L131: 【64†MeSH】  | 【65†D013162†meshb.nlm.nih.gov】
L132: 【66†TA98】  | 【67†A12.3.12.028†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L133: 【66†TA2】  | 【68†5123†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】
L134: 【69†FMA】  | 【70†14331†bioportal.bioontology.org】
L135: 【71†Anatomical terminology】
L136: In 【72†human anatomy】, the splenic vein (formerly the lienal vein) is a 【73†blood vessel】 that drains blood from the 【55†spleen】, the 【74†stomach fundus】 and part of the 【75†pancreas】. It is part of the 【53†hepatic portal system】.
L137: ## Structure
L138: 
L139: [【76†edit】]
L140: The splenic vein is formed from small venules that leave the spleen. It travels above the 【75†pancreas】, alongside the 【62†splenic artery】. It collects branches from the 【77†stomach】 and 【75†pancreas】, and most notably from the 【78†large intestine】 (also drained by the 【79†superior mesenteric vein】) via the 【59†inferior mesenteric vein】, which drains in the splenic vein shortly before the origin of the 【60†hepatic portal vein】.
L141: The splenic vein ends in the portal vein, formed when the splenic vein joins the superior mesenteric vein.
L142: ## Clinical significance
L143: 
L144: [【80†edit】]
L145: The splenic vein can be affected by 【81†thrombosis】, presenting some of the characteristics of 【82†portal vein thrombosis】 and 【83†portal hypertension】 but localized to part of the territory drained by the splenic vein. These include 【84†varices in the stomach wall】 due to hypertension in the 【56†short gastric veins】 and abdominal pain. This results in gastric varices, in which the treatment of choice would be splenectomy.
L146: The most common cause for splenic vein thrombosis is both chronic and acute 【85†pancreatitis】.^{【86†[1]】}^{【87†[2]】}

L141: Superior vena cava
L142: ---
L143: The superior vena cava drains from the left and right brachiocephalic veins into the 【75†right atrium】

L145: ---

L153: 【81†MeSH】  | 【82†D014683†meshb.nlm.nih.gov】

L157: 【88†Anatomical terminology】
L158: This article uses 【88†anatomical terminology】.
L159: The superior vena cava (SVC) is the 【89†superior】 of the two 【90†venae cavae】, the great 【91†venous】 trunks that return deoxygenated 【92†blood】 from the 【93†systemic circulation】 to the 【94†right atrium】 of the 【95†heart】. It is a large-diameter (24 mm) short length (~7 cm) vein that receives venous return from the upper half of the body, above the 【96†diaphragm】. Venous return from the lower half, below the diaphragm, flows through the 【97†inferior vena cava】.
L160: The SVC is located in the anterior right superior 【98†mediastinum】.^{【99†[1]】} It is the typical site of central venous access via a 【100†central venous catheter】 or a 【101†peripherally inserted central catheter】. Mentions of "the cava" without further specification usually refer to the SVC.
L161: ## Structure
L162: 
L163: [【102†edit】]
L164: The superior vena cava is formed by the left and right 【103†brachiocephalic veins】, which receive blood from the 【104†upper limbs】, 【105†head】 and 【106†neck】, behind the lower border of the first right 【107†costal cartilage】. It passes vertically downwards behind the first intercostal space and receives the 【79†azygos vein】 just before it pierces the fibrous 【108†pericardium】 opposite the right second costal cartilage and its lower part is intrapericardial.
L165: It then terminates in the upper and posterior part of the sinus venarum of the right atrium, at the upper right front portion of the heart. It is also known as the cranial vena cava in other animals. No 【109†valve】 divides the superior vena cava from the right atrium.
L166: The superior vena cava is made up of three layers, starting with the innermost endothelial 【110†tunica intima】.
L167: The middle layer is the 【111†tunica media】, composed of smooth muscle tissue, and the outermost and thickest layer is the 【112†tunica adventitia】, composed of collagen and elastic connective tissue that allow for flexibility.^{【113†[2]】}^{【114†[3]】} The tunica adventitia contains three zones, with the middle zone consisting of few smooth muscle fibers; this differs from the longitudinal bundles of smooth muscle found in the same zone of the inferior vena cava.^{【115†[4]】}
L168: ### Anatomical variation
L169: 
L170: [【116†edit】]
L171: 
L172: The most common 【117†anatomical variation】 is a 【118†persistent left superior vena cava】. In persons with a persistent left superior vena cava, the right superior vena cava may be normal, small or absent, with or without an anterior communicating vein. This variation is present in less than 0.5% of the general population, but in up to 10% in patients with 【119†congenital heart disease】.^{【120†[5]】}
L173: ## Clinical significance
L174: 
L175: [【121†edit】]
L176: 【122†Superior vena cava obstruction】 refers to a partial or complete obstruction of the superior vena cava, typically in the context of 【123†cancer】 such as a 【124†cancer of the lung】, 【125†metastatic cancer】, or 【126†lymphoma】. Obstruction can lead to enlarged veins in the head and neck, and may also cause breathlessness, cough, chest pain, and difficulty swallowing. 【127†Pemberton's sign】 may be positive.

L133: 【65†Anatomical terminology】
L134: In 【66†human anatomy】, the superior mesenteric vein (SMV) is a 【67†blood vessel】 that drains 【68†blood】 from the 【69†small intestine】 (【70†jejunum】 and 【71†ileum】). Behind the neck of the 【72†pancreas】, the superior mesenteric 【73†vein】 combines with the 【74†splenic vein】 to form the 【75†portal vein】 that carries blood to the 【76†liver】. The superior mesenteric vein lies to the right of the similarly named 【57†artery】, the 【58†superior mesenteric artery】, which originates from the 【77†abdominal aorta】.
L135: ## Structure
L136: 
L137: [【78†edit】]
L138: 
L139: Tributaries of the superior mesenteric vein drain the 【69†small intestine】, 【79†large intestine】, 【80†stomach】, 【72†pancreas】 and 【81†appendix】 and include:
L140: 
L141:   * 【82†Right gastro-omental vein】 (also known as the right gastro-epiploic vein)
L142:   * 【83†inferior pancreaticoduodenal veins】
L143:   * 【84†veins from jejunum】
L144:   * 【85†veins from ileum】
L145:   * 【86†middle colic vein】 – drains the 【87†transverse colon】
L146:   * 【88†right colic vein】 – drains the 【89†ascending colon】
L147:   * 【90†ileocolic vein】
L148: The superior mesenteric vein combines with the 【74†splenic vein】 to form the 【75†portal vein】.^{【91†[1]】}^{【92†[2]】}
L149: ## Clinical significance
L150: 
L151: [【93†edit】]
L152: 
L153: 【94†Thrombosis】 of the superior mesenteric vein is quite rare, but a significant cause of 【95†mesenteric ischemia】 and can be fatal. It is estimated that 10–15% of mesenteric 【96†ischemia】 is due to mesenteric 【94†thrombosis】.^{【97†[3]】}

L136: 【66†Anatomical terminology】
L137: The superior rectal artery (superior hemorrhoidal artery) is an artery that descends into the 【67†pelvis】 to supply blood to the 【54†rectum】.
L138: ## Structure
L139: 
L140: [【68†edit】]
L141: 
L142: The superior rectal artery is the continuation of the 【55†inferior mesenteric artery】. It descends into the 【67†pelvis】 between the layers of the 【69†mesentery】 of the 【53†sigmoid colon】, crossing the left 【70†common iliac artery】 and vein.
L143: 
L144: It divides, opposite the third 【71†sacral vertebra】 into two branches, which descend one on either side of the 【54†rectum】. About 10 or 12 cm from the 【57†anus】, these branches break up into several small branches.^{【72†[1]】}
L145: These pierce the muscular coat of the bowel and run downward, as straight vessels, placed at regular intervals from each other in the wall of the gut between its muscular and mucous coats, to the level of the 【73†internal anal sphincter】; here they form a series of loops around the lower end of the rectum, and communicate with the 【74†middle rectal artery】 (from the 【75†internal iliac artery】) and with the 【76†inferior rectal artery】 (from the 【77†internal pudendal artery】).
L146: ## Function
L147: 
L148: [【78†edit】]
L149: 
L150: The superior rectal artery supplies the 【54†rectum】 and the 【57†anus】.^{【72†[1]】}^{【79†[2]】}
L151: 
L152: ## Pathology
L153: 
L154: [【80†edit】]
L155: 
L156: The superior rectal artery may be enlarged in patients with 【81†hemorrhoids】.^{【82†[3]】} The superior rectal artery may be embolized to treat patients with symptomatic internal hemorrhoids in a procedure called 【83†hemorrhoidal artery embolization】.^{【84†[4]】}

L136: 【63†Anatomical terminology】
L137: The left coronary artery (LCA, also known as the left main coronary artery, or left main stem coronary artery) is a 【64†coronary artery】 that arises from the 【65†aorta】 above the 【66†left cusp】 of the 【67†aortic valve】, and supplies blood to the left side of the 【68†heart muscle】. The left coronary artery typically runs for 10–25 mm, then bifurcates into the 【55†left anterior descending artery】, and the 【69†left circumflex artery】.^{【70†[1]】}
L138: The part that is between the aorta and the bifurcation only is known as the left main artery (LM), while the term "LCA" might refer to just the left main, or to the left main and all its eventual branches.
L139: ## Structure
L140: 
L141: [【71†edit】]
L142: 
L143: ### Variation
L144: 
L145: [【72†edit】]
L146: 
L147: Sometimes, an additional artery arises at the bifurcation of the left main artery, forming a trifurcation; this extra artery is called the ramus or intermediate artery.^{【73†[2]】}
L148: 
L149: A "first septal branch" is sometimes described.^{【74†[3]】}

L125: Details
L126: ---
L127: Location  | 【57†Heart】
L128: Supplies  | 【58†Right atrium】, 【59†right ventricle】, 25-35% of 【60†left ventricle】
L129: Identifiers
L130: ---
L131: 【61†Latin】  | arteria coronaria dextra
L132: Acronym  | RCA
L133: 【62†TA98】  | 【63†A12.2.03.101†ifaa.unifr.ch】
L134: 【62†TA2】  | 【64†4131†ta2viewer.openanatomy.org】
L135: 【65†FMA】  | 【66†50039†bioportal.bioontology.org】
L136: 【67†Anatomical terminology】
L137: In the 【56†blood supply of the heart】, the right coronary artery (RCA) is an 【68†artery】 originating above the right cusp of the 【69†aortic valve】, at the 【70†right aortic sinus】 in the 【57†heart】.^{【71†[1]】}^{【72†[2]】} It travels down the right 【73†coronary sulcus】, towards the 【74†crux of the heart】.^{【71†[1]】}^{【75†[3]】} It gives off many branches, including the 【76†sinoatrial nodal artery】, 【77†right marginal artery】, 【78†posterior interventricular artery】, 【79†conus artery】,^{【80†[4]】} and 【81†atrioventricular nodal branch】.
L138: It contributes the right side of the heart, and parts of the 【82†interventricular septum】.^{【72†[2]】}^{【83†[5]】}
L139: ## Structure
L140: 
L141: [【84†edit】]
L142: 
L143: The right coronary artery originates above the 【70†right aortic sinus】 above the 【69†aortic valve】.^{【71†[1]】}^{【72†[2]】} It passes along the right 【73†coronary sulcus (right atrioventricular groove)】 towards the 【74†crux of the heart】.^{【71†[1]】}^{【75†[3]】}
L144: ### Segments
L145: 
L146: [【85†edit】]
L147: 
L148:   * Proximal: starting at RCA origin, spanning half the distance to the 【86†acute margin】^{【87†[6]】}^{【88†[7]】}
L149:   * Middle: from proximal segment to the acute margin^{【87†[6]】}^{【88†[7]】}
L150:   * Distal: from middle segment to origination point of the posterior interventricular artery, where the 【89†posterior interventricular sulcus】 meets the 【90†atrioventricular groove】 on the base of the heart.^{【87†[6]】}^{【88†[7]】}
L151: ### Variation
L152: 
L153: [【91†edit】]
L154: 
L155: In approximately 80% of patients (right dominant), the RCA gives off the 【92†posterior descending artery】 (PDA). In the other 20%, of cases (left dominant or codominant), the PDA arises from the 【93†left circumflex artery】 or is supplied by both the right coronary artery and the left circumflex.^{【94†[8]】} The PDA supplies the 【95†inferior wall】, 【96†ventricular septum】, and the posteromedial 【97†papillary muscle】.
L156: The RCA also supplies the 【98†SA nodal artery】 in 60% of people. The other 40% of the time, the SA nodal artery is supplied by the 【93†left circumflex artery】.
L157: 
L158: Although rare, several anomalous courses of the right coronary artery have been described including origin from the left aortic sinus.^{【99†[9]】}
L159: ### Distribution
L160: 
L161: [【100†edit】]
L162: 
L163: The right coronary artery supplies oxygenated blood to the 【101†right atrium】, the 【102†right ventricle】, and the posterior third and inferior end of the 【82†interventricular septum】.^{【72†[2]】}^{【83†[5]】} It may also supply 25% to 35% of the 【60†left ventricle】 (LV).^{【103†[10]】}
L164: There is significant 【104†overlap】 of supply of the 【105†coronary arteries】.^{【72†[2]】} The right coronary artery is dominant over the 【106†left coronary artery】 50% of the time, equal to it 20% of the time, and less significant than it 30% of the time.^{【72†[2]】}

L166: 【102†Anatomical terminology】
L167: The aortic arch, arch of the aorta, or transverse aortic arch (English: 【103†/eɪˈɔːrtɪk/】^{【104†[1]】}^{【105†[2]】}) is the part of the 【93†aorta】 between the 【83†ascending】 and 【85†descending aorta】. The arch travels backward, so that it ultimately runs to the left of the 【106†trachea】.
L168: ## Structure
L169: 
L170: [【107†edit】]
L171: The aorta begins at the level of the upper border of the second/third 【108†sternocostal articulation】 of the right side, behind the 【109†ventricular outflow tract】 and 【110†pulmonary trunk】. The right 【111†atrial appendage】 overlaps it.
L172: The first few centimeters of the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk lies in the same 【112†pericardial sheath】 and runs at first upward, arches over the 【110†pulmonary trunk】, 【113†right pulmonary artery】, and 【114†right main bronchus】 to lie behind the right second 【115†costal cartilage】. The right lung and sternum lies anterior to the aorta at this point.
L173: The aorta then passes posteriorly and to the left, anterior to the trachea, and arches over 【116†left main bronchus】 and 【117†left pulmonary artery】, and reaches to the left side of the T4 vertebral body.^{【118†[3]】}^{【119†[4]】} Apart from T4 vertebral body, other structures such as trachea, oesophagus, and 【120†thoracic duct】 (from front to back) also lies to the left of the aorta.^{【118†[3]】} Inferiorly, the arch of aorta is connected to 【121†ligamentum arteriosum】 while superiorly, it gives rise to three main branches.^{【118†[3]】} The arch of aorta continues as the 【85†descending aorta】 after T4 vertebral body.^{【122†[5]】}^{: 214 }^{【123†[6]】}

L135: 【70†Anatomical terminology】
L136: The thoracic aorta is a part of the 【54†aorta】 located in the 【71†thorax】. It is a continuation of the 【72†aortic arch】. It is located within the 【73†posterior mediastinal】 cavity, but frequently bulges into the left 【74†pleural cavity】. The descending thoracic aorta begins at the lower border of the fourth 【75†thoracic vertebra】 and ends in front of the lower border of the twelfth thoracic vertebra, at the 【76†aortic hiatus】 in the 【77†diaphragm】 where it becomes the 【59†abdominal aorta】.
L137: At its commencement, it is situated on the left of the vertebral column; it approaches the median line as it descends; and, at its termination, lies directly in front of the column.
L138: 
L139: The thoracic aorta has a curved shape that faces forward, and has small branches. It has a radius of approximately 1.16 cm.^{【78†[1]】}
L140: ## Structure
L141: 
L142: [【79†edit】]
L143: 
L144: Main article: 【54†Aorta】
L145: The thoracic aorta is part of the 【55†descending aorta】, which has different parts named according to their structure or location. The thoracic aorta is a continuation of the descending aorta and becomes the 【59†abdominal aorta】 when it passes through the 【80†diaphragm】. The initial part of the 【54†aorta】, the 【81†ascending aorta】, rises out of the left ventricle, from which it is separated by the 【82†aortic valve】.
L146: The two 【83†coronary arteries】 of the heart arise from the aortic root, just above the cusps of the 【82†aortic valve】. The aorta then arches back over the right 【84†pulmonary artery】. Three vessels come out of the 【72†aortic arch】: the 【85†brachiocephalic artery】, the left 【86†common carotid artery】, and the left 【87†subclavian artery】. These vessels supply blood to the 【88†head】, 【89†neck】, 【71†thorax】 and 【90†upper limbs】.
L147: Behind the descending thoracic aorta is the 【91†vertebral column】 and the 【92†hemiazygos vein】. To the right is the 【93†azygos veins】 and 【94†thoracic duct】, and to the left is the left 【95†pleura】 and lung. In front of the thoracic aorta lies the root of the left 【96†lung】, the 【97†pericardium】, the 【98†esophagus】, and the diaphragm.
L148: The 【98†esophagus】, which is covered by a nerve 【99†plexus】 lies to the right of the descending thoracic aorta. Lower, the esophagus passes in front of the aorta, and ultimately is situated on the left.
L149: ## Function
L150: 
L151: [【100†edit】]
L152: 
L153: The 【54†aorta】 is an 【101†artery】 that conveys oxygenated 【102†blood】 from the 【103†heart】 to other parts of the body. It is one of the largest arteries in the body.^{【104†[2]】} The aorta gives off several paired branches as it descends. In descending order, these include the

L156:   * 【105†Mediastinal arteries】
L157:   * 【57†Esophageal arteries】
L158:   * Pericardial arteries

L128: 【58†Anatomical terminology】
L129: In 【59†human anatomy】, the brachial veins are 【60†venae comitantes】 of the 【51†brachial artery】 in the 【61†arm】 proper. Because they are deep to muscle, they are considered 【62†deep veins】. Their course is that of the brachial artery (in reverse): they begin where 【47†radial veins】 and 【48†ulnar veins】 join (corresponding to the bifurcation of the brachial artery). They end at the inferior border of the 【63†teres major】 muscle.
L130: At this point, the brachial veins join the 【64†basilic vein】 to form the 【49†axillary vein】.
L131: The brachial veins also have small tributaries that drain the 【65†muscles】 of the upper arm, such as 【66†biceps brachii muscle】 and 【67†triceps brachii muscle】.

L163: 
L164: [【97†edit】]
L165: 
L166: There are four main pulmonary veins, two from each lung – an inferior and a superior main vein, emerging from each 【98†hilum】. The main pulmonary veins receive blood from three or four feeding veins in each lung, and drain into the 【80†left atrium】. The peripheral feeding veins do not follow the bronchial tree. They run between the pulmonary segments from which they drain the blood.^{【99†[1]】}
L167: At the root of the lung, the right superior pulmonary vein lies in front of and a little below the pulmonary artery; the inferior is situated at the lowest part of the lung hilum. Behind the pulmonary artery is the 【100†bronchus】.^{【101†[2]】} The right main pulmonary veins (contains oxygenated blood) pass behind the 【102†right atrium】 and 【103†superior vena cava】; the left in front of the descending 【104†thoracic aorta】.
L168: ### Variation
L169: 
L170: [【105†edit】]
L171: 
L172: Occasionally the three lobar veins on the right side remain separate, and not infrequently the two left lobar veins end by a common opening into the left atrium. Therefore, the number of pulmonary veins opening into the left atrium can vary between three and five in the healthy 【106†population】.
L173: 
L174: The two left lobar veins may be united as a single pulmonary vein in about 25% of people; the two right veins may be united in about 3%.^{【101†[2]】}
L175: ## Function
L176: 
L177: [【107†edit】]
L178: 
L179: Further information: 【96†Pulmonary circulation】
L180: 
L181: The pulmonary veins play an essential role in 【108†respiration】, by receiving blood that has been oxygenated in the 【109†alveoli】 and returning it to the left atrium.
L182: ## Clinical significance
L183: 
L184: [【110†edit】]
L185: 
L186: As part of the pulmonary circulation they carry oxygenated blood back to the heart, as opposed to the veins of the 【111†systemic circulation】 which carry deoxygenated blood. By definition, a 【92†vein】 is a blood vessel that carries blood to the heart, whether oxygenated or deoxygenated.

L129: 【57†Anatomical terminology】
L130: The superficial palmar arch is formed predominantly by the 【46†ulnar artery】, with a contribution from the 【47†superficial palmar branch of the radial artery】. However, in some individuals the contribution from the radial artery might be absent, and instead anastomoses with either the 【58†princeps pollicis artery】, the 【59†radialis indicis artery】, or the 【60†median artery】, the former two of which are branches from the radial artery.
L131: Alternative names for this arterial arch are: superficial volar arch,^{【61†[1]】} superficial ulnar arch, arcus palmaris superficialis,^{【62†[2]】} or arcus volaris superficialis.^{【63†[3]】}
L132: 
L133: The arch passes across the 【64†palm】 in a curve (Boeckel's line) with its convexity downward,
L134: With the 【65†thumb】 fully extended, the superficial palmar arch would lie approximately 1 cm from a line drawn between the first web space to the 【66†hook of hamate】 (Kaplan's cardinal line). The superficial palmar arch extends more 【67†distally】 than the 【68†deep palmar arch】. The connection between the deep and superficial palmar arterial arches is an example of 【69†anastomosis】, and can be tested for using 【70†Allen's test】.
L135: Three 【48†common palmar digital arteries】 arise from the arch, proceeding down on the second, third, and fourth 【71†lumbrical muscles】, respectively. They each receive a contribution from a 【72†palmar metacarpal artery】. Near the level of the 【73†metacarpophalangeal joints】, each common palmar digital artery divides into two 【74†proper palmar digital arteries】.
L136: 
L137: Four digital branches arise from this palmar arch that supplies the medial/ulnar 3 1/2 fingers.

L127: 【54†Anatomical terminology】
L128: The posterior tibial veins are 【55†veins】 of the 【56†leg】 in 【57†humans】. They drain the 【58†posterior compartment】 of the leg and the 【59†plantar】 surface of the 【60†foot】 to the 【45†popliteal vein】.
L129: ## Structure
L130: 
L131: [【61†edit】]
L132: 
L133: The posterior tibial veins receive blood from the medial and lateral plantar veins.^{【62†[1]】} They drain the 【58†posterior compartment】 of the leg and the 【59†plantar】 surface of the 【60†foot】 to the 【45†popliteal vein】, which it forms when it joins with the 【63†anterior tibial vein】.^{【62†[1]】}
L134: The posterior tibial vein is accompanied by an homonym 【46†artery】, the 【47†posterior tibial artery】, along its course.^{【64†[2]】} It lies posterior to the 【65†medial malleolus】 in the 【66†ankle】.^{【64†[2]】}
L135: 
L136: They receive the most important 【67†perforator veins】: the Cockett perforators, superior, medial and inferior.^{【68†[3]】}

L126: 【52†Anatomical terminology】
L127: The anterior tibial vein is a 【53†vein】 in the 【54†lower leg】.
L128: 
L129: In 【55†human anatomy】, there are two anterior tibial veins. They originate and receive blood from the 【56†dorsal venous arch】, on the back of the 【57†foot】 and empties into the 【43†popliteal vein】.
L130: 
L131: The anterior tibial veins drain the 【58†ankle joint】, 【59†knee joint】, 【60†tibiofibular joint】, and the 【61†anterior portion】 of the lower leg.^{【62†[1]】}
L132: The two anterior tibial veins ascend in the 【63†interosseous membrane】 between the 【64†tibia】 and 【65†fibula】 and unite with the 【66†posterior tibial veins】 to form the popliteal vein.
L133: 
L134: Like most 【67†deep veins】 in legs, anterior tibial veins are accompanied by the homonym 【44†artery】, the 【45†anterior tibial artery】, along its course.^{【62†[1]】}

L143: 【76†Anatomical terminology】
L144: In 【77†human anatomy】, the hepatic veins are the 【78†veins】 that drain venous 【79†blood】 from the 【80†liver】 into the 【65†inferior vena cava】 (as opposed to the 【81†hepatic portal vein】 which conveys blood from the gastrointestinal organs to the liver^{【82†[1]】}^{: 1212 }). There are usually three large upper hepatic veins draining from the left, middle, and right parts of the liver, as well as a number (6-20) of lower hepatic veins.^{【83†[2]】} All hepatic veins are valveless.^{【84†[3]】}
L145: ## Structure
L146: 
L147: [【85†edit】]
L148: 
L149: All the hepatic veins drain into the 【65†inferior vena cava】. The hepatic veins are divided into an upper and a lower group.^{【83†[2]】}
L150: ### Upper group
L151: 
L152: [【86†edit】]
L153: 
L154: The upper group consists of three hepatic veins^{【83†[2]】} - the right, middle, and left hepatic veins^{【82†[1]】}^{: 1212 } - draining the central veins from the right, middle, and left regions of the liver and are larger than the lower group of veins.^{【83†[2]】} The veins of the upper group drain into the suprahepatic part of the inferior vena cava (i.e. part superior to the liver).^{【82†[1]】}^{: 1212 }
L155: #### Right hepatic vein
L156: 
L157: [【87†edit】]
L158: The right hepatic vein is the longest and largest of all the hepatic veins. It drains the liver segments VI and VII in their entirety, and variably participates in the drainage of segments V and VIII; the extent of drainage of the latter two segments by the right hepatic veins as opposed to the middle hepatic vein and possible variant accessory veins determines the calibre of the right hepatic vein.
L159: It arises anteriorly near the inferior border of the liver, coursing along the right portal fissure to drain into the inferior vena cava near the superior margin of the caudate lobe. It usually reaches the inferior vena cava as a single vessel, but sometimes drains into it as two separate trunks.^{【82†[1]】}^{: 1212 }
L160: #### Middle hepatic vein
L161: 
L162: [【88†edit】]
L163: 
L164: The middle hepatic vein drains the central portion of the liver, draining segments IV, V, and VIII. The middle hepatic vein most often joins the left hepatic vein to form a short common trunk to drain jointly into the inferior vena cava; the middle hepatic vein drains into the inferior vena cava as a separate vessel in less than 10% of individuals.^{【82†[1]】}^{: 1212 }
L165: #### Left hepatic vein
L166: 
L167: [【89†edit】]
L168: 
L169: The left hepatic vein usually drains liver segments II and III, and occasionally also segment IV. The umbilical fissure vein is a major tributary of the left hepatic vein.^{【82†[1]】}^{: 1213 } The left hepatic vein most often forms a short common trunk with the middle hepatic vein before these jointly drain into the inferior vena cava.^{【82†[1]】}^{: 1212 }
L170: ### Lower group
L171: 
L172: [【90†edit】]
L173: 
L174: The lower group consists of 6-20 smaller hepatic veins which drain the 【91†right lobe】 and the 【92†caudate lobe】, are in contact with the hepatic tissue, and are valveless.^{【83†[2]】} All veins of the lower group drain into the retrohepatic part of the inferior vena cava (i.e. part posterior to the liver).^{【82†[1]】}^{: 1212 }
L175: The lower group consists of 1-5 veins draining the liver segment I, and may consist of (inconsistently present) accessory inferior hepatic vein, accessory middle right hepatic vein, and several smaller retrohepatic veins draining the right lobe of the liver.^{【82†[1]】}^{: 1213 }
L176: ## Clinical significance
L177: 
L178: [【93†edit】]
L179: 
L180: The hepatic veins (and their variant anatomy) are relevant in liver resection and transplantation, and in 【94†Budd–Chiari syndrome】.^{【82†[1]】}
L181: Budd–Chiari syndrome is a condition caused by blockage of the hepatic veins, such as by a 【95†blood clot】. It presents with a "classical triad" of abdominal pain, ascites, and liver enlargement. It occurs in 1 out of a million individuals. The syndrome can be fulminant, acute, chronic, or asymptomatic.
L182: The independent lower veins draining the liver segment I directly into the inferior vena cava are unaffected by obstruction of the large hepatic veins, leading to compensatory hypertrophy.^{【82†[1]】}^{: 1213 }
L183: The hepatic veins may be connected with the portal veins in a 【96†TIPS】 procedure.
